task.title: Indexed reference-type event parameters decoded wrong (upstream #53)
task.body: lib/abi/event.ex:146-172 decoded indexed reference-type event params incorrectly. Indexed complex types are stored as keccak256 hashes in topics, not as their plain encoding.
task.implemented: Indexed reference-type params (all arrays — fixed or dynamic — plus tuples, string, bytes) now return {:indexed_hash, <<32 bytes>>} via a local reference_type?/1 predicate matching the Solidity spec's 'all complex types' event-indexing rule (broader than FunctionSelector.dynamic?/1's head/tail rule). Static value-type indexed params unchanged. Filed upstream as #53; awaiting maintainer response.

task.title: fixed/ufixed/function parse but cannot encode + typespec gaps (upstream #54)
task.body: lib/abi/parser.ex and function_selector.ex: fixed/ufixed/function types parsed but had no encoder, and @type type was missing {:bytes, N}.
task.implemented: Parse-time rejection of :function, {:fixed, M, N}, {:ufixed, M, N} (incl. nested in arrays/tuples) with an ArgumentError linking upstream #54; {:bytes, pos_integer()} added to @type type. NOTE: the :function rejection was later lifted in 1.3.0 (see task 33). fixed/ufixed stay rejected per Solidity's own incomplete support. Awaiting upstream response.

task.title: Lexer 'x' terminal shadowed by LETTERS rule (sub-bug of #54)
task.body: src/ethereum_abi_lexer.xrl / ethereum_abi_parser.yrl: a single 'x' (the separator in fixedMxN) was shadowed by the {LETTERS} rule, so the explicit-M/N fixed forms never lexed correctly.
task.implemented: Dedicated fixed_typename / ufixed_typename lexer terminals so 'x' only separates in fixed/ufixed contexts; 'x' rule moved before {LETTERS} so single 'x' lexes as the terminal; parser gains identifier_part -> 'x' | fixed_typename | ufixed_typename so single-char 'x' and keyword forms still work as names. Explicit M/N forms route through reject_unsupported!/1 with the #54 ArgumentError. Shift/reduce count 1 → 3 (new conflicts resolve as shift, desired; documented inline). Upstream filing deferred to a future batched issue.

task.title: dynamic?/1 crashes on zero-length fixed array
task.body: lib/abi/function_selector.ex:484: dynamic?/1 had no clause for {:array, _type, 0} and crashed on T[0].
task.implemented: One-line fix: def dynamic?({:array, _type, 0}), do: false. Encoder/decoder already handled zero-length arrays correctly — verified by extending roundtrip_property_test.exs's fixed-array length domain to 0..3. Pre-existing upstream; not yet filed (candidate to fold with the lexer fix into a single PR).

task.title: encode_int/2 byte-vs-bit overflow guard rejected ALL int<N> (upstream #55)
task.body: lib/abi/type_encoder.ex:382-401: the overflow guard compared byte_size(significant_bytes) against desired_size_bytes - 1 (= 0 for int8), so even encoding 0 raised; most non-trivial int16/int32 values failed too.
task.implemented: Replaced the byte-vs-bit guard with an up-front numeric range check against 2^(N-1), so the encoder accepts the full signed range -2^(N-1)..2^(N-1)-1 for every int<N>. The pre-existing 'int overflow raises data overflow' test passed only because the encoder was broken for all values; tightened to assert in-range values encode AND boundary cases (128, -129) raise. Surfaced by the round-trip property suite on first run. Filed upstream #55; awaiting response.

task.title: :string decode silently truncated at first NUL byte
task.body: lib/abi/type_decoder.ex:295-298: the :string decode clause split the decoded binary at the first <<0>> via nul_terminate_string/1, treating Solidity strings as C strings. Solidity strings are length-prefixed UTF-8 and may legally contain NUL codepoints. Affects ABI.decode/3, decode_call/3, decode_event/4, TypeDecoder.decode/3.
task.implemented: Removed the nul_terminate_string/1 helper entirely; :string decode now delegates straight to decode_bytes(rest, length, :right) (Math.unpad already returns the right length). Surfaced by the mixed-element tuple[] property (task 28). Pre-existing upstream since 2018 (bdceb719). Three regression tests added (leading/embedded/all-NUL). Upstream filing pending — batch with the lexer x sub-bug.

task.title: Descripex on ABI top-level
task.body: Annotate the public ABI module so its surface is discoverable via __api__/0 and progressive disclosure. Add {:descripex, ~> 0.6} as a runtime dep.
task.implemented: Added :descripex runtime dep; annotated the seven public functions in lib/abi.ex (encode/2, method_id/1, decode/3, decode_call/3, decode_event/4, event_signature/1, parse_specification/1) with api() under namespace /abi; wired use Descripex.Discoverable, modules: [ABI]. Verified: ABI.describe/0..2 returns hints, ABI.__api__() lists all seven, mix descripex.manifest emits 11 entries (7 annotated + 4 Discoverable bookkeeping).

task.title: Descripex on remaining public modules
task.body: Extend api() annotations to the remaining public modules so the full surface is declared and the hint-rot cross-check can enforce coverage.
task.implemented: Annotated all 18 documented public functions across ABI.Event (/selector), ABI.FunctionSelector (/selector — 3 @doc false internals excluded), ABI.TypeEncoder (/codec — encode_bytes/1 excluded), ABI.TypeDecoder (/codec), ABI.Math (/math); wired composes_with: across natural pairings; extended Discoverable to all six modules. Manifest now emits 25 user-declared api() entries + 4 framework exports.

task.title: Custom manifest task + hint-rot validation test
task.body: Add a project manifest task and a test that prevents hint rot by asserting every non-framework export is api()-declared.
task.implemented: Added lib/mix/tasks/hieroglyph.manifest.ex (mix hieroglyph.manifest [path], defaults to api_manifest.json) and test/abi/agent_economy_test.exs (17 tests; load-bearing cross-check walks module_info(:exports) and asserts every non-framework export is api()-declared). Documented in README 'Agent Integration'; CLAUDE.md 'Layout' gets the manifest task row.

task.title: decode_event/4 error contract narrowed (bugfix-honoring-typespec)
task.body: lib/abi/event.ex: the @spec declared {:error, term()} but the runtime path raised on malformed payloads and returned string-formatted signature errors.
task.implemented: Wrapped the decode_raw-driven payload decode in try/rescue → {:error, {:malformed_data, _}}; tightened verify_event_signature/2 to atom-tagged {:error, {:event_signature_mismatch, %{expected, got}}}. Added @type ABI.Event.decode_error/0 and narrowed decode_event/4's @spec to the closed set; api() carries an errors: block. Not a meaningful breaking change (prior contract was unreachable for malformed payloads). Pair upstream with task 11 as one bug/hygiene PR.

task.title: encode_bytes/1 flipped to defp
task.body: lib/abi/type_encoder.ex: encode_bytes/1 was accidentally public (def + @doc false) with zero external callers.
task.implemented: Flipped def → defp and dropped the now-redundant @doc false. Already @doc false, zero callers across the monorepo, already excluded from the hint-rot test — manifest user-declared count unchanged. Pair upstream with task 10.

task.title: ABI.decode_error/2 helper (Solidity 0.8.4+ custom errors)
task.body: Decode Solidity 0.8.4+ custom-error revert data by matching the first-4-byte selector against a list of known error definitions, mirroring decode_call/3's contract.
task.implemented: Matches the 4-byte selector against a list of error definitions (signature strings or pre-parsed FunctionSelector structs, mixed accepted), decodes the first match. Returns {:ok, %{error: name, args: [...]}}, {:error, :no_match}, or {:error, :calldata_too_short}. Malformed payload after a selector match still raises (same as decode/3). Pair upstream with task 13 as one feature PR.

task.title: ABI.encode_packed/2 support
task.body: Solidity non-standard packed encoding for Merkle airdrop leaves and keccak256(abi.encodePacked(...)) schemes.
task.implemented: Per spec: types <32 bytes concatenate tight (no padding); dynamic types (bytes, string) inline as raw payload (no length prefix); array elements pad to 32 bytes (or 32-byte multiples for string/bytes); tuples/structs and nested arrays raise ArgumentError with a spec link. Polymorphic first arg like encode/2. Cross-checked against the canonical spec example and a Merkle-leaf golden vector (address ++ uint256 → 52 bytes). Pair upstream with task 12.

task.title: Map-input encoder tests
task.body: type_encoder.ex data_to_list/2 map branch (struct/map input) lacked explicit coverage.
task.implemented: 7 test cases + a demonstrative doctest in test/abi/type_encoder_test.exs covering atom keys, string keys, camelCase→snake_case resolution, string-over-atom priority, integer values in nested named-struct maps, and the two raise paths.

task.title: Round-trip property test suite
task.body: Property-based decode(encode(x)) == x coverage for every type in FunctionSelector.@type type/0.
task.implemented: Added test/abi/roundtrip_property_test.exs using stream_data — per-type properties for uint/int/address/bool/string/bytes/bytesN, fixed and dynamic arrays, mixed static+dynamic tuples, plus a recursive composite property (depth ≤ 3) for nested {:tuple, [{:array, ...}]}. The composite property surfaced the encode_int bug (task 5) on first run.

task.title: Error-path tests
task.body: 11 error branches across encoder/decoder/function-selector were untested.
task.implemented: Regression coverage for bool/bytes type mismatches, int/uint overflow, trailing decode data, unsupported type atoms across encoder/decoder/function-selector, and event-signature / topics-length mismatches in decode_event/4.

task.title: Fill @spec and @doc gaps
task.body: Many public functions lacked @spec/@doc, dragging Doctor coverage down.
task.implemented: Added specs for every previously-undeclared public function across ABI, ABI.Event, ABI.TypeDecoder, ABI.TypeEncoder, ABI.FunctionSelector; added docs for TypeDecoder.tuple_value/3 and decode_bytes/3. Doctor spec coverage 42% → 88%, doc coverage 88% → 96%.

task.title: Refresh README
task.body: README carried a stale tuple caveat, wrong encode/2 arity, wrong bytes<M> marker, and dead solidity.readthedocs.io links.
task.implemented: Dropped stale tuple caveat, corrected ABI.encode/2 arity and bytes<M> support marker, migrated links to docs.soliditylang.org, added runnable examples for parse_specification/1, Event.decode_event/4, and map/struct input to encode/2.

task.title: Extract padding helpers into ABI.Math
task.body: Encoder and decoder each duplicated the 32-byte byte-domain padding formula (three TODO: add to ABI.Math comments).
task.implemented: Added ABI.Math.pad/4 and unpad/3; TypeEncoder and TypeDecoder now delegate. Resolved the three TODOs. Zero behavior change.

task.title: Credo strict cleanup (AliasUsage + MaxLineLength + ParameterPatternMatching + Nesting)
task.body: mix credo --strict reported 51 issues.
task.implemented: Drove 51 → 0. Top-of-module aliases across ABI, Event, FunctionSelector, Parser, TypeDecoder, TypeEncoder, Hex; wrapped long specs; refactored the Enum.reduce tuple-encoder into encode_tuple_element/2; flipped three record = %{} heads; extracted verify_event_signature/2 and fetch_named_field/2 + fetch_by_name/2 to drop nesting.

task.title: Rename ABI.FunctionSelector.is_dynamic?/1 → dynamic?/1
task.body: Credo PredicateFunctionNames flagged is_dynamic?/1.
task.implemented: Renamed all 9 clause heads, the @spec, 2 recursive self-calls, and 3 private call-sites in TypeDecoder/TypeEncoder. No deprecation shim — @doc false since 2017, zero external callers, and a defdelegate shim would recreate the violation.

task.title: address payable vs address doc note
task.body: Document that address payable collapses to :address.
task.implemented: Added a @typedoc to FunctionSelector.@type type/0 clarifying that address payable collapses to :address (ABI JSON only emits 'address'; on-the-wire encoding identical; payability is a state_mutability property, not a type variant).

task.title: Bound atom creation in decode_structs: true path
task.body: DoS surface: ABI.TypeDecoder.tuple_value/3 and TypeEncoder.fetch_by_name/2 created atoms from contract-supplied field names (gated by sobelow_skip on a 'trusted ABI metadata' assumption that breaks for arbitrary-source ABIs). The atom table is non-reclaimable VM resource.
task.implemented: Both call sites route through String.to_existing_atom/1; sobelow_skip annotations removed. Decoder requires snake_case field atoms to be pre-interned; new private atom_key_for!/1 re-raises ArgumentError with a migration hint naming both the underscored atom and the original field. Encoder change is a silent safety upgrade. Picked option (a); rejected per-selector budget / per-process cap as API bloat. README grew a 'Pre-interning atoms for decode_structs: true' subsection. Upstream filing pending — propose the same switch or a decode_structs: :existing_atoms opt-in.

task.title: Mine defi-skills intent-to-transaction action surface for ABI coverage gaps
task.body: Read-only discovery exercise: enumerate the defi-skills action surface (~53 actions across 13 protocols) and map relevant actions to hieroglyph's scope — ABI encoding patterns surfaced by the calldata (selectors, struct encoding, dynamic types, nested tuples, edge cases). Propose D/B/U-scored candidate tasks.
task.implemented: pipx install defi-skills 0.3.0; mined 53 actions across 13 protocols. Output landed as the 'Proposed additions from defi-skills mining' section, which became the DeFi Fixtures + Property Suite bundles (tasks 25-31). Discovery only — no ABI.* edits in this task.

task.title: Real-world golden calldata fixtures from defi-skills build
task.body: Capture round-trip golden calldata vectors from defi-skills build across multiple protocols so the encoder/decoder are pinned against real-world calldata.
task.implemented: test/abi/defi_calldata_test.exs — 10 round-trip golden vectors via defi-skills build --json (v0.3.0). Inline @fixtures attribute (the test/fixtures/defi_calldata.exs proposal was discarded — no .exs data-loading idiom in the repo). Each fixture asserts both directions. Covers Aave V3 supply/borrow/setCollateral, Compound V3 supply/claim, Lido stake/unstake (uint256[] head/tail), EigenLayer deposit, ERC-20 transfer, WETH unwrap.

task.title: Function selector golden vectors against FunctionSelector.encode/1
task.body: Golden-vector tests proving method_id/1 and the canonical-signature serialization match the spec across protocols, incl. tuple / tuple[] / fixed-array signatures.
task.implemented: test/abi/function_selector_real_world_test.exs — 12 ABI.method_id/1 golden vectors (Aave, Compound, Lido uint256[], Curve uint256[3], Uniswap V3 tuple arg, Balancer V2 multiple top-level tuples, EigenLayer tuple[], ERC-20, WETH). task.body:
Give the ABI suite an oracle that is independent of the implementation, and prove it by planting defects that must fail the run.

WHY (corrected premise — do not repeat the older framing). The weakness is NOT that encoder and decoder share padding helpers: `ABI.Math.pad/4` (math.ex:120) and `unpad/3` (math.ex:185) are two independently written implementations, and `TypeDecoder.decode_int/2` (type_decoder.ex:475) uses the BEAM's native signed bit-syntax rather than re-deriving two's complement — so a padding-direction flip or a sign-extension bug DOES break the round trip. The real blind spot is narrower and stronger: the decoder never reads the offset the encoder writes. `TypeDecoder` parses the head word into `{:dynamic, type, tail_position}` (type_decoder.ex:365) and then discards it — `{:dynamic, type, _tail_position} -> decode_type(...)` (type_decoder.ex:378) — consuming the tail sequentially in declaration order instead. Offset arithmetic is therefore round-trip-invisible by non-use. The second class is self-verification: `ABI.method_id/1` is called once to build the selector (abi.ex:253) and again to check it (abi.ex:487), and `Event.event_signature/1` likewise (event.ex:148 vs event.ex:487) — the same deterministic bug computes both sides.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (extend it, do not rebuild it). ~30 independent hex/selector assertions are already in place: 9 real DeFi calldata fixtures (defi_calldata_test.exs, sourced from defi-skills v0.3.0), 11 mainnet method_ids plus 4 selector round-trips (function_selector_real_world_test.exs), the Solidity packed-mode spec example and a Merkle leaf (encode_packed_test.exs), 4 ERC-20 selectors (abi_test.exs). Doctests additionally pin `Math.kec/1` digests, `method_id("transfer(address,uint256)") == "a9059cbb"`, the ERC-20 Transfer topic0, and nested-tuple hex in TypeEncoder's moduledoc. roundtrip_property_test.exs (28 properties, composite depth 5) is pure self-consistency and exercises only `encode_raw`/`decode_raw` — it never touches the selector or event paths at all.

AUTHORITIES. Solidity ABI spec, https://docs.soliditylang.org/en/latest/abi-spec.html — #formal-specification-of-the-encoding (head/tail; head(X(i)) is the offset of tail(X(i)) relative to the start of enc(X); bytes/string are `enc(k) pad_right(X)`; uint left-padded with zero bytes, int left-padded with 0xff when negative), #function-selector, #events, #encoding-of-indexed-event-parameters. Vector corpus: ethers.js `@ethersproject/testcases` 5.8.0 (MIT) — the only surveyed corpus that is machine-readable, large, and derived from real solc-compiled output; eth-abi, viem and alloy keep their vectors inline in test code and are not copyable. `ethereum/tests` ABITests/basic_abi_tests.json holds only 3 vectors. solc 0.8.10 is available locally (`--combined-json abi,bin-runtime,hashes`) if a fixture needs generating rather than borrowing.

PLANTED MUTANTS (verified single-site edits; several are already caught by existing doctests — that does not count, see AC4):
1. type_encoder.ex:469 — write `encode_uint(0, 256)` instead of `encode_uint(tail_position, 256)`
2. type_encoder.ex:472 — drop the `+ byte_size(el)`, so tail_position never advances
3. type_encoder.ex:429 — `tail_start = count(types) * 32 + 32`
4. abi.ex:287 — shift the 4-byte selector slice by one byte
5. math.ex:70 — reverse the keccak digest in `kec/1`
6. event.ex:528 — `FunctionSelector.encode(selector, true)` in `event_signature/1`
7. event.ex:397 — delete the `reference_type?({:tuple, _})` clause
8. math.ex:41 — flip the negative-dividend branch of `mod/2`

MECHANICS. Mutants live as patches and are applied/reverted by the mix task; lib/abi/* is touched only transiently and must be restored byte-exact. Run the corpus twice and keep the signals apart: against the new vectors alone (the number that matters) and against the full suite (the "caught by something else" column). Do not let `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` or credo count as a kill — static analysis is a different oracle. Reviewer must be cross-family relative to the implementer; cursor and grok are one family, so a codex implementer pairs with either.
task.implemented: Vendored a 1,601-vector filtered subset of the MIT @ethersproject/testcases 5.8.0 corpus under test/support/fixtures/ethers/ (PROVENANCE.md records source, license, fetch date and the four ordered filter criteria; vendor.py re-vendors deterministically) plus test/support/ethers_corpus.ex as its loader. test/abi/ethers_corpus_test.exs asserts ABI.encode/2, ABI.decode/3, ABI.method_id/1, ABI.encode_event_topics/2, event data and ABI.decode_event/4 byte-for-byte against solc-recorded expectations, with no decode(encode(x)) step on any assertion path. test/abi/abi_spec_test.exs adds 19 spec-anchored assertions citing their ABI-spec section, pinning the head/tail offset VALUE, the length word for bytes/string/dynamic arrays, and standard-ABI padding direction (cross-checked with Foundry cast, never with this library). test/support/mutants/mutants.exs plants the eight enumerated single-site mutations, applied and reverted byte-exactly by MIX_ENV=test mix hieroglyph.mutants (test/support/mix/tasks/, not lib/, so the runner does not enter the 95% coverage gate); anchors must match exactly once, so a moved site fails loudly. 7 of 8 are killed by the new vectors ALONE; mod-negative-branch is recorded as a survivor with the call-site evidence that ABI.Math.mod/2's negative branch is unreachable from the wire path. The oracle found and this task fixed two real defects invisible to the round-trip suite: TypeEncoder counted a static T[k] as one head slot (offset 0x40 where Solidity writes 0x80 for (bytes,address[3]) — 79/811 interface vectors failed) and Event.do_decode_event/4 reserved a topics[0] slot for anonymous events (194/414 event vectors failed). docs/abi-verification-ledger.md records authorities with fetch dates, the vendored corpus, the mutant table and the survivor review; CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased]. api_manifest.json unchanged. mix ci green: 453 tests, 97.19% coverage, dialyzer clean.

task.title: Gate api_manifest.json freshness in mix ci
acceptance_criteria: mix hieroglyph.manifest gains a --check mode that regenerates in memory, compares against the committed api_manifest.json ignoring only the generated_at timestamp, and exits non-zero with a readable diff when they differ
The check is a step in the mix ci alias, so a descripex upgrade or an api() edit that changes the manifest fails the gate instead of drifting silently
The committed api_manifest.json is regenerated once against the currently locked descripex so the gate starts green; the regeneration diff is reviewed, not blind-accepted
A test covers both directions of --check (matching manifest passes, mutated manifest fails), so the new task-mode code does not sink the 95% coverage gate
CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased]
out_of_scope: Changing which functions carry api() declarations, or any change to the public ABI surface
Making generated_at deterministic or dropping it from the artifact — the check ignores the field instead
Publishing the manifest anywhere outside this repo
task.body:
api_manifest.json is a committed contract-stability artifact consumed by the downstream cartouche/onchain CI, and nothing verifies it still matches the code that generates it.

Discovered 2026-08-22 while landing task 44. A bare `mix hieroglyph.manifest` against the currently locked descripex produces a large diff against the committed file: descripex 0.13 emits `schema` objects on `:value` params (`{"type": "string"}`, array/enum/minimum shapes) that the committed manifest predates, and it rewrote the `describe/1` description and spec (`module() | atom()` -> `module() | atom() | String.t()`). None of that came from a hieroglyph change — the artifact simply drifted behind a dependency upgrade that `mix ci` had no way to notice. Task 44 deliberately restored the committed file rather than regenerating it, because its acceptance criteria required the manifest to come out unchanged; the drift is real and still there.

The gate has one wrinkle worth naming: the task stamps `generated_at` on every run, so a byte comparison can never pass. `--check` must compare everything except that field.

Right-size note: the regeneration itself is a one-command inline fix. What earns a task is the gate — without it the next dependency bump re-drifts the artifact, and the repo learns about it the same accidental way it did this time.

Both directions covered in test/abi/agent_economy_test.exs. The CHANGELOG entry was added post-land by the orchestrator: the reviewer reverted it because reviewers must not deliver CHANGELOG changes.

The campaign covers lib/abi/*.ex with all 18 mutators, no filtering and no sampling, from a reproducible script committed under .mutation/
Every survivor is dispositioned in writing as one of: killed by a new test added in this task, provably equivalent with the argument, or an accepted gap with the reason. None is left unclassified
docs/abi-verification-ledger.md gains a campaign section recording muex version, mutator set, per-module counts and each survivor disposition
mix ci passes and the touched modules stay at or above their current coverage
out_of_scope: Adopting muex as a mix ci gate. This stays an on-demand measurement plus the tests it produces
Mutating src/ (yecc and leex output) or lib/mix/tasks/
Re-deriving task 44 oracle, spec assertions or planted corpus. They are the input here, not the work
Patching muex under deps/ to work around #20. A measurement produced by a hand-patched tool is not a durable verification record
task.body:
Task 44 built the deterministic half of ABI wire-format verification: an independent 1,601-vector oracle from @ethersproject/testcases, 19 spec-anchored assertions, and eight planted single-site mutants under test/support/mutants/mutants.exs, applied and reverted byte-exactly by `MIX_ENV=test mix hieroglyph.mutants`. It deliberately excluded an automated sweep, in its own words: "muex 0.8.2 (MIT, Elixir ~> 1.14) was released 2026-08-19 and is unproven on this codebase; the deterministic planted corpus is the gate here. Revisit once the corpus and ledger exist and there is something to compare a sweep against." Both now exist on disk (test/support/mutants/mutants.exs, docs/abi-verification-ledger.md), so the stated revisit condition is met. This task is that revisit.

The deliverable is not a mutation score. It is the faults the hand-planted eight did not think of. Task 44 own yield is the argument that this surface rewards the search: the oracle exposed two real defects the round-trip suite structurally could not see - TypeEncoder counted a static T[k] as one head slot (offset 0x40 where Solidity writes 0x80), and Event.do_decode_event/4 reserved a topics[0] slot for anonymous events - both shipped as fixes in 1.7.0. Neither is reachable from the onchain family, which is why nobody here noticed them for years.

Grade the tool before trusting it. The planted corpus is a known-answer test for muex: 7 of the 8 mutants are killed by the existing vectors alone, and the 8th (mod-negative-branch) is a recorded survivor carrying a call-site unreachability argument. A run that cannot reproduce that split is not measuring anything, and a 100% score is its known failure signature rather than a result.

That failure is live right now. muex 0.8.2 cannot report a surviving mutant on Elixir 1.20 at all: Muex.TestRunner.Port.count_failures/2 matches the pre-1.20 ExUnit summary wording (N tests, M failures), while 1.20 prints Result: N passed / Failed: N test. The regex misses, the fallback returns 1 failure, and the only path to :survived is unreachable - so every survivor is reported killed. Filed as Oeditus/muex#20 (2026-08-23) with a four-file reproduction and a patch; upstream acknowledged it the same morning. Verified against cartouche task 114, whose campaign hit exactly this and could not produce its central deliverable.

Add the dep in the same change (only: [:dev, :test], runtime: false, matching cartouche) at whatever release carries the #20 fix. Do not pin 0.8.2.

Copy the campaign mechanics rather than re-deriving them: ~/_DATA/code/cartouche/.mutation/run.sh runs ONE invocation over the whole surface with all 18 mutators and --no-filter --no-optimize --coverage-guided. Per-module invocations are not equivalent in cost - muex rebuilds its coverage line index by running the suite once per test file, serially, with no cache, so N invocations pay that N times over. In cartouche that is what exhausted a harness run lifetime budget.

Scope muex at lib/ only. src/ is yecc and leex output, and .reach.exs already had to be scoped away from it for the same class of reason: a smell or a mutant in generated Erlang is unfixable by definition. Premise unverified - muex behavior on :erlc_paths has not been tested here; confirm it on the first run and record what it does.

Routing is left open on purpose. The surface is a dispatch trigger and the tool now works, so this is genuinely dispatchable - but rmap freezes assignee at creation, and nobody has yet measured what a campaign over this surface costs in wall-clock or in survivor-triage judgement. Decide the routing when the campaign is actually scheduled, not here.

Confirmed 2026-08-24 on muex 0.8.3 (released the same day; Oeditus/muex#20 closed 09:42Z): the four-file reproduction reports survived=2 and a 0.0% score on Elixir 1.20.2 / OTP 29, and the converse check - the same two mutants against a value-asserting test - reports killed=2 and 100%, so the tool is not simply calling everything survived now. Re-run the reproduction against whatever version is installed when the campaign actually starts; this note records that a working release exists, not that the installed one is it.

task.title: Cartouche.Transaction.V_2930 — add EIP-2930 (type 0x1) JSON deserialization
task.body:
Surfaced during PR #55 / INE-44 close-out (Codex GitHub bot finding). EIP-2930 (Berlin, 2021) introduced the access-list transaction type; mainnet-active for ~5 years. Cartouche.Block.deserialize/1 currently raises ArgumentError with a 'not yet supported' message when it encounters params['type'] == '0x1' — correct as a temporary stance but means any block containing an EIP-2930 tx crashes the deserializer. The matching raw-bytes envelope dispatcher in Cartouche.Transaction.decode/1 returns {:error, :unknown_envelope_type} for the <<0x01, _::binary>> pattern — same gap on the raw side.

Implement: introduce Cartouche.Transaction.V_2930 module mirroring V2's structural shape minus max_fee_per_gas/max_priority_fee_per_gas (EIP-2930 is pre-EIP-1559, single gas_price field with access list); wire from_json/1 into the Cartouche.Block dispatch table; replace decode/1's <<0x01, _>> error tuple with V_2930.decode/1. Add integration anchor against a known type-1 mainnet block.

Pre-mutation gate: Cartouche.Transaction is critical-tier (≥95%); confirm coverage before mutating. Both bot-finding pinning tests flip from assert_raise / assert {:error, :unknown_envelope_type} to positive shape assertions when this lands.

task.title: Audit RPC-level requirements bubbling up from defi-skills mining
task.body:
Read-only triage: scan the sibling-repo defi-skills:intent-to-transaction mining output for RPC-level requirements that bubble down to cartouche — eth_call edge cases (revert-data shape, gas-stipend behavior), eth_estimateGas semantics on reverts, log-filter quirks, fee-history math, eth_getCode for proxy detection. Surfaced needs get filed as new tasks here. No cartouche code edits in this task itself.

TRIAGE PASS 1 EXECUTED 2026-08-22 — three of the four upstream inputs are settled and produced nothing RPC-relevant. The original gate ("after all four upstream tasks close") is unsatisfiable as written and must not be waited on:
- hieroglyph (done): output was pure ABI-encoding work — golden calldata vectors, selector vectors, tuple[]/nested-struct round-trips (its tasks 25-31). Zero JSON-RPC content.
- onchain_evm #51 (SUPERSEDED, never executed): its named successor is a local revm/ForkDB simulation bug in native/onchain_evm/src/lib.rs (default BlockEnv, state-override clobbering un-fetched accounts). Internal to that repo's Rust harness; no bearing on cartouche's JSON-RPC client.
- onchain: the mining task was NEVER PLANTED there (0 matches for defi-skills in its roadmap/tasks.toml). It will never close.
- onchain_aave #54: still pending. THE ONLY OUTSTANDING INPUT.

Pass 1 surfaced one real cartouche defect on its own — Error(string) reverts were being labelled with an unrelated caller-supplied ABI entry — which was fixed inline in the same session (lib/cartouche/rpc.ex: classify_decoded_error/4 built-in clause + a selector guard in find_error_abi/3), not deferred.

REMAINING WORK IS NARROW: when onchain_aave #54 lands, scan only its output. If it also yields nothing RPC-relevant, close this as "no action needed" citing pass 1 — do not re-derive the three settled repos. Reference points from pass 1 for judging any future finding: eth_getLogs is absent from cartouche entirely; eth_getCode (rpc.ex:567) is a raw bytecode fetch with no EIP-1967/1167 slot inspection; eth_feeHistory (rpc.ex:1570) is a passthrough over Cartouche.FeeHistory.deserialize/1. Those are uncovered ground, not gaps anyone has yet asked for.
task.implemented:
TRIAGE PASS 2 EXECUTED 2026-08-23, closing as "no action needed". The last outstanding input, onchain_aave #54, landed; its output was scanned per pass 1's instruction and yields nothing that bubbles down to cartouche's JSON-RPC layer. The four finding classes and why each stops short of this repo:

- Aave coverage gaps (setUserUseReserveAsCollateral, repayWithATokens, claim_rewards, eMode) are calldata-construction work; they became onchain_aave tasks 58/59/60 and name no RPC requirement. Grep for "cartouche" across that repo's roadmap returns only the 2026-04-30 planting note.
- Deployed-error semantics. #54 found swapBorrowRateMode gone from IPool since v3.2 (reverts live), and tasks 58/59/60 each pin a deployed error through fork tests. Aave v3.2+ raises custom Solidity errors, so the requirement is decoding those from revert data — already covered: Cartouche.RPC.decode_error/2 resolves caller-supplied :errors ABIs through find_error_abi/3, handles the compiler-defined Error(string) from its own selector (the defect pass 1 fixed), and carries the full Panic(uint256) code table.
- The eMode struct-arity mismatch (deployed six/seven-field EModeCategory vs eight in aave-v3-origin/main, which buffer-overruns when decoded against the source branch) is an ABI-decoder concern in hieroglyph, not in this library's RPC layer.
- ERC-2612 permit, deferred in #54 as "blocked on ERC-2612 signing absent from onchain core", is an onchain gap and not a cartouche one. Cartouche.Typed already expresses it: Domain carries name/version/chain_id/verifying_contract/salt, types are an arbitrary type_map, and encode/1 emits the canonical 0x1901 || domainSeparator || hashStruct preimage that Cartouche.Signer.sign/3 consumes.

Pass 1's reference points stand unchanged as uncovered-but-unrequested ground: eth_getLogs is absent from cartouche entirely, eth_getCode (rpc.ex:567) is a raw bytecode fetch with no EIP-1967/1167 slot inspection, and eth_feeHistory (rpc.ex:1570) is a passthrough over Cartouche.FeeHistory.deserialize/1. Nobody has asked for any of them; no task filed.

Read-only triage as scoped — no cartouche code edits in either pass. The one defect the audit did surface, pass 1's Error(string) mislabelling, shipped inline in ed1d091.

task.title: Cartouche.DebugTrace.StructLog — add CLZ (EIP-7939/Osaka) to the closed whitelist
task.body:
CLZ ('count leading zeros') is in go-ethereum master's newOsakaInstructionSet() per EIP-7607 Osaka composition, with EIP-7939 defining the opcode at slot 0x1e. Once Osaka activates, any eth_debug_traceCall against an Osaka tx that uses CLZ will raise ArgumentError in the closed whitelist.

Pre-add gate: confirm the mnemonic emitted in struct-logs matches 'CLZ' exactly against an Osaka testnet trace (geth's opCodeToString in core/vm/opcodes.go master is the source of truth); add the atom to @single_opcodes in lib/cartouche/debug_trace.ex and a regression test that round-trips the new mnemonic.

Watch list for Amsterdam (post-Osaka): SLOTNUM (0x4b, EIP-7843) — currently Draft, file separately when EIP leaves Draft and Amsterdam composition firms up.

Replaces the abandoned Task 68 (which conflated EIP-3074's withdrawn AUTH/AUTHCALL with EIP-7702). Discovered during Codex consultation 2026-05-01.

Added CLZ to @single_opcodes in lib/cartouche/debug_trace.ex (next to SAR, matching its 0x1e slot), updated the deserialize/1 doc to say the whitelist covers Osaka's CLZ, and added a regression test asserting StructLog.deserialize decodes "CLZ" to :CLZ. task.title: Restore dialyzer to the standard PR harness — the OOM premise was the Assembly bomb, now fixed
task.body:
PREMISE FALSIFIED 2026-06-05 by the Task 103 Assembly fix. The original framing of this task — "the deps PLT exceeds the 16 GB ubuntu-latest budget; run 25319850405 OOM'd while adding 621 modules; needs a larger runner" — attributed the 2026-05-04 CI OOM to dep-set SIZE. It was not size. It was Cartouche.Assembly.compile/1's 7-arity tuple_set product exploding dialyzer's success-typing fixpoint on OTP 29 — the same ~30 GB bomb Task 103 diagnosed and fixed. Collapsing the seven heads to one is_tuple/1 clause cut a downstream cold PLT build 27.6 GB -> 1.02 GB; cartouche's own local dialyzer now peaks ~3.49 GB. The 621-module dep PLT was never the problem.

Consequences for this task:
- The three old "restoration shapes" (32 GB ubuntu-latest-large workflow / aggressive :plt_ignore_apps trimming / nightly cron) are ALL obsolete — a stock 16 GB ubuntu-latest now has ~12 GB headroom.
- The 2026-05-04 "upstream dep-slimming ruled out" investigation is moot — size was never the lever.
- :plt_ignore_apps for the GCP cluster (google_api_cloud_kms et al.) can stay as-is for unknown_type hygiene, but is no longer load-bearing for memory.

Re-scoped work:
1. Measure cartouche's COLD CI PLT build peak RSS post-Assembly-fix on a stock ubuntu-latest (rm priv/plts cache; /usr/bin/time the deps PLT add). Expectation: well under 16 GB.
2. If it fits (very likely), restore dialyzer to the NORMAL PR harness (.github/workflows/harness.yml) — no separate workflow, no larger runner. If it somehow doesn't, fall back to the push-to-development workflow, but that is now the unlikely branch.
3. This is the trigger that lifts the project-CLAUDE.md rule "Never delegate dialyzer-scoped tasks to cloud agents" — once a cloud-agent VM completes a full cartouche PLT build at the new memory floor, that rule and this repo's no-cloud-dialyzer delegation block can both relax. Verify with one cloud/CI cold-build measurement before lifting; don't lift on the downstream onchain number alone.
task.implemented: Cold `mix dialyzer` (PLT build + analysis, MIX_ENV=dev, priv/plts removed) measured 2026-06-05 on host: peak RSS 1,054,408,704 B ≈ 1.0 GB, 26.0s real, 0 warnings (11 skipped via .dialyzer_ignore.exs), exit 0 — ~15x under the 16 GB ubuntu-latest budget. Restored dialyzer to .github/workflows/harness.yml as a normal step (MIX_ENV=dev, with a priv/plts cache); reverted the 2026-05-04 carve-out comments in harness.yml top + body. No larger runner / separate workflow / extra :plt_ignore_apps trim needed — the size premise was the Assembly tuple_set bomb (Task 103), not dep count. Real ubuntu-latest verification runs on the push-to-development that ships this. NOTE: the CLAUDE.md 'never delegate dialyzer to cloud agents' rule still needs one cloud-agent (Cursor/Codex VM) cold PLT build observed under budget before it lifts — CI green on GitHub's runner is necessary but the cloud-VM memory ceiling differs; keep that rule hard until a cloud build is actually seen completing.

task.title: Phase 4 follow-up — tighten Cartouche.Typed.encode_value_map/3 impl so dialyzer infers binary(), restore stricter @spec
task.body:
Filed 2026-05-06 from PR #50 review (Copilot low-confidence finding). Loosening the spec to bitstring() in INE-39 silenced dialyzer cheaply but masks the byte-alignment invariant hash_struct/3's <> operator requires (type_hash <> encode_data would crash at runtime on a non-byte-aligned bitstring). Every actual branch in Type.encode_data_value/2 returns 32-byte aligned binary, so the impl IS byte-aligned in practice — but the spec no longer pins it against future drift.

Tighten the for {field, type} <- fields, into: <<>> comprehension (e.g. annotate the body as ::binary or wrap each branch through IO.iodata_to_binary/1) so dialyzer can prove binary(), then restore @spec encode_value_map/3 :: binary(). Pinning tests in test/typed_test.exs from Task 45 cover the contract. Touched-file scope; no callsite changes.

task.title: Fix the ~30 GB downstream dialyzer bomb — collapse Assembly.compile/1's 7-arity tuple_set (NOT IConsole)
acceptance_criteria: A downstream `mix dialyzer` over a cartouche-dependent app no longer spikes to ~30 GB — documented peak ceiling < 4 GB, measured before/after with /usr/bin/time -l. ACHIEVED: onchain cold PLT build 27.6 GB -> 1.02 GB.

`Cartouche.Assembly.compile/1` behavior preserved — operand ordering, arity validation, raise-on-unknown/wrong-arity all unchanged; new assembly_test.exs cases for 1-/2-operand opcodes + wrong-arity raise.
Cartouche's full suite stays green and coverage gates hold; no dead-branch / dialyzer warnings on the touched file.
Before/after dialyzer peak-RSS numbers recorded in CHANGELOG + the implemented field.
out_of_scope: No onchain-side changes — onchain Task 75 already shipped its serialization stopgap.
IConsole surface-slimming — turned out to be ~250 MB, not the bomb; split to follow-up Task 105.
Not touching the IConsole ABI / console.sol version.
task.body:
ORIGINAL PREMISE (FALSIFIED): this task was opened blaming `Cartouche.Contract.IConsole` (the 4,577-fn generated Hardhat console.sol binding) as the ~30 GB downstream dialyzer memory bomb, on the theory that its 2.0 MB beam / combinatorial typed `log` overload surface dominated dialyzer's success-typing peak. That premise was WRONG and is corrected below — left in the record so future sessions don't re-chase it.

ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed 2026-06-04 via isolated A/B + onchain end-to-end measurement): `Cartouche.Assembly.compile/1`. The function had seven fixed-arity tuple heads — `{op,a}`, `{op,a,b}`, … `{op,a,b,c,d,e,f,g}` — each guarded `opcode in @n_operands` (a large atom-union in tuple slot 0). Together those form a 7-shape `tuple_set` product type with big atom-unions; under `compile/1`'s self-recursion, dialyzer's success-typing fixpoint over that product explodes to ~30 GB peak RSS on OTP 29. NOT IConsole, NOT List.flatten, NOT the polymorphic return — the tuple_set product itself.

DISPROOF OF THE IConsole PREMISE:
- PLT *stored bytes* and PLT-*build peak RSS* are decoupled. IConsole was #1 in stored type-surface bytes (5.9 MB, 21% of the .plt file) but only ~1% of peak RSS during build.
- The Assembly fix was measured with the FULL, un-slimmed IConsole still present: onchain cold PLT build dropped 27.6 GB -> 1.02 GB. Slimming IConsole on top (the abandoned data-table prototype) bought only a further ~250 MB (1.02 -> 0.77 GB). So IConsole was never the bomb.
- Isolated A/B on Assembly alone: 31.1 GB -> 1.54 GB.

THE FIX (shipped on `development`): collapse the seven fixed-arity heads into ONE generic `def compile(op) when is_tuple(op) and tuple_size(op) >= 2` clause that reads the opcode's operand count from `@opcodes` via `Map.fetch/2` and validates arity in the body (`length(args) == arity`), instead of per-arity heads + atom-union guards. Eliminates the tuple_set. Behavior-preserving: operands still reverse-compile so they land on the stack in source order; unknown opcode / wrong arity still raises `InvalidAssembly`. Also dropped a dead `if false && x == 0` branch in the integer clause. Replaced the `@opcodes_with_operand_count` lambda with an inline comprehension for `@no_operands` (the other arity attrs were unused after the collapse).

MEASUREMENTS (onchain, `plt_add_deps: :apps_direct`, path-dep to this checkout, cold PLT build, /usr/bin/time -l peak RSS):
- Before (7-arity tuple_set): 27.6 GB, minutes of wall.
- After (generic is_tuple/1 clause): 1.02 GB, 14.9 s. ~27x memory cut.
- Cached-PLT analysis phase after the fix: 0.54 GB / 1.1 s.
task.implemented: Done 2026-06-04 on `development` (direct commit). Root cause was NOT IConsole (original premise falsified) but `Cartouche.Assembly.compile/1`'s 7-arity tuple_set product type, which blew dialyzer's success-typing fixpoint to ~30 GB under self-recursion on OTP 29. Fix: collapse the seven fixed-arity heads into one `is_tuple/1` clause with body-level arity validation against `@opcodes`. onchain downstream cold PLT build 27.6 GB -> 1.02 GB (~27x); isolated Assembly A/B 31.1 -> 1.54 GB. Behavior preserved (operand order, arity check, raise-on-invalid); 3 new assembly_test.exs cases; full suite green. IConsole-slimming split to Task 105 (only ~250 MB, optional).

task.body:
Spun out of Task 103 after the ~30 GB bomb was correctly attributed to `Cartouche.Assembly.compile/1` (not IConsole). IConsole's combinatorial generated surface (4,577 fns across call/prepare/estimate_gas/execute/build_trx/encode/decode/log families for 381 ABI entries) is still the single largest contributor to PLT *stored bytes* (~5.9 MB, ~21% of the .plt file) and contributes ~250 MB to downstream dialyzer peak RSS — real but second-order versus the 27 GB Assembly win.

A data-table decode prototype (preserved on branch `task-103-slim-iconsole`, commit `fbe6dcc`, worktree `~/_DATA/worktrees/cartouche/103`) collapsed IConsole to a selector->FunctionSelector map + one generic `decode_call/1`, preserving the VM-facing contract. It was set aside because it was built on the falsified "IConsole is the bomb" premise; revisit ONLY if the ~250 MB / smaller PLT file is independently worth the generator's new whole-contract data-table emission mode. The only real consumer is `Cartouche.VM.decode_call/1`; downstream onchain `lib/`+`test/` reference IConsole zero times.

Low priority: the headline memory problem is already solved by Task 103.

task.title: Formalize signer backends as a behaviour (pure digest-signer contract) — unlock multi-provider signing
acceptance_criteria: A `Cartouche.Signer.Backend` behaviour exists with documented `@callback get_address/...` and `@callback sign/...`; the existing implicit MFA contract is now compile-checked.
`Cartouche.Signer.Curvy` and `Cartouche.Signer.CloudKMS` declare `@behaviour Cartouche.Signer.Backend` + `@impl true`, compile clean (warnings-as-errors), all existing doctests/tests green.

The sign contract is a PURE DIGEST/PAYLOAD signer: the backend signs exactly the bytes it is handed (secp256k1 backends expect the 32-byte digest; ed25519 backends expect the raw message). Message hashing moves OUT of the backend into the caller (`Cartouche.Signer` / a helper), so plain Eth-tx signing, EIP-712 typed-data, and Solana all reuse one backend set with no per-venue backend change. `find_recid` is fed the same digest the backend signed.

Both signer modules are at critical-tier >=95% coverage BEFORE mutating (raise first if below); full suite green; dialyzer run LOCALLY (per CLAUDE.md KMS-dialyzer-stays-local rule) shows no new warnings on touched files.

Config decision is recorded and proven by a test: either (a) keep `:priv_key`/`:cloud_kms` shorthands AND accept an explicit `{BackendModule, config}` form (non-breaking), or (b) clean break to module-form-only. A test asserts the chosen config path still starts a working signer end-to-end.
CHANGELOG + `implemented` field document the contract and the config decision.
out_of_scope: New backend implementations (AWS KMS secp256k1, Azure Key Vault P-256K/ES256K, HashiCorp Vault Transit ed25519 + Kaleido ethsign plugin for secp256k1, MPC/custody Turnkey/Fireblocks/Dfns) — each is a separate follow-up task once the behaviour lands.
EIP-712 / Hyperliquid 'phantom agent' and other Axis-B venue message builders — orthogonal (a message builder on top of `Cartouche.Typed`, not a signer backend); separate task.
Req/Goth-based dep-light rewrite of the GCP CloudKMS backend (dropping google_api_cloud_kms + google_gax) — separate task; the behaviour just makes it a drop-in second impl later.
Solana signer-family refactor is IN scope only if the Eth/Solana parallel structures would otherwise diverge; splitting Solana onto the behaviour can be a fast-follow if it balloons this task.
task.body:
Investigation thread (this session): the existing MFA dispatch in Cartouche.Application (`signer_mfa/1` / `solana_signer_mfa/1`) + `Cartouche.Signer`'s `apply(mod, :get_address, args)` / `apply(mod, :sign, [message | args])` is ALREADY a de-facto signer API — every backend exposes `get_address` + `sign`, called blindly. This task formalizes that implicit contract into a real `@behaviour` (compile-time `@impl` checks, docs, discoverability) and makes adding backends not require a new clause in the per-type dispatch.

TWO ORTHOGONAL AXES surfaced and must stay separated:
- Axis A (THIS task) — key custody / signer backend: WHERE the key lives, WHO computes the secp256k1/ed25519 signature. Local Curvy, GCP/AWS/Azure KMS, Vault, MPC all collapse to the same two callbacks. The only variance is auth, request shape, signature encoding (DER vs raw), and prehash-vs-raw.
- Axis B (separate tasks) — signing TARGET / message format: Ethereum tx, EIP-712 typed data, Hyperliquid phantom-agent action hash, Solana tx. These are message builders on top of Cartouche.Typed (lib/cartouche/typed.ex, already present), NOT signer backends.

THE ONE DESIGN DECISION THAT MATTERS (the payoff): make the backend a pure digest/payload signer. Today CloudKMS/Curvy keccak the message INTERNALLY — wrong for EIP-712/Hyperliquid where the caller already computed the typed-data hash. If the behaviour signs exactly the bytes handed to it (secp256k1 -> 32-byte digest; ed25519 -> raw message) and the caller owns hashing, then ONE backend set covers plain Eth tx + EIP-712 + Hyperliquid + Solana with zero per-venue backend touches. Bake hashing into the backend and every new venue forces a backend change.

CURVE-SUPPORT CONSTRAINT (verified this session via web research; sources in transcript): only GCP Cloud KMS signs BOTH curves natively (secp256k1 EC_SIGN_SECP256K1_SHA256 + ed25519 EC_SIGN_ED25519, Apr 2024). AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault do secp256k1 but NOT ed25519. HashiCorp Vault Transit does ed25519 natively but NOT secp256k1 (needs Kaleido vault-plugin-secrets-ethsign). MPC/custody (Turnkey/Fireblocks/Dfns/Fordefi) cover both but are higher-level/async. Implication: a multi-provider story is NOT 'swap Google for X' — it's pick-a-provider-per-curve. The behaviour must NOT assume one backend covers both chains.

IMPLEMENTATION GOTCHA to bake into the contract from the start (so backend tasks inherit it): AWS/Azure return DER-encoded ECDSA needing low-s canonicalization (EIP-2 malleability — the classic 'dark side of the elliptic curve' bug). The contract / a shared helper should normalize to low-s so each new secp256k1 backend does not re-solve it.

OPEN FORKS for the design phase (do not pre-decide here): (1) config back-compat — keep :priv_key/:cloud_kms shorthands + add module form, vs clean break to module-form-only; (2) Eth-only vs Eth+Solana scope; (3) which provider proves the extension point first — recommended AWS KMS (largest install base, smallest delta from GCP shape, forces DER/low-s handling into the contract early).

Touch points: lib/cartouche/signer.ex (sign_direct hashing, GenServer handle_call), lib/cartouche/signer/{curvy,cloud_kms}.ex, lib/cartouche/application.ex (signer_mfa dispatch / config parsing), and the Solana parallels if in scope. CloudKMS work => dialyzer verification stays LOCAL (cartouche PLT OOMs on cloud VMs — see CLAUDE.md). Critical-tier (signing) => >=95% coverage gate before mutating.
task.implemented: Shipped in 7c82cd8 (CHANGELOG 'Cartouche.Signer.Backend behaviour'). Three callbacks — algorithm/1, public_key/1, sign_payload/2 — NOT the get_address/sign names this task's acceptance criteria guessed at scoping time; the shipped names are the better ones and the criteria were never re-worded. Pure digest/payload contract: sign_payload/2 signs exactly the bytes handed to it, hashing moved into the caller (Cartouche.Signer), so one backend set serves Eth tx, EIP-712, Hyperliquid and Solana. Cartouche.Signer.{Curvy,CloudKMS} and Cartouche.Solana.Signer.{Ed25519,CloudKMS} all declare @behaviour + @impl. Address derivation, low-s canonicalization (new Recover.normalize_low_s/1) and recid recovery live caller-side so future secp256k1 backends inherit them. Config decision (a) non-breaking: :priv_key/:cloud_kms/:ed25519 shorthands kept, explicit {BackendModule, config} form additionally accepted (application.ex:57-97), proven end-to-end by test/signer_test.exs:39 '{backend, config} carrier (pure-payload path)'. Signer/recover modules at 100% coverage bar the unreachable find_recid guard. Three latent defects the audit recorded and deferred (32-byte payload guard, CloudKMS DER parse-wrap, unconsumed algorithm/1 curve guard) are carried forward as a separate task, not silently dropped.

task.title: Generator fixture: unlinked-library / immutable bytecode placeholders through blank_bytecode?/hex!
task.body:
solc/Foundry emit bytecode objects that are present but not valid hex: unlinked library references appear as __$<34-hex-keccak>$__ placeholders, and immutable references leave 0-filled gaps recorded in a separate map. Current generator input handling (blank_bytecode?/1 and hex!/1 in lib/mix/cartouche.gen.ex) is tested against absent / "0x" / whitespace-only bytecode, but not against malformed-but-present bytecode containing __$...$__ link markers. hex! on such a string would raise mid-generation rather than degrading to the no-bytecode (RPC-only) path or surfacing an actionable error.

Implement a fixture (inline ABI + a bytecode object carrying a __$...$__ placeholder) and assert the generator either (a) treats unlinked bytecode as blank and emits the RPC-only surface, or (b) raises a generator-specific error naming the unlinked library — decide which after checking what hex!/1 does today. This is a real-world edge: any contract that links an external library (common for math/string libs) ships this bytecode shape from Foundry's forge build. Adds a new input-validation branch, not redundant coverage.

task.title: Unblock tesla >= 1.18.3 — supply :max_body_size to the google_gax CloudKMS Tesla client
acceptance_criteria: The CloudKMS Tesla client passes :max_body_size to Tesla.Middleware.Compression (or Compression is configured/removed so it does not raise under tesla >= 1.18.3).
tesla pin in mix.exs lifted from `== 1.18.2` to allow >= 1.18.3 (target 1.20.0); mix.lock updated; the pin-rationale comment is updated or removed to reflect the fix.
Full cloud_kms_test suite is green against the bumped tesla (the 14 previously-failing tests pass).
Critical-tier coverage (>=95%) held on both CloudKMS signer modules; dialyzer run LOCALLY shows no new warnings on touched files.

Bumping any other transitive dep in the GCP cluster beyond what the tesla bump requires.
task.body:
tesla is pinned to EXACTLY 1.18.2 in mix.exs because tesla 1.18.3 made Tesla.Middleware.Compression require an explicit :max_body_size option (DoS hardening). The GCP CloudKMS signer cluster (google_api_cloud_kms -> google_gax, latest 0.4.1, abandoned since 2021) builds its Tesla client with the Compression middleware but WITHOUT :max_body_size, so any tesla bump to >= 1.18.3 raises on every CloudKMS signer call (14 cloud_kms_test failures, observed 2026-06). This blocks Dependabot PR #68 (tesla 1.18.2 -> 1.20.0), which carries five tesla security CVE fixes (CVE-2026-48594 decompression bomb, -48595 auth-header leak on cross-origin redirect, -48596 CRLF injection, -48597 atom exhaustion, -48598 multipart smuggling).

Make the Tesla client used for CloudKMS pass :max_body_size to the Compression middleware (or configure/strip Compression so it no longer raises), so the tesla pin can be lifted. google_gax won't fix this upstream — investigate how google_api_cloud_kms builds its Connection/Tesla client and whether cartouche can inject a custom client or middleware config at the signer boundary. Once the CloudKMS path tolerates tesla >= 1.18.3, bump tesla in mix.exs/mix.lock (replace the `== 1.18.2` pin), update the pin-rationale comment, and confirm the full cloud_kms_test suite is green.

This is the narrow unblock; the broader Req/Goth dep-light rewrite that drops google_api_cloud_kms + google_gax entirely is Task 104's out_of_scope follow-up — cross-reference, don't duplicate. CloudKMS work => dialyzer verification stays LOCAL (cartouche PLT OOMs on cloud VMs, see CLAUDE.md). Critical-tier (signing) => >=95% coverage gate before mutating.

task.title: Req/Goth dep-light CloudKMS backend — drop google_api_cloud_kms + google_gax + tesla, retire the tesla pin gymnastics
acceptance_criteria: Both KMS signer modules (Eth `Cartouche.Signer.CloudKMS` and the Solana parallel) sign and fetch public keys via Req + Goth, with identical external behaviour — existing doctests and cloud_kms_test pass unchanged.

`google_api_cloud_kms` and `google_gax` removed from mix.exs/mix.lock; `tesla` removed (or, if a kept dep still needs it, the `== 1.18.2` pin lifted to a normal range and the pin-rationale comment deleted).
Goth retained for token minting; confirmed it does not transitively force tesla (or that finding is documented).
The dialyzer `:plt_ignore_apps` GCP cluster in mix.exs is reduced to only what remains needed; CLAUDE.md / mix.exs pin-rationale comments updated to reflect the dropped deps.
Critical-tier (signing) >=95% coverage held on both CloudKMS signer modules; dialyzer run LOCALLY (cartouche PLT OOMs on cloud VMs) shows no new warnings on touched files.
CHANGELOG + `implemented` field document the dep removals and that Task 107's tesla pin is now moot (supersede 107 if this lands first).
out_of_scope: New non-GCP backends (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Vault Transit, MPC custody) — each is its own follow-up per Task 104's out_of_scope.
Changing the `Cartouche.Signer.Backend` contract — this is a drop-in second impl onto the existing behaviour, not a behaviour change.
Goth replacement — Goth stays; only the google_api_cloud_kms/google_gax/tesla cluster is dropped.
task.body:
Reimplement the GCP Cloud KMS signer backend(s) directly over Req + Goth, behind the existing `Cartouche.Signer.Backend` behaviour (formalized in Task 104), so we can drop `google_api_cloud_kms`, `google_gax`, and the `tesla` pin entirely — retiring all the tesla/Compression/:max_body_size/plt_ignore gymnastics in one move.

The named follow-up from Task 104's and Task 107's `out_of_scope`. The KMS call surface is tiny — two REST endpoints plus an auth token:
  - GET  cryptoKeyVersions:getPublicKey  → PEM-encoded public key (parse the same way the current impl does: `:public_key.pem_decode` → ECPoint)
  - POST cryptoKeyVersions:asymmetricSign  with body `{digest: {sha256: <base64>}}` → base64 signature (parse via `Curvy.Signature.parse`)
Both already implemented against `GoogleApi.CloudKMS.V1.Api.Projects` in `lib/cartouche/signer/cloud_kms.ex` and the Solana parallel — port them call-for-call onto `Req` (we already depend on `~> 0.6.2`).

Auth: KEEP `goth` (~> 1.4.5, well-maintained). It mints the bearer token; Req sends it. Only `google_api_cloud_kms` + `google_gax` + `tesla` get dropped from mix.exs. Verify Goth has no hard tesla dependency of its own before declaring tesla gone — if it does, that's a finding, not a silent workaround.

There is no lighter maintained Elixir GCP KMS library — `google_api_cloud_kms` (heavy autogenerated, depends on the abandoned `google_gax`, last release 0.4.1 in 2021) is the only one. Hand-rolling the two endpoints over Req is the dep-light path.

Payoff: removes two abandoned deps and RETIRES the tesla gymnastics — the `tesla == 1.18.2` pin, the `:max_body_size` Compression breakage, the pin-rationale comment, and the `:plt_ignore_apps` GCP cluster (google_api_cloud_kms/google_gax/tesla) in mix.exs all go away (the cluster shrinks toward just goth). That pin is the entire reason Task 107 exists.

Relationship to Task 107: 107 is the narrow tesla-unblock that KEEPS google_gax and merely patches around its broken Tesla client. This task is the structural fix that makes 107 unnecessary. If this lands first, supersede 107. If 107 lands first (quick CVE unblock), this still proceeds and removes the pin 107 patched around. Not a dependency either way — they are alternatives; do not chain them.

CloudKMS Eth+Solana signers rewritten over Req + Goth.fetch!; google_api_cloud_kms, google_gax, and the tesla==1.18.2 pin removed from mix.exs/mix.lock. plt_ignore_apps GCP cluster shrank to just :goth.
