task.title: Finish + normalize typed-transaction helper extraction (dedup maybe_to_wei/chain_id_value; migrate V3 onto TypedDecode/Signature)
acceptance_criteria: maybe_to_wei/1 and chain_id_value/1 are each defined once and called from V3/V4 — no surviving private copies
V3.decode routes through Cartouche.Transaction.TypedDecode (like V4 and V_2930 already do); V3's private safe_rlp_decode is removed
The binary-form add_signature/2 in V3 and V4 delegates to Cartouche.Transaction.Signature (single home for the packed r<>s<>v parsing)
encode/decode round-trip doctests + tests pass unchanged (byte-identical behavior); touched modules stay >=95% coverage
out_of_scope: RPC wrapper changes — Task 110
Any change to RLP field ordering or struct shapes
New macros — this is plain-function consolidation; the typed-tx macro question was settled by 97869ab choosing shared callback modules
task.body:
Commit 97869ab partially extracted shared typed-transaction helpers into Cartouche.Transaction.TypedDecode (envelope decode + safe_rlp_decode via a callback) and Cartouche.Transaction.Signature (add/get on the struct-as-map), but the migration is uneven and small clones survive. Finish and normalize it — plain functions throughout, NOT macros:

1. Dedup the still-duplicated `maybe_to_wei/1` (v3.ex + v4.ex) and `chain_id_value/1` (v3.ex) into shared plain functions — maybe_to_wei alongside Cartouche.Wei (it already wraps Wei.to_wei/1), chain_id_value with Cartouche.Chain (nil -> Cartouche.Application.chain_id(), else Cartouche.Chain.parse_id/1). These survive the `ex_dna --max-clones 0` gate only because each is a 2-line function below the clone-mass threshold; they are still real duplication.
2. Migrate V3.decode onto Cartouche.Transaction.TypedDecode the way V4 and V_2930 already are, removing V3's private safe_rlp_decode (lib/cartouche/transaction/v3.ex) so all three typed decoders share one envelope path.
3. Route the binary-form add_signature/2 through Cartouche.Transaction.Signature across V3 and V4 so the packed r<>s<>v parsing lives in one place.

The typed-transaction macro question (was Task 111) is settled — 97869ab deliberately chose shared callback modules over a `use`-macro, so this is consolidation, not a new abstraction. The remaining genuine macro opportunity is defrpc (Task 110), a different surface.

Pre-mutation gate: Cartouche.Transaction* is critical-tier (signing-adjacent, >=95% coverage). Confirm/raise coverage on the touched modules BEFORE refactoring.
task.implemented: Landed by cursor via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1782293704724-7735ab31, 3e681e4e07bb3b04a1f70ce0cff1ca85aefe53b4).

task.title: defrpc macro — generate uniform JSON-RPC wrappers + @spec + @doc + Descripex api() from one declaration
acceptance_criteria: `defrpc` macro defined with a @moduledoc/@doc explaining the declaration shape
Each generated wrapper emits an equivalent @spec, @doc, and Descripex api() block — Cartouche.describe output for converted methods is unchanged
The uniform subset in Cartouche.RPC and Cartouche.Solana.RPC is converted; compiled behavior is byte-identical (existing doctests + tests pass unchanged)
Irregular wrappers (guards, struct dispatch, multi-clause) are left hand-written and listed in the PR description
Both RPC modules stay at >=95% line coverage
out_of_scope: Transaction-variant modules (Tasks 109/111)
Changing send_rpc/3 itself or the decode option semantics
Converting irregular/guarded wrappers into the macro
task.body:
Cartouche.RPC (~2250 LOC) and Cartouche.Solana.RPC (~1170 LOC) repeat one wrapper shape ~50 times: a hand-written Descripex `api(...)` annotation, a `@doc`, a `@spec`, and a thin body that hex-encodes arguments, optionally normalizes a block selector, and calls `send_rpc(method, params, decode: <type>)`. The account-at-block trio — get_balance / get_code / get_transaction_count — is byte-for-byte identical except for the RPC method string and the decode type. Keeping the four artifacts (body, spec, doc, api metadata) in sync by hand is the cost this removes.

Introduce a `defrpc` macro that generates all four from a single declaration. The macro MUST emit the Descripex `api()` block, not replace or bypass it — agent introspection (Cartouche.describe/*, __descripex_modules__/0) must see identical metadata for converted methods. Apply `defrpc` only to the genuinely uniform subset of wrappers in both RPC modules. Leave the irregular methods hand-written — those with binary/address guards, struct dispatch (send_trx, to_call_params, simulate/send_transaction), or multi-clause normalization. A defrpc that tries to swallow the irregular ones would grow more knobs than the duplication it removes.

Keep the macro thin and readable — these wrappers are read often, and macro-generated bodies obscure stack traces; the mitigation is a dumb, declarative macro, not a clever one. Precedent: exth_rpc / ethers-style libs generate RPC wrappers, so this is not novel complexity.

Pre-mutation gate: both RPC modules are critical-tier (signing-adjacent transport, >=95% coverage). Confirm/raise coverage before converting.
task.implemented: Shipped 3b8f27b. Added Cartouche.RPC.DSL with defrpc/3 generating wrapper + @spec + @doc + Descripex api() from one declaration; two uniform shapes (address-at-block, no-arg). Converted 7 ETH wrappers: get_code/get_balance/get_transaction_count (address-at-block) + eth_chain_id/eth_block_number/gas_price/max_priority_fee_per_gas (no-arg). __api__ introspection proven byte-identical for all 7 (mix-run baseline diff), 82 rpc tests + doctests green. Boundary cases left hand-written and documented: get_nonce (param name 'account', :big_hex encoder, AND a different opts description — 3 deviations); Cartouche.Solana.RPC out of scope — its send_rpc has no :decode contract and wrappers post-process via with-pipelines/params_with_config/commitment configs, so no fitting uniform subset. Doctor's defmacro/def-unquote blind spot handled via existing ignore_modules precedent. verified unset: hand-built, self-verified (introspection diff + hooks), no separate reviewer.

task.title: Spike: evaluate a Cartouche.Transaction.Typed envelope macro across V_2930/V3/V4
acceptance_criteria: Written recommendation (implement | reject) with the LOC-saved-vs-indirection-cost math, recorded in `implemented`
Prototype exists against V3 + V4 (branch or inline) demonstrating the measurement
If implemented: V_2930/V3/V4 use the macro, behavior byte-identical, coverage >=95%; if rejected: the reasoning is durable enough to prevent re-proposal
out_of_scope: Re-implementing the wei/chain-id helpers — Task 109 owns those; the macro calls them
RPC wrappers (Task 110)
Touching legacy V1/V2 (non-typed, no 0x envelope byte)
task.body:
SPIKE (bounded investigation + prototype, deliver a recommendation). V_2930, V3, and V4 share an EIP-2718 envelope shape: encode = `<<@tx_type>> <> ExRLP.encode(rlp_payload)`, `hash/1` (keccak of the encoded bytes), the binary-form `add_signature/2`, and `safe_rlp_decode/1`. Evaluate whether a `use Cartouche.Transaction.Typed, type: 0xNN` macro that injects those shared envelope methods nets more than it costs — the per-variant field sets and RLP payload ordering vary a lot, so the FIXED part being factored out may be small.

Prototype the macro against V3 and V4 only. Measure LOC actually removed vs the indirection and stack-trace cost added. Deliver a clear implement-or-reject recommendation recorded in the task's `implemented` field. If implement: land it across V_2930/V3/V4. If reject: document the LOC/indirection math that killed it so a future session does not re-propose it.

The macro must CALL the shared maybe_to_wei/chain_id_value helpers from Task 109, never re-inject them. Critical-tier (signing) — keep coverage >=95% on any code that actually lands.

SUPERSEDED 2026-06-24: commit 97869ab landed the EIP-2718 envelope sharing as plain callback modules — Cartouche.Transaction.TypedDecode (decode + safe_rlp_decode via a `decode_fields` callback) and Cartouche.Transaction.Signature (add/get on struct-as-map) — explicitly choosing function extraction over a `use`-macro ("so they work uniformly across the typed-transaction modules without coupling them to one another"). That answers this spike's macro-vs-not question: function extraction captured the win, and the per-variant residue (field sets, rlp_payload ordering) is exactly the part a macro could not factor out. The remaining real macro opportunity is defrpc (Task 110); the residual extraction cleanup (uneven V3 migration) folded into the reframed Task 109.

task.title: Finish typed-tx Signature extraction: migrate V4.get_signature onto Signature.get/1
acceptance_criteria: V4.get_signature/1 delegates to Cartouche.Transaction.Signature.get/1

V4.get_authorization_signature/1 stops hand-rolling the same nil-guard + packed assembly — extract a shared primitive (e.g. Signature.pack/3) that both the struct path and the EIP-7702 authorization 6-tuple call, since Signature.get/1 pattern-matches struct keys and cannot take a tuple

After this task no hand-rolled signature nil-guard or `r <> s <> y_parity` assembly remains under lib/cartouche/transaction/ outside Cartouche.Transaction.Signature — verify by grep; the legacy V1 integer-v path at transaction.ex:310 is explicitly excluded

The r/s length tightening is deliberate and tested: Signature.get/1 constructs with binary-size(32) where V4 concatenated unbounded, so a struct carrying a short r or s now raises instead of emitting a malformed packed signature — assert the 32-byte path stays byte-identical AND add a test pinning the new rejection
Existing V4 transaction tests (sign to encode to decode to recover round-trip) and the EIP-7702 authorization round-trip stay green
out_of_scope: V2/V1 legacy signature paths
any change to the packed signature wire format
task.body:
Task 109 extracted the shared signature-field helpers into `Cartouche.Transaction.Signature` and migrated V3 (`get_signature/1` now delegates to `Signature.get/1`), but left `Cartouche.Transaction.V4.get_signature/1` hand-rolled — it still duplicates the exact nil-guard error clause and the packed `r <> s <> y_parity` assembly that `Signature.get/1` now owns. This is the residual half of the "uneven extraction" the dedup task set out to finish.

Migrate `V4.get_signature/1` to delegate to `Cartouche.Transaction.Signature.get/1` (as V3 already does), confirming the recovery-byte encoding stays byte-identical (`<<y_parity_integer(v)>>` vs `Signature.get`'s `:binary.encode_unsigned/1` form — both emit `<<0>>`/`<<1>>`). Keep V4's existing tests green; the round-trip sign/encode/decode/recover path is the equivalence check.

SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-22 (roadmap review). Two corrections, both to criteria that the task as originally scoped could not have met:

1. There are TWO hand-rolled sites in v4.ex, not one. `get_signature/1` (v4.ex:220) is the struct path and is straight delegation. `get_authorization_signature/1` (v4.ex:281) handles the EIP-7702 authorization tuple `{chain_id, address, nonce, v, r, s}` and duplicates the identical nil-guard and `r <> s <> <<y_parity_integer(v)>>` assembly. `Signature.get/1` matches on `%{signature_y_parity:, signature_r:, signature_s:}` keys and cannot serve a 6-tuple, so closing this site needs a shared primitive both call. The old criterion "no remaining duplication across V3 and V4" would still have been false on delivery.

2. This is NOT a pure no-op. `Signature.get/1` builds with `<<r::binary-size(32), s::binary-size(32), v_enc::binary>>`; V4 concatenates with an unbounded `r <> s <> ...`. Every current producer pads to 32 bytes (`decode_word/1` -> `Hex.pad(word, 32)` at v4.ex:564; `add_signature/2` matches `binary-size(32)` at v4.ex:257), so live behaviour is unchanged — but a directly-constructed struct carrying a short `r`/`s` goes from silently emitting a malformed packed signature to raising. That is desirable hardening; pin it with a test rather than describing the task as behaviour-preserving.
task.implemented: V4.get_signature/1 now delegates to Cartouche.Transaction.Signature.get/1, and get_authorization_signature/1 uses the new shared Signature.pack/3 (nil-guard + 32-byte r/s <> y_parity) so the EIP-7702 authorization 6-tuple no longer hand-rolls the packing. Grep of lib/cartouche/transaction/ confirms no packed-signature assembly remains outside Signature; the surviving is_nil guards are RLP unsigned-preimage omission, not recovery packing. V1's integer-v path at transaction.ex:310 left untouched per scope. 32-byte packing verified byte-identical; short r/s now raises and is pinned by a test. Signature at 100% coverage.

task.title: Property + cross-implementation vector suite for Ethereum tx envelopes and signing
acceptance_criteria: `stream_data` added as a test-only dependency (mix.exs + mix.lock committed)

Property tests cover every ENCODABLE envelope — V1 (legacy/EIP-155), V_2930 (EIP-2930), V2 (EIP-1559), V3 (EIP-4844), V4 (EIP-7702) — asserting encode/decode round-trip identity, sign to recover_signer identity, and boundary-sized fields (zero, one, 2^256-1, empty data, empty and maximal access lists, 32-byte r/s). V_2930 gained its full write surface in task 115 (landed 82a990d) and is now in scope on equal footing with the others

Chain-id / domain separation is a property, not an example: a payload signed for chain A must not recover the signing address when re-checked under chain B, and the EIP-155 v-encoding is asserted against the EIP formula rather than a recorded constant

Low-s (EIP-2) is asserted as a property, not per backend: for every signing route that emits a 65-byte signature, the packed s is at most n/2 over generated inputs, including a backend forced to return high-s. Task 118 (landed 51b971c) made this a library-wide invariant behind one emission funnel, so a red property here means 118 regressed

Golden vectors live under test/fixtures/vectors/ as committed files, each carrying inline provenance: source implementation, its exact version, and the command that generated it. The EIP text is the authority for semantics; vectors from at least two independently maintained implementations are required ONLY where an EIP leaves edge behaviour implicit — where the EIP is explicit, cite the EIP and one vector suffices
A short docs/verification-ledger.md records, for this task: which EIPs were treated as authoritative, every vector's provenance, and the toolchain versions used to generate them
Touched critical modules (lib/cartouche/transaction*, lib/cartouche/signer*, lib/cartouche/recover.ex) are at >=95% coverage and `mix ci` passes
out_of_scope: The mutation-adequacy campaign, the deliberate-fault canary and the survivor ledger — those are the follow-up task that depends on this one

Fixing any conformance defect the properties surface — task 117 closes the known encode/decode asymmetries (V2 bare-address access list, V4 empty authorization_list, V3 blob-hash emptiness and version prefix) and this task depends on it, so a red round-trip property here means 117 regressed, not that the property should be weakened
Solana signing and transaction paths
Any change to public API signatures — this task only adds tests, fixtures and a test-only dep
task.body:
Establish the evidence base that cartouche's signing and transaction encoding are correct against the specs rather than merely self-consistent. Two instruments: properties that must hold across generated inputs, and golden vectors produced by implementations outside this codebase.

The authority order is the one this repo already follows: the EIP text first (EIP-155 chain-id replay protection, EIP-2718 typed envelopes, EIP-1559, EIP-4844, EIP-7702, EIP-2 low-s), then independently generated vectors where an EIP leaves edge behaviour implicit. Third-party clients are compatibility evidence, never semantics. Where a vector and the EIP disagree, record the discrepancy — do not pick a reading.

Why vectors from outside cartouche matter here specifically: the existing suite computes expectations with the same code it is testing, so a wrong constant or a wrong field order would be ratified by its own golden values. An externally generated vector is the only artifact in the suite that cannot share that mistake.

SPLIT NOTE 2026-08-22 (roadmap review): this was one oversized task also carrying a mutation campaign, a fault canary and a survivor ledger — five criteria, each a session's work, with no mutation tool named. It is now the first half; the mutation-adequacy half is a separate task that depends on this one, because it measures the suite this task builds.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787387047478-02622bc7, 6c8acb20b15fcda238473c5b9c5fed31edcfd2be).

task.title: Mutation-adequacy campaign over the signing and transaction paths
acceptance_criteria: The campaign runs on `muex` (hex, actively maintained in 2026, 18 mutators). Do NOT reach for `muzak`: its last release is 1.1.1 from Dec 2022 and the free tier caps each run at 25 randomly chosen mutations, which cannot satisfy a reproducible, exhaustive campaign. If muex proves unworkable on this codebase, say so with the concrete failure and stop — do not silently fall back to a capped tool

The mutated surface is enumerated explicitly: lib/cartouche/transaction.ex, lib/cartouche/transaction/*, lib/cartouche/signer.ex, lib/cartouche/signer/*, lib/cartouche/recover.ex, lib/cartouche/recovery_bit.ex. Mutations target RLP field order and arity, EIP-2718 type bytes, chain-id handling, v / y-parity encoding, low-s normalization, hash-domain selection and signer dispatch

Every survivor is triaged and dispositioned in writing as one of: killed by a new test added in this task, provably equivalent (with the argument), or an accepted gap (with the reason). No survivor is left unclassified

A deliberate-fault canary proves the harness detects real faults: at minimum a wrong-chain-id mutant and a skipped-low-s-normalization mutant. Each must be killed by the suite; if either survives, the run fails and the gap is closed before the task is done
docs/verification-ledger.md is extended with the campaign record: muex version, mutator set, mutation and survivor counts per module, and each survivor's disposition
Touched critical modules stay at >=95% coverage and `mix ci` passes
out_of_scope: Building the property suite and golden vectors — that is task 113, which this depends on
Solana signing and transaction paths
Mutating the generated contract wrappers under lib/cartouche/contract/ — machine-generated, fix the generator instead
Adopting mutation testing as a permanent CI gate; this is a one-off measurement plus the tests it produces
task.body:
Measure whether the signing and transaction suite detects plausible semantic faults, rather than merely executing the lines. Line coverage says the code ran; mutation adequacy says a wrong answer would have been caught. This is the check that catches the failure mode where a test's expected value was computed with the same wrong constant as the code.

Run only after task 113 lands: mutating a suite that has no external vectors measures self-consistency, and the survivors would be uninformative.

The deliverable is not the mutation score. It is (a) the tests written to kill genuine survivors and (b) a written disposition for every survivor that was not killed. A campaign that reports a number and closes has produced nothing durable.

TOOLING DECISION 2026-08-22 (roadmap review): `muex` is named deliberately. The obvious reach is `muzak`, which is stale (1.1.1, Dec 2022) and whose free tier samples 25 random mutations per run — reproducibility and exhaustiveness are both impossible under it, so a campaign built on it would satisfy the letter of this task and none of its intent.
task.implemented: Campaign ran (muex 0.8.2, 4905 mutants, 13 files, 98 min) but its central deliverable — the survivor triage — has no input: muex cannot report a surviving mutant on Elixir 1.20, so a mutant no test notices is reported as killed and the score is a constant 100%. Closed under AC1's own clause for an unworkable tool, with the concrete failure recorded rather than papered over. Verified against a four-file reproduction outside the repo and filed as Oeditus/muex#20 with a patch; task 119 re-runs the measurement once a release reports survivors. What the run did establish, and what landed: the no_coverage class (unaffected — decided from the coverage index before any test runs) found 55 mutants on lines no test reached, traced to six sites; five are now covered by new tests (test/cartouche/transaction/mutation_gap_test.exs, test/recovery_bit_test.exs) and the sixth, v4.ex:574 decode_y_parity(nil), is dispositioned as an unreachable dead clause. A verification pass over the three affected files confirms 55 -> 3, all at that clause. Deliberate-fault canaries (test/cartouche/mutation_canary_test.exs, 9 tests) pin which invariant catches each of three hand-built faults and which plausible one does not. docs/verification-ledger.md carries the full record. mix ci green; RecoveryBit 100%, V3 100%, V4 98.98% coverage.

task.title: Cartouche.Transaction.V_2930 write surface — new/encode/sign/hash/signature/recover
acceptance_criteria: V_2930 gains new/…, encode/1, sign/2, hash/1, add_signature/4, add_signature/2 (packed), get_signature/1 and recover_signer/1, mirroring the shapes V3 already uses at v3.ex:94/133/200/212/218/224/230/236

encode/1 emits `0x01 || rlp([chainId, nonce, gasPrice, gasLimit, to, value, data, accessList, yParity, r, s])` per EIP-2930 — verify the field order against the EIP text, not against the existing decode_fields/1, so a pre-existing order error cannot be copied forward
Cartouche.Transaction.encode/1 gains a %V_2930{} clause (transaction.ex:1509-1512 currently has V1/V2/V3/V4 only, so a hand-built type-1 struct raises FunctionClauseError at the dispatcher)
The signature helpers are delegation to Cartouche.Transaction.Signature, not re-implementation — Signature is already struct-agnostic and V_2930 carries the same signature_y_parity/r/s keys

New describe blocks in test/transaction_test.exs mirroring V3's: encode/decode round-trip, sign then recover_signer identity, both add_signature arities, and the missing-signature error path. Module at >=95% coverage (signing-adjacent, critical tier); mix ci passes
out_of_scope: build_trx_v_2930 / build_signed_trx_v_2930 convenience wrappers — V3 and V4 have no equivalent either, so adding them only for V_2930 creates new asymmetry rather than parity
The Typed-envelope macro (task 111, superseded — and its premise that V_2930 already shared encode/hash/add_signature was factually wrong)
Any downstream repo change: nothing in onchain / onchain_aave / onchain_evm / onchain_tempo references V_2930 today
task.body:
Cartouche.Transaction.V_2930 (EIP-2930, type 0x01) is decode-only. It has decode/1 (v_2930.ex:47), from_json/1 (v_2930.ex:53) and private field decoders — and nothing else. A caller cannot construct, encode, sign, hash or recover a type-1 transaction by any route in this library: verified by enumerating every V_2930 reference in lib/ (the dispatcher's decode/1 clause at transaction.ex:1564, the block-JSON dispatch at block.ex:402, and the module itself), and by the absence of a %V_2930{} clause in the encode dispatcher at transaction.ex:1509-1512.

The omission is historical, not a decision. Task 99 (done 2026-06-05, cf9e2d3) introduced the module for one purpose — stop the block deserializer crashing on type-1 transactions — and its body scoped exactly that. No task or CHANGELOG entry anywhere argues the write side should be withheld; CHANGELOG.md:98 notes "V_2930 is decode-only" only as a factual aside.

Most of the work is delegation. Cartouche.Transaction.Signature and TypedDecode are already struct-agnostic (they match on map keys, not module), so the four signature functions are the same one-liners V3 uses. The genuinely new code is encode/1 (single gas_price field instead of the two EIP-1559 fee fields, no blob fields), sign/2, hash/1, new/… and the dispatcher clause — roughly the same increment V3 needed over the shared helpers.

Honest demand note: nothing downstream consumes this today — onchain, onchain_aave, onchain_evm and onchain_tempo reference V_2930 zero times, and every access_list hit in those repos is EIP-1559 or Tempo plumbing. Score it as completeness of a public transaction-type surface in a general-purpose library, which is what it is. Do not inflate it with a usage claim.
task.implemented: V_2930 gained new/8, encode/1, sign/2, hash/1, add_signature/4, add_signature/2, get_signature/1 and recover_signer/1, all signature helpers delegating to Cartouche.Transaction.Signature. encode/1 emits 0x01 || rlp([chainId, nonce, gasPrice, gasLimit, to, value, data, accessList, yParity, r, s]) with the field order checked against the EIP-2930 text rather than the existing decoder; a mainnet type-1 vector round-trips encode == raw. Cartouche.Transaction.encode/1 now dispatches %V_2930{}, so a hand-built type-1 struct no longer raises FunctionClauseError. Reviewer additionally aligned the descripex api(:encode) metadata, which still listed only V1/V2/V3/V4 (f53c888). V_2930 at 100% coverage.

task.title: Enforce the Signer.Backend contract at the boundary — payload length, curve, DER parse
acceptance_criteria: secp256k1 sign_payload/2 rejects a non-32-byte payload instead of signing it: the guard in Cartouche.Signer.Curvy and Cartouche.Signer.CloudKMS is tightened from is_binary/1 to an explicit 32-byte match, with a test asserting the rejection for both a short and an over-long payload

The algorithm/1 callback is either consumed or removed — no third option. If consumed: Cartouche.Signer and Cartouche.Solana.Signer validate the backend's curve before dispatching, so an ed25519 backend under the Eth signer (or Curvy under the Solana signer) fails loudly with a clear error rather than mis-signing; tests cover both mismatch directions. If removed: the callback and all four @impl definitions go, and the reason is recorded

Cartouche.Signer.CloudKMS no longer wraps a possibly-non-struct in {:ok, Curvy.Signature.parse(decoded_sig)} (cloud_kms.ex:88): a parse failure returns an error tuple rather than producing a term that makes Recover.normalize_low_s/1 raise FunctionClauseError, with a test over malformed DER input
The three fixes ship together in one diff — they are the same contract-boundary surface and one reviewer verifies them as one change
Both signer module families stay at >=95% coverage; dialyzer runs LOCALLY (KMS PLT rule) with no new warnings on touched files; mix ci passes
out_of_scope: New backend implementations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Vault Transit, MPC/custody) — each is its own task once the contract is enforced
Changing the pure-payload contract itself or moving hashing back into backends — that decision is settled by task 104
EIP-712 / Hyperliquid message builders (Axis B)
task.body:
Task 104 formalized Cartouche.Signer.Backend and landed clean, but its dual-reviewer audit (.audit/7c82cd8-task-104-formalize-signer.md, 2026-06-24) recorded three defects it deliberately did not fix, on the grounds that hardening critical signing code belonged to the warm implementer rather than an audit pass. Task 104 then closed. This task carries those three forward so they are not lost with it.

1. Findings 2 (pri 3, verified latent) — the secp256k1 sign_payload/2 guard is only is_binary/1. The behaviour's freshly-documented contract says the argument IS the 32-byte digest, but a caller passing anything else gets it signed as garbage rather than rejected. No live trigger today: every caller passes keccak(message). It is a footgun against a contract that now exists in writing, and it is the kind of thing a future backend author trips over.

2. Finding 4 (discuss-design, Claude and Codex agreed) — algorithm/1 is declared by the behaviour and implemented by all four backends, and consumed by nobody. There is no curve-mismatch guard: an ed25519 backend configured under the Eth signer, or Curvy under the Solana signer, mis-dispatches instead of failing. An unconsumed callback is either a missing guard or dead weight; decide which and act, do not leave it declared-and-ignored.

3. Finding 3 (pri 4, verified latent) — cloud_kms.ex:88 wraps Curvy.Signature.parse/1 output in {:ok, ...} without checking it is a %Curvy.Signature{}; a malformed DER response then reaches Recover.normalize_low_s/1 and raises FunctionClauseError instead of returning an error. KMS-path only and pre-existing, but low-s normalization is exactly where a malleability bug hides.

They are grouped as one task because they are one surface — the backend contract boundary — touching the same four modules, and a reviewer verifies them in a single pass. Splitting them would pay three dispatch cycles for one coherent diff.
task.implemented: All three contract-boundary defects carried forward from task 104's audit shipped in one diff: secp256k1 sign_payload/2 now matches an exact 32 bytes in both Curvy and CloudKMS instead of is_binary/1; algorithm/1 is CONSUMED (not removed) via a shared pre-dispatch curve check in both the Eth and Solana signer families, so a cross-curve backend fails loudly instead of mis-signing; and CloudKMS maps a Curvy.Signature.parse/1 failure to {:error, :invalid_signature} before low-s normalization instead of wrapping a non-struct that made Recover.normalize_low_s/1 raise. Tests cover both invalid payload lengths, both curve-mismatch directions, and malformed DER. 100% coverage on every Cartouche.Signer and Cartouche.Solana.Signer module; dialyzer clean.

task.title: Encode must not emit wire-non-conformant RLP — close the encode/decode conformance gap across V2/V3/V4
acceptance_criteria: The invariant is stated once and enforced for every encodable envelope: anything `encode/1` accepts must produce RLP that this library's own `decode/1` reads back to an equal struct, and that matches the EIP's wire shape. Verify the shape against the EIP text (EIP-2930 access-list item is `[address, storage_keys]`; EIP-7702 forbids an empty `authorization_list`; EIP-4844 requires a non-empty `blob_versioned_hashes` whose entries begin with VERSIONED_HASH_VERSION_KZG 0x01), not against the existing encoders

V2's bare-address access-list shorthand no longer produces a raw 20-byte RLP item: `normalize_access_list/1` (lib/cartouche/transaction.ex:843) either rejects a bare address or lifts it to `[address, []]`. Whichever is chosen, the choice is recorded in the CHANGELOG as a behaviour change and `V2.t()`'s declared `access_list` type (transaction.ex:473) and the private spec agree with the runtime

The seven doctests that currently pin the non-conformant bytes are corrected, not deleted: transaction.ex:735-738, :745-748, and the `build_trx_v2`/`build_signed_trx_v2` examples at :1718 and :1736. Each corrected expected value is justified by hand-decoding the RLP, and the corrected V2 hex round-trips through `V2.decode/1`

A round-trip test per envelope asserts `decode(encode(tx)) == {:ok, tx}` over the previously-broken inputs: a V2 access list containing a bare address, a V4 with `authorization_list: []`, a V3 with an empty `blob_versioned_hashes` and a V3 whose blob hash lacks the 0x01 prefix. Each currently fails; each must pass or be rejected at encode with a named error

Encode-side validation and decode-side validation are symmetric: no envelope rejects on decode a value it silently accepted on encode. Verified by enumerating the decode-side guards (v3.ex:398-407, v4.ex:533) and pointing at the matching encode-side guard
Touched modules stay at >=95% coverage (transaction encoding is critical tier) and `mix ci` passes
out_of_scope: V_2930's write surface — that is task 115, which this depends on; if 115 has landed, its encoder must satisfy the same invariant and is in scope only for that check
The property-test and golden-vector suite — task 113 consumes this invariant, it does not establish it
Any change to the RLP codec itself or to `Cartouche.Hex`
Solana transaction paths
task.body:
`Cartouche.Transaction.V2.encode/1` can emit an access list that no conformant Ethereum node will accept, and the library's own decoder cannot read back.

Verified by reading the code, not inferred. `normalize_access_list/1` (lib/cartouche/transaction.ex:843-849) carries a `bare_address when is_binary(bare_address) -> bare_address` clause that passes a raw 20-byte address straight through as an RLP string item, where EIP-2930 requires each access-list entry to be a two-element `[address, storage_keys]` list. `V2.decode_access_list/1` (:1021-1035) pattern-matches only `[address, storage]`, so the bare-address entry raises FunctionClauseError into the rescue clause and decode returns `{:error, "invalid v2 transaction"}`. `V2.t()` declares `access_list: [{<<_::160>>, [<<_::256>>]}]` (:473) — tuples only — so the struct type, the encoder and the decoder disagree three ways. V3 (v3.ex:337-340) and V4 (v4.ex:371-374) accept only the tuple form, so this is V2-specific drift.

The shorthand is not an accident that nobody exercises: five module doctests pin its output as correct (transaction.ex:735-738, :745-748) and the `build_trx_v2` / `build_signed_trx_v2` convenience-builder doctests (:1718, :1736) use it too. Hand-decoding the pinned hex at :738 confirms the defect — `...EA 94<20 bytes> 94<20 bytes>` is a list of two 20-byte strings, not a list of two sublists. So the documented happy path of the library builds transactions with a malformed access list.

Scope this as the class invariant, not as the one patch. The same encode-permits / decode-rejects asymmetry appears twice more on the same surface, and fixing only V2 leaves the next instance free to spawn a sibling task:
- V4 `authorization_list: []` — EIP-7702 declares such a transaction invalid; `decode_authorization_list/1` (v4.ex:533) rejects it, but `V4.new/10` and `encode_authorization_list/1` (v4.ex:377) accept it silently.
- V3 `blob_versioned_hashes` — EIP-4844 requires a non-empty list whose entries carry the 0x01 KZG version prefix; decode enforces the prefix (v3.ex:398-407) but the `Enum.all?` is vacuously true on `[]`, and encode (v3.ex:337-340) checks neither.

Authority is the EIP text, per this repo's standing rule: verify the wire shape against EIP-2930 / EIP-4844 / EIP-7702 directly, never against the current encoders, so a copied-forward error cannot be ratified.

Dispatch trigger: this is transaction-encoding code on the money path and the fix changes a documented public input shape.

Discovered 2026-08-22 by an orchestrator conformance sweep that read every envelope's RLP field order against the fetched EIP texts. That sweep found the base field orders of V1/V2/V3/V4 correct and the EIP-155 v-formula computed rather than hard-coded — the access-list and list-emptiness asymmetries above are the only conformance defects it surfaced.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787384096316-ad114146, 710868e80fcdb0dc560febd4bedfd35e30a170ff).

task.title: Low-s is a library-wide invariant, not a per-backend convention — close the sign_direct/4 bypass
acceptance_criteria: Every path that produces a 65-byte Ethereum signature normalizes low-s per EIP-2, with no path relying on the backend to have done it. Verified by enumerating the signature-producing functions in lib/cartouche/signer.ex and pointing at the `Cartouche.Recover.normalize_low_s/1` call each one passes through

`Cartouche.Signer.sign_direct/4` (signer.ex:222-229) specifically no longer emits an unnormalized signature: a test stubs a signing MFA that returns a deliberately high-s `Curvy.Signature` and asserts the resulting packed signature carries `s <= secp256k1n/2`. This test must fail against the current code — confirm that before fixing

The legacy `{module, function, args}` signer carrier is either kept with the invariant enforced, or retired outright — no third option. If retired: the `sign_direct/4` public function, the legacy clause of `backend_sign/4` (signer.ex:269-271), the legacy arm of `start_link/1`'s spec (signer.ex:61) and `Cartouche.Signer.CloudKMS.sign/7` (cloud_kms.ex:98-102) all go, the CHANGELOG records the removal, and the downstream call site named in the body is migrated in its own repo's task. If kept: the reason is recorded and the invariant holds on it
`Cartouche.Signer.CloudKMS.sign/7` no longer returns a DER-parsed signature with no low-s normalization while presenting the same shape as a signing entry point
Both signer module families stay at >=95% coverage; dialyzer runs LOCALLY per the KMS PLT rule with no new warnings on touched files; `mix ci` passes
out_of_scope: The three fixes task 116 carries (32-byte payload guard, `algorithm/1` consume-or-remove, CloudKMS DER parse) — this task depends on 116 and must not re-do them
New backend implementations
Changing the pure-payload contract settled by task 104
Editing the downstream `onchain` repo — that is a task in onchain's own roadmap once this lands
task.body:
The library guarantees low-s signatures on one signing path and not the other, and the unguarded one is the path a downstream repo actually uses in production.

Verified by reading the code, not inferred. `Cartouche.Signer.backend_sign/4`'s pure-payload clause (lib/cartouche/signer.ex:259-267) calls `Cartouche.Recover.normalize_low_s/1` on the raw backend signature before searching the recid. `Cartouche.Signer.sign_direct/4` (:222-229) — the legacy `{module, function, args}` path — takes whatever the MFA returns and goes straight to `find_recid/3` and `encode_eip155/3` with no normalization. `sign_direct/4` is public, Descripex-`api()`-annotated, and also reachable via `start_link/1` when handed a raw 3-tuple, because `backend_sign/4`'s second clause (:269-271) forwards to it.

This is not a latent-only gap. `onchain/lib/onchain/signer.ex:211` signs every transaction through `Cartouche.Signer.sign_direct/4`, and that module's own moduledoc names it as the signing route. It currently produces low-s signatures only by accident of its backend: it passes `{Cartouche.Signer.Curvy, :sign, [key_bin]}`, whose `sign_payload/2` (signer/curvy.ex:74-81) calls `Curvy.sign(digest, priv_key, hash: :keccak)` without a `normalize:` option, and the curvy 0.3.1 dependency defaults `:normalize` to `true` (confirmed in deps/curvy/lib/curvy.ex, `sign/3` docs). Change that dep default, or plug in any backend that does not normalize internally, and the library silently starts emitting malleable signatures.

`Cartouche.Signer.CloudKMS.sign/7` (cloud_kms.ex:98-102) is exactly that backend. It is legacy-MFA-shaped, returns a DER-parsed `Curvy.Signature` with no normalization, and cloud KMS providers give no low-s guarantee — the case `Cartouche.Signer.Backend`'s own moduledoc (backend.ex:33-36) and `Cartouche.Recover`'s comment (recover.ex:138-141) both warn about. Wired into `sign_direct/4` as its shape invites, it produces malleable signatures today.

Scope this as the invariant, not as a one-line patch, so the next non-normalizing backend cannot reopen it: state once that this library never emits a signature with `s > n/2`, and make the code structurally enforce it rather than delegating the guarantee to whichever backend happens to be configured. The legacy MFA carrier is the thing that makes the invariant unenforceable, so decide its fate as part of this — the library is pre-1.0 (0.7.1) and `Cartouche.Signer.Backend` was formalized in task 104 precisely to replace it.

Discovered 2026-08-22 by an orchestrator conformance sweep of the signing surface. The same sweep confirmed the EIP-155 v-formula is computed rather than hard-coded (signer.ex:277-283), that the y_parity translation is convention-invariant, and that recovery correctly does not require low-s — this bypass is the only malleability gap it found.

task.title: Re-run the mutation-adequacy campaign once muex can report survivors
acceptance_criteria: The installed muex passes a per-defect gate before a campaign is started, each result recorded in the ledger with the muex version: Oeditus/muex#20 (survivor reporting) — the #20 reproduction reports survived=2 and score 0%; Oeditus/muex#23 (shared _build) — a sandbox's _build/<env>/lib/<app> is a real directory, not a symlink into the project build, in a project with dependencies; Oeditus/muex#24 (line-keyed mutation matching) — a StatementDeletion and a bare-boolean mutant both reach the sandbox as modified source. Every one of them must pass; #20 alone is not the gate

The campaign re-runs over the surface task 114 enumerated (lib/cartouche/transaction.ex, lib/cartouche/transaction/*, lib/cartouche/signer.ex, lib/cartouche/signer/*, lib/cartouche/recover.ex, lib/cartouche/recovery_bit.ex) with the same flags, so the run is comparable to the recorded baseline

Every survivor is triaged and dispositioned in writing as one of: killed by a new test added in this task, provably equivalent (with the argument), or an accepted gap (with the reason). No survivor is left unclassified
docs/verification-ledger.md replaces the task 114 'measurement blocked' record with the real campaign record: muex version, mutator set, per-module counts, and each survivor's disposition
Touched critical modules stay at >=95% coverage and mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Patching muex locally to work around the defect — deps/ is not committable and a measurement produced by a hand-patched tool is not a durable verification record. Wait for the upstream release

Re-deriving the no_coverage result from task 114 — that class is decided from the coverage index before any mutation is applied and is unaffected by all three defects. The equivalent class is NOT out of scope: TCE runs on the applied mutant source, so #24 no-ops are absorbed into it
Adopting mutation testing as a permanent CI gate; this stays a one-off measurement plus the tests it produces
Solana signing and transaction paths
task.body:
Task 114 ran the campaign and could not produce its central deliverable: muex 0.8.2 cannot report a surviving mutant on Elixir 1.20, so the survivor triage that task 114 exists for has no input. This task re-runs the measurement once a muex release carries the fix.

The defect, verified against a four-file reproduction outside this repo and filed as Oeditus/muex#20: `Muex.TestRunner.Port.count_failures/2` matches the pre-1.20 ExUnit summary wording (`N tests, M failures`). Elixir 1.20 prints `Result: N passed (...)` for a green run and `Result: 0/M passed` + `Failed: N test` for a red one. Neither matches, and neither contains the substring `0 failures`, so the regex misses, the fallback returns 1 failure, and `classify_test_result({:ok, %{failures: 0}})` — the only path to `:survived` — is unreachable. Every survivor is reported `killed` and the score is a constant 100%. The same stale patterns make `has_exunit_summary?/1` always false, which reduces `compile_error?/1` to "does the output contain `** (SomethingError)`" — true whenever a test fails by raising rather than asserting — so mutants also flip between `killed` and `invalid` depending on which tests coverage guidance happened to select. In task 114's two runs over byte-identical `lib/`, 337 of 1,379 re-measured mutants changed class.

What task 114 established and this task does NOT need to redo: the surface enumeration, the campaign script (`.mutation/run.sh`, single whole-surface invocation — per-module invocations pay a full serial coverage pass each and exhausted a harness run's budget), the flag set and its rationale, and the `no_coverage` / `equivalent` results. Those two classes are decided before or without a test run — `no_coverage` from the coverage index in `select_tests/2`, `equivalent` by Trivial Compiler Equivalence bytecode comparison — so the muex defect does not touch them. Their numbers stand and are recorded in docs/verification-ledger.md.

Start by confirming the fix is real rather than assuming a version bump fixed it: run the reproduction from Oeditus/muex#20 and require it to report two survivors and a 0% score before spending hours on the full surface.

2026-08-24 attempt, aborted — that gate is necessary but not sufficient. muex 0.8.3 closes #20 (the reproduction reports survived=2 / score 0%), so a full campaign was run: 4,905 mutants, 88 minutes, 1,308 killed / 111 survived / 2,227 invalid / 1,256 equivalent / 3 no_coverage. The survivor class is not usable. Spot-checking one before triage — `transaction.ex:222`, `:binary` to `:mutated_atom`, on a line `V1.decode/1` covers with 13 assertions — showed it is killed at `test/transaction_test.exs:1213`, and killed again when driven through muex's own `Sandbox.apply_mutation/4` + `TestRunner.Port.run_tests/2`. It was scored `survived` because the mutation never reached the beam.

Two open upstream defects cause that, both unfixed in 0.8.3. Oeditus/muex#23: `Sandbox.detect_app_from_build/2` resolves the app name only on a single `_build/<env>/lib/*/.mix/compile.elixir` match and cartouche has 45, so `ensure_build_copy_for_file/2` no-ops and every sandbox's `_build/test/lib/cartouche` stays a symlink into the real project build — measured directly, before and after `apply_mutation`. Parallel workers then share one ebin and one compile manifest, and a mutant whose file a sibling recompiled in between is read as up to date and tested unmutated. This also explains task 114's 337-of-1,379 class churn over a byte-identical `lib/`. Oeditus/muex#24: mutations are keyed by their reported line, so `StatementDeletion` is a 100% no-op and bare-boolean flips are ~70% — 383 of the 4,905 mutants here, 8 of the 111 survivors, graded on unmodified source. #22 and #25 do not reach this campaign (`--no-filter` bypasses the file filter, `--test-paths test` links the whole test root).

`--concurrency 1` removes #23's race and `.mutation/run.sh` is pinned to it with the reasoning in its header, but #24 stays regardless of scheduling, so the campaign was stopped rather than run to a partly-invalid result. Blocked until a muex release carries #23 and #24; the first acceptance criterion is now a per-defect gate rather than #20 alone. Task 114's `no_coverage` result remains unaffected — that class is decided before any mutation is applied. Its `equivalent` result is NOT: Trivial Compiler Equivalence runs after the line-keyed application #24 breaks (`WorkerPool.run_mutation_worker/4` -> `Compiler.compile_to_source/3` -> `Tce.equivalent_source?/2`), so a #24 no-op compiles to identical bytecode and is scored `equivalent` without reaching a sandbox, and `--no-optimize` does not disable TCE. Both recorded `equivalent` counts are upper bounds; the re-run has to re-derive that class too.
task.blocked_reason: muex 0.8.3 fixes survivor reporting (Oeditus/muex#20) but Oeditus/muex#23 (sandboxes share the project _build, so a mutant can be graded on unmutated code) and Oeditus/muex#24 (mutations keyed by reported line, so StatementDeletion and bare-boolean flips are never applied) are open; a 2026-08-24 campaign was run and discarded. Unblocks when a muex release carries both fixes and the per-defect gate in the first acceptance criterion passes

task.title: Cartouche.RPC.create_access_list/2 — eth_createAccessList
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.RPC.create_access_list/2 sends eth_createAccessList with the same call-object encoding as eth_call and accepts the same block parameter forms (integer, :latest, hex tag) as the rest of the module

The returned access list is the {address, [storage_keys]} binary tuple list that Cartouche.Transaction.V2.new/9 and V_2930.new/8 accept, proven by a test that feeds the decoded result into V_2930.new/8 and round-trips the encoded transaction
gas_used is decoded as a non-negative integer
A node-returned error field is surfaced to the caller rather than dropped, and does not discard the access list the node returned with it

A live integration test (@moduletag :integration, Cartouche.Test.Live.live_opts/0) calls a storage-touching mainnet contract at a pinned block and asserts specific addresses and storage keys appear in the result, not merely that a list came back
A live integration test pins the node's behaviour for a reverting call, asserting the actual observed response rather than an assumed one
Doctest and @spec match the conventions of the surrounding defrpc entries
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: eth_getBlockAccessList (EIP-7928 block-level access lists) — filed against onchain, it is a block read
Automatically populating access lists during signing or gas estimation — this task adds the read, not a policy
Any access-list gas-cost heuristics
task.body:
Add `eth_createAccessList` to `Cartouche.RPC`. This is the one JSON-RPC method in the completeness sweep that belongs in cartouche rather than in onchain: it produces exactly the structure `Cartouche.Transaction.V2` and `V_2930` already encode, so it closes the loop opened by the V_2930 write surface shipped in 0.8.0 — a caller can now build a type-1 transaction but cannot ask a node what to put in its access list.

The method takes the same call object as `eth_call` / `eth_estimateGas` (reuse `to_call_params/2`) plus a block parameter, and returns `{accessList, gasUsed}` — and optionally an `error` string when the call reverts, which the node returns alongside a usable access list rather than instead of one. Decode the access list into cartouche's native representation, the `{address_binary, [storage_key_binary]}` tuple list that `V2`/`V_2930` accept, so the result can be handed straight to `new/8` without a caller-side shim. Do not invent a new struct shape for it.

Authority for the response shape is the provider-owned spec (`ethereum/execution-apis`, `src/eth/execute.yaml`) plus the live node, not a third-party client.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787470449354-d8c31a68, 670b22b49c91c5c80432a3fd5c000e92207a7992).

task.title: Complete the Cartouche.Filter lifecycle — uninstall, getFilterLogs, and the block/pending filter kinds
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.Filter uninstalls its node-side filter on normal termination, and a test asserts the eth_uninstallFilter call is issued with the filter id the node handed out
An uninstall that fails or times out during shutdown is logged and does not crash the terminating process, proven by a test that makes the uninstall call fail
Cartouche.RPC exposes get_filter_logs/2 (eth_getFilterLogs), decoding to the same Cartouche.Filter.Log shape eth_getFilterChanges already produces
Cartouche.RPC exposes new_block_filter/1 and new_pending_transaction_filter/1

Cartouche.Filter can be started as a block or pending-transaction filter through its existing option surface, and delivers the corresponding hash lists to listeners; log filters keep their current behaviour and existing tests stay green unchanged
The expired-filter recovery branch that task 58 hardened still fires for every filter kind, not only log filters
A live integration test (@moduletag :integration) creates each of the three filter kinds against the node, polls it, and uninstalls it, asserting the observed payload shape for each
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: eth_subscribe / eth_unsubscribe and any WebSocket transport — cartouche is HTTP-only over Req; onchain owns the subscription surface
eth_getLogs — onchain owns historical log queries
Changing the polling interval strategy or the listener protocol
task.body:
`Cartouche.Filter` implements two of the six filter methods: it creates a filter with `eth_newFilter` and polls it with `eth_getFilterChanges`. Three consequences, the first being a defect rather than a gap.

The GenServer never calls `eth_uninstallFilter`. It registers a filter on the node and, when the process stops, abandons it — the node holds the filter until its own idle timeout expires (commonly around five minutes, but it is a node policy, not a guarantee). A supervised Filter that restarts repeatedly leaks a filter registration per restart. Install a `terminate/2` that uninstalls, and treat an uninstall failure as a logged non-fatal event rather than a crash during shutdown.

`eth_getFilterLogs` is absent, so there is no way to read a filter's full backlog — only the changes since the last poll. A consumer that attaches to an existing filter, or that wants the current matching set rather than a delta, has no route.

`eth_newBlockFilter` and `eth_newPendingTransactionFilter` are absent, so the module only supports log filters even though the polling machinery is identical for all three kinds; only the payload deserialization differs (a block-hash list, a transaction-hash list, or `Cartouche.Filter.Log` entries). Extend the existing `start_link/1` option surface to select the kind rather than adding parallel modules.

Authority for the response shapes is `ethereum/execution-apis` (`src/eth/filter.yaml`) plus the live node.
task.implemented: Landed by cursor via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787475083725-256dd007, ee89999227890b284573647435c759c7fc4cc03a).

task.title: Cartouche.RPC fee reads — eth_baseFee and eth_blobBaseFee
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.RPC.base_fee/1 and blob_base_fee/1 send eth_baseFee and eth_blobBaseFee and decode to non-negative integers, following the defrpc conventions of the surrounding fee reads

A live integration test asserts base_fee/1 against an independently computed value: eth_baseFee returns the NEXT block's base fee, so compute it in the test from a fetched block's gas_used, gas_limit and base_fee_per_gas via the EIP-1559 update rule (or read the pending block's base_fee_per_gas), fetching the anchor block and calling base_fee/1 close together and re-fetching on mismatch since the head can advance between the two calls — proving the two routes agree rather than merely that a number came back

A live integration test asserts blob_base_fee/1 is consistent with the latest block's excess_blob_gas via EIP-4844's fake_exponential computed in the test, with the same fetch-close-together-and-retry-on-head-advance handling as the base-fee check
A node that does not support the method surfaces the node's own error unchanged, pinned by a test against the observed response
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Implementing fake_exponential as library code
Any blob-fee estimation policy or V3 gas-pricing helper
eth_feeHistory changes
task.body:
Cartouche already exposes `eth_gasPrice`, `eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas` and `eth_feeHistory`. Two fee reads from the current spec are missing, and both are plain quantity returns that belong beside them.

`eth_baseFee` returns the computed base fee of the next block, which today a caller can only obtain by fetching a block and reading `base_fee_per_gas`, or by going through `eth_feeHistory`.

`eth_blobBaseFee` matters more than its size suggests: cartouche can construct and sign EIP-4844 blob transactions through `Cartouche.Transaction.V3`, but offers no way to price one. The value is derivable today — `Cartouche.Block` already deserializes `excess_blob_gas`, and EIP-4844's `fake_exponential` turns that into the blob base fee — so this is a convenience over an existing route, not an unblocking. Implement it as the direct node read; do not reimplement `fake_exponential` locally.

Note that a node may not support either method (they are recent, and `eth_blobBaseFee` is Cancun-onward). Surface the node's actual response for an unsupported method rather than translating it into a synthetic value.

Authority is `ethereum/execution-apis` (`src/eth/fee_market.yaml`) plus the live node.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787470449354-d8c31a68, 670b22b49c91c5c80432a3fd5c000e92207a7992).

task.title: Cartouche.RPC node introspection — eth_config (EIP-7910) and eth_capabilities
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.RPC.eth_config/1 returns a deserialized struct with typed fields for at least chain id, fork id, fork activation, blob schedule, precompiles and system contracts, with optional fields typed as nilable
Cartouche.RPC.eth_capabilities/1 returns the node's capability report deserialized into a documented shape
Both deserializers tolerate a response that omits optional fields, proven by unit tests over recorded payloads, and neither raises on an unknown extra field
The moduledoc states explicitly whether and how eth_config relates to the static Cartouche.Chain table; Cartouche.Chain does not acquire a runtime network dependency

A live integration test calls both methods against the node and asserts domain values, not merely shape; if the node does not implement a method the test flunks with the method name and the node's actual error rather than skipping
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Making any existing code path consume eth_config at runtime
eth_getStorageValues and eth_getBlockAccessList — filed against onchain
A chain-registry refactor
task.body:
Two node-introspection methods from the current spec are missing. They sit beside the existing `net_version` and `eth_chainId` as questions about the node and chain rather than about state.

`eth_config` (EIP-7910) returns the chain's configuration: fork activation times, the blob schedule, chain id, fork id, precompiles, and system contracts. It is the only method that lets a client discover which fork rules a node is applying without hardcoding a chain table, and cartouche carries exactly such a table in `Cartouche.Chain`. Decide, and record in the moduledoc, whether the result is offered purely as a read or is also usable to cross-check `Cartouche.Chain`; do not silently make the static table depend on a network call.

`eth_capabilities` reports which capabilities the node has available — notably whether state or state proofs are unavailable, as happens on a node without genesis world state.

Both return structured objects rather than scalars, so each needs a deserializer following the conventions of `Cartouche.FeeHistory` and `Cartouche.Block`: a struct with typed fields and a `deserialize/1`, tolerating fields a given client omits rather than raising on them. The `eth_config` payload is the larger of the two and is still evolving — read the current shape from the spec, and be explicit in the type about which fields are optional.

Authority is EIP-7910 and `ethereum/execution-apis` (`src/eth/client.yaml`, `src/eth/capabilities.yaml`) plus the live node. Note that client support is uneven; if the integration node does not implement a method, the test must record that observation and fail loudly rather than skip.

task.title: Cartouche.RPC node-custody methods — eth_accounts, eth_coinbase, eth_fillTransaction, eth_sign, eth_signTransaction, eth_sendTransaction
acceptance_criteria: All six methods are exposed on Cartouche.RPC following the surrounding defrpc conventions, with @spec, doc and doctest matching their neighbours

eth_fillTransaction's populated transaction is deserialized into cartouche's existing transaction representation rather than returned as a raw map, and a test proves the result can be encoded and decoded through Cartouche.Transaction
eth_signTransaction's returned raw transaction decodes through Cartouche.Transaction.decode/1, and a test asserts the recovered signer equals the node account that signed it

test/support/live.ex gains a development-node lane with its own env var and availability assertion; when the env var is unset the lane may fall back to booting a locally installed anvil ephemerally for the test run (cleanly torn down afterwards), and when neither is available the tests flunk with the exact env var and the anvil install/launch command, never skip; the existing mainnet chain-id-1 assertion is unchanged and the current integration suite still passes against a mainnet archive node

Live integration tests against a development node cover all six methods: accounts and coinbase return the node's configured addresses, fillTransaction populates a transaction, and signTransaction and sendTransaction produce a transaction whose recovered signer is the expected account

A live test pins the node's actual refusal for a disabled or locked-account case, asserting the observed error rather than an assumed one; a node that has the method disabled is a recorded observation, never a skip

The Cartouche.RPC moduledoc states that local signing remains the normal route, explains that the distinction is which side constructs the transaction rather than key custody, and carries the eth_sign caveat scoped to eth_sign alone
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: The personal_* namespace and any account-unlocking calls
Wiring these into Cartouche.Signer as an alternative backend — they stay raw RPC
Making any existing signing or send path prefer the node
Shipping or packaging a development node binary; booting a locally installed anvil ephemerally from the test lane is in scope, installing or vendoring one is not
task.body:
The last six `eth_` methods missing from the stack are the ones where the node, not the caller, holds the key. Cartouche's model is the opposite — build the envelope locally, sign it through `Cartouche.Signer`, submit `eth_sendRawTransaction` — which is why they were left out. For a library that aims at full JSON-RPC coverage that omission costs more to explain than to close, and against a development node (Anvil, Hardhat, geth --dev) these methods are the normal way to work.

Add all six as passthroughs. They divide into three groups and must not be documented as one thing:

- `eth_accounts` and `eth_coinbase` are pure reads with no signing at all: which addresses this node manages, and its fee recipient. Nothing about them conflicts with local signing.
- `eth_fillTransaction` asks the node to populate nonce, gas and fee fields and return the completed transaction without signing it.
- `eth_sign`, `eth_signTransaction` and `eth_sendTransaction` delegate signing, and in the last case broadcasting, to the node's own keystore.

Two things the moduledoc must state plainly. First, that local signing through `Cartouche.Signer` remains the library's normal route, and that these exist for nodes that hold keys — the distinction is not key custody as such (`Cartouche.Signer.CloudKMS` already signs with a key cartouche does not hold) but which side constructs the transaction: with these methods the envelope construction, nonce and fee policy, EIP-155 `v` derivation and low-s normalization all move into the node. Second, that `eth_sign` signs an arbitrary 32-byte digest and has historically been usable to trick a signer into signing a transaction hash; most nodes ship it disabled, and EIP-191 / `personal_sign` superseded it. Do not add a warning that discourages the other five by association.

These are passthroughs, not policy. Return what the node returns — including its refusal when a method is disabled or an account is locked — rather than translating, retrying, or substituting a locally-signed path.

Authority is `ethereum/execution-apis` (`src/eth/sign.yaml`, `src/eth/submit.yaml`, `src/eth/fill.yaml`, `src/eth/client.yaml`) plus the live node.

Note on test infrastructure: `Cartouche.Test.Live.assert_node_available!/0` flunks unless the node reports chain id 1, because the existing integration suite pins mainnet historical anchors. A mainnet archive node has no unlocked accounts, so these six cannot be exercised there. This task must add a development-node lane alongside the mainnet one — its own env var and availability assertion, following the shape of the existing helper — without weakening the mainnet check that the current suite depends on.

task.title: Cartouche.RPC.fill_transaction/2 cannot deserialize a spec-conforming eth_fillTransaction result
acceptance_criteria: fill_transaction/2 deserializes a spec-conforming FillTransactionResult — a required, unsigned `tx` object with no `raw` — into a cartouche transaction struct
The unsigned-envelope representation is explicit: whatever carries the absent v/r/s is typed to admit that absence, and dialyzer under MIX_ENV=test is clean
The geth-shaped `{raw, tx}` response keeps working and still round-trips through Cartouche.Transaction.encode/decode
A unit test covers both response shapes; the spec-conforming one asserts the populated nonce, gas and fee fields survive deserialization

Cartouche.Transaction.from_json/1 on V1/V2/V3/V4 keeps rejecting a genuinely malformed signed transaction — tolerating an unsigned fill result must not silently accept a signed one with a corrupt signature
The eth_getBlockBy* decode path is unchanged, proven by the existing integration tests staying green
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: eth_signTransaction, which returns a signed transaction and is already handled
Adding an unsigned-transaction type to the public API beyond what deserializing a fill result requires
Making anvil implement eth_fillTransaction, or vendoring a node that does
task.body:
`fill_transaction/2` decodes only the `raw` field of an `eth_fillTransaction`
response. That is geth's shape — geth answers with a `{raw, tx}` pair — but it
is not the shape the provider-owned contract defines. In `execution-apis`,
`src/schemas/transaction.yaml`, `FillTransactionResult` requires exactly one
property, `tx`, a `FilledTransaction`, and carries no `raw` at all. Against a
node that answers per spec, `fill_transaction/2` returns an error.

The reason it cannot simply decode `tx` is structural, not an oversight. A
filled transaction is populated but unsigned, so its `tx` object has no `v`,
`r`, `s` or `yParity`. Every cartouche envelope's `from_json/1` requires those
fields — `V1.from_json/1` calls `decode_hex_number!(params["v"])` and raises in
`Cartouche.Hex.decode_hex_/1` when it is absent — because the structs have no
representation for an unsigned envelope. `V2.t()` already types its signature
fields as non-nilable while `defstruct` defaults them to `nil`, the same
mismatch that produced the generated-fixture dialyzer trap documented in
CLAUDE.md, so widening `from_json/1` to tolerate missing signature fields would
push that inconsistency into a shared decoder used by `eth_getBlockBy*`.

Surfaced by the audit of `e0e240e` / `ee89999` (`.audit/e0e240e-*.md`, finding
7), confirmed against the spec rather than inferred. That audit only replaced
the opaque `FunctionClauseError` with a named `ArgumentError` that states the
limitation; it did not close it. Deciding how an unsigned envelope should be
represented is a change to a public method's contract, which is why it is a
task rather than an audit fix.

Authority is `ethereum/execution-apis`
(`src/schemas/transaction.yaml` → `FillTransactionResult`, `FilledTransaction`)
plus a live node. Note that geth and anvil disagree here: anvil 1.5.1-stable
does not implement `eth_fillTransaction` at all and answers `-32601`, which
`test/rpc_dev_node_test.exs` already pins, so the dev-node lane cannot verify
the fix on its own.
