task.title: Spec-path fill_transaction V1 results drop chainId, so encode is pre-EIP-155
acceptance_criteria: A spec-conforming unsigned legacy FillTransactionResult that includes chainId deserializes so the chain id is not discarded
Encoding that filled V1 produces the EIP-155 unsigned payload [chainId, 0, 0], not the pre-EIP-155 [0, 0, 0]
A spec-conforming unsigned legacy result that omits chainId still deserializes; encode of that struct remains the pre-EIP-155 unsigned payload
V1.get_signature/1 still reports missing signature on both shapes
V2/V_2930/V3/V4 spec-path fills continue to keep chain_id from from_json/1; from_json/1 on signed V1–V4 still raises InvalidHex on a corrupt present signature
A unit test covers both the chainId-present and chainId-absent legacy fill shapes
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Changing eth_getBlockBy* decode of signed legacy transactions
Adding a public unsigned-transaction type beyond what this preservation requires
Making anvil implement eth_fillTransaction
task.body:
Open decision before dispatch: how should an unsigned legacy fill carry chain id? Two coherent answers, pick one and write it into the implementation — do not leave both.

1. Keep v/r/s as nil (the Task 125 unsigned representation) and also preserve chainId, then teach V1.encode/1 to emit [chainId, 0, 0] when the signature is absent.
2. When chainId is present, restore the V1.new/7 convention of v=chain_id, r=0, s=0 so the existing encode path already emits EIP-155 unsigned RLP. When chainId is absent, keep nil → encode as 0.

A spec-path `eth_fillTransaction` result is a `FillTransactionResult` whose `tx` is a `FilledTransaction` (`ethereum/execution-apis` `src/schemas/transaction.yaml`). For legacy that is `TransactionLegacyUnsigned`: no `v`/`r`/`s`, and `chainId` is an optional property (not in `required`). Task 125 deserializes that shape by injecting throwaway signature placeholders, running `from_json/1`, then clearing v/r/s to nil.

The drop: `V1.from_json/1` never reads `chainId` (legacy signed JSON carries replay protection in `v`, not a separate field), and `clear_transaction_signature/1` then sets `v: nil`. `V1.encode/1` treats nil as 0, so a filled legacy struct encodes as the pre-EIP-155 payload `[0, 0, 0]` rather than `[chainId, 0, 0]`. Typed envelopes already keep `chain_id` because their `from_json/1` reads it. Surfaced as a residual concern on the Task 125 review, not a rejection.

Authority is `ethereum/execution-apis` (`TransactionLegacyUnsigned.chainId`) plus EIP-155. The current unit fixture `unsigned_filled_v1_json/0` omits `chainId`, so it cannot catch this.
task.implemented: lib/cartouche/rpc.ex,lib/cartouche/transaction.ex,test/rpc_test.exs — acceptance criterion 3 ("a legacy result that omits chainId still deserializes; encode remains the pre-EIP-155 unsigned payload") was deliberately OVERRULED, not met: [0, 0, 0] is not a valid pre-EIP-155 payload either (that is a six-field body), so a legacy fill with no chain id from either the response or the chain_id: option is refused instead of encoded. Criterion 4 ("get_signature/1 still reports missing signature on both shapes") now applies to the one surviving shape. Rationale recorded in .audit/a98c5c0.md and .audit/17b7f2a-rpc-decode-eth-filltrans.md.

task.title: base_fee/1 portability — probe the real hosted-provider refusal, then decide standard vs extension
acceptance_criteria: The real refusal is observed, not assumed: a live call to eth_baseFee against at least two independent hosted mainnet endpoints (e.g. Alchemy and Infura) is made, and the actual JSON-RPC error code and message from each is recorded verbatim in the task's implemented note
A live integration test pins the observed hosted refusal for base_fee/1 — a real result or its real refusal, never a skip — flunking with exact export instructions when the endpoint env var is absent

The existing mocked unsupported-node test in test/rpc_test.exs is corrected to replay an error actually observed from a provider rather than an assumed -32601 message, or is removed in favour of the live test

Cartouche.RPC.base_fee/1 carries a @doc that states eth_baseFee's standardization status accurately — Erigon-origin, now implemented by reth/Nethermind/geth and merged to execution-apis main on 2026-06-15, but carried by no tagged spec release — names which clients serve it, states the error a consumer on a common hosted provider receives, and points at the portable construction (pending block header baseFeePerGas)

A decision is recorded in the task body or CHANGELOG on whether base_fee/1 keeps calling eth_baseFee or switches to the pending-header read, with the reasoning; if it switches, a live test proves the two agree on a node that serves both
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Changing blob_base_fee/1 (eth_blobBaseFee is a separate method with its own support story)
Adding a general capability-probe framework to cartouche
Changing the :ethereum_node default value
task.body:
`Cartouche.RPC.base_fee/1` (lib/cartouche/rpc.ex) wraps `eth_baseFee`. Its status was re-verified on 2026-08-27 and the earlier "Erigon extension" label was too simple: the method is Erigon-origin (erigontech/erigon#11992, 2024-09-18), was adopted by reth (2026-05-08), Nethermind (2026-05-15) and go-ethereum (PR #34904, shipped v1.17.4 on 2026-06-22), and was merged into `ethereum/execution-apis` **`main`** on 2026-06-15 (PR #795, title "feat: eth_baseFee", whose own body describes it as documenting a method "supported by enterprise RPCs and Erigon"). It is nonetheless carried by **no tagged spec release** — the newest is `v1.0.0-beta.7` (2026-06-10), five days before the merge — it is absent from the vendored `openrpc-v1.0.0-beta.4.json`, and neither Alchemy nor Infura documents it. So it is spec-resident on an unreleased branch and still non-portable in practice. Our own reth node serves it, so every check the library runs is green here while consumers on the most common hosted endpoints get an error.

Do not resolve this by reading `execution-apis` `main` and concluding "standard, nothing to do" — that is precisely the inference this task exists to prevent, and rule 1 of node-portability.md now says to read a tagged release rather than the branch. Alchemy mainnet was observed on 2026-08-25 answering `-32600 "eth_baseFee is not available on the ETH_MAINNET"`; that single observation is the trigger for this task, not its conclusion.

Task 122 shipped the wrapper and did include an acceptance criterion about unsupported nodes, but it was satisfied with a mocked plug asserting `-32601 "The method eth_baseFee does not exist/is not available"` (test/rpc_test.exs:180, :458). That message was assumed, not observed — and it does not match what Alchemy actually returns. The mock therefore ratifies a guess and stays green regardless of what providers really do. This task replaces that guess with evidence.

The exposure is sharpened by cartouche's own defaults: `lib/cartouche/application.ex` defaults `:ethereum_node` to `https://mainnet.infura.io`, and README.md's configuration example recommends Infura. A user following the README's own example and calling `base_fee/1` hits the refusal.

Two things are genuinely open and should be decided with the probe results in hand, not pre-decided here:

(1) Whether `base_fee/1` should keep calling `eth_baseFee` and simply document the constraint, or switch to reading `baseFeePerGas` from the pending block header. Note the question is NOT "standard vs extension" — the spec settles that, and the answer is "standard on main, in no release". The real question is deployment lag: whether a substrate library tracks the spec or tracks what the consumer's endpoint actually serves — which every EIP-1559 node serves. `Onchain.RPC.base_fee/1` in the sibling `onchain` package took the second route on 2026-08-25 and verified the two equivalent against reth v2.5.1 in a single batch request (`eth_baseFee` == pending `baseFeePerGas` == 71_739_926, while `latest` was 68_871_658 — so the pending header, not the latest one, carries the "next block" semantics). See the `NOTE (portability):` comment above that function for the worked precedent. Switching is a behaviour-preserving change on nodes that serve both, but it is a public API's semantics, so it deserves the evidence.

(2) Whether the fix is scoped to this one function or generalized. Prefer scoping it here; a capability-probe framework is explicitly out of scope.

Premise to confirm before building on it: that Infura also refuses `eth_baseFee` is expected but unverified — only Alchemy was probed. Probe both; if a provider does serve it, say so rather than asserting a uniform refusal.

Authority is the live providers plus `ethereum/execution-apis`. A third-party client's behaviour is reference material only.

task.title: Own eth_getLogs in cartouche — stateless log queries, and delete onchain's copy
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.RPC gains an eth_getLogs wrapper accepting the standard filter object (fromBlock/toBlock/address/topics, and the mutually-exclusive blockHash form) and decoding into the existing Cartouche.Filter log struct — one wrapper, one struct, per the stack boundary

Log decoding is the SAME code the existing filter surface uses (lib/cartouche/filter.ex), not a second decoder. If the filter surface's decode is not reusable as-is, refactor it so it is — do not copy it

A live integration test pins one real success (logs from a known mainnet event range) and one relevant real error the node actually refuses, recorded verbatim — a real result or its real refusal, never a skip; flunks with exact export instructions when the node env var is absent

The same call is exercised on >=1 hosted endpoint via the task-136 seam, since hosted providers commonly cap getLogs by block range or result count — that cap is a real, recordable answer, not a test failure
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Changing the existing filter-installation surface (eth_newFilter / eth_getFilterChanges) — it stays; this adds the stateless sibling
ABI event decoding — that is hieroglyph's layer, above the log struct
Editing the onchain repo — cartouche cannot touch it from its own worktree; the deletion there is the companion task named in the body
task.body:
`eth_getLogs` is in the tagged execution-apis release (`v1.0.0-beta.7`, `src/eth/filter.yaml`) and in the vendored local spec, so under the stack boundary it is cartouche's, unambiguously: cartouche owns one wrapper plus one decoded struct for every method in a tagged spec release.

Today cartouche's only log access is filter-based — `eth_newFilter` + `eth_getFilterLogs` / `eth_getFilterChanges` in lib/cartouche/filter.ex. The stateless query that takes the same filter object with no server-side filter installation is missing. That is the one most consumers actually use, because hosted providers limit or discourage installed filters: the filter-only surface is a portability gap on exactly the endpoints consumers run against.

Meanwhile `onchain` has its own `eth_getLogs` at lib/onchain/rpc.ex:974, decoding into its own shape. That is the duplication the boundary reversal exists to end.

**The invariant this task must satisfy: one decoder, one struct.** cartouche gains the method and the log struct. onchain's duplicate log DECODER stops existing — whether its public `eth_get_logs/2` disappears entirely or survives returning cartouche's struct is onchain's call, made in onchain's own task, and this task must not prejudge it. What is not negotiable is that no second derivation of the same wire shape remains anywhere in the stack.

This task delivers the cartouche half only, because a cartouche worktree cannot edit the onchain repo. The companion task in onchain's roadmap deletes lib/onchain/rpc.ex:974 and repoints its callers. Sequence: this lands first (onchain depends on cartouche, not the reverse), then the deletion.

Authority: the tagged execution-apis spec and the live node. A third-party client's reading is reference material only, never semantics.

task.title: Own the transaction and receipt read-back in cartouche — 4 methods, and delete onchain's copies
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.RPC gains eth_getTransactionByHash, eth_getTransactionByBlockHashAndIndex, eth_getTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex and eth_getBlockReceipts, each decoding into a cartouche struct — all four are in the tagged spec and are therefore cartouche's to own

Transaction-object decoding covers all five 2718 types the repo already models (legacy, 2930, 1559, 4844, 7702), including yParity/v, accessList, blobVersionedHashes and authorizationList; a live test fetches a known mainnet type-2 tx AND a legacy tx and asserts decoded domain fields, not just shape
A null result for an unknown hash maps to an explicit not-found return, never a decode crash — pinned by a live test against a hash that genuinely does not exist
eth_getBlockReceipts reuses the EXISTING receipt decoding rather than adding a second one; a live test asserts the receipt list of a known block

The decode target follows the repo's existing JsonField / typed_decode precedent — decide between the existing transaction structs and a dedicated RPC-view struct by reading how Cartouche.Block already handles the same JSON-vs-RLP split, and follow it rather than inventing a third convention
Live tests flunk with exact export instructions when the node env var is absent, never skip
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Pending-pool inspection (txpool_* namespaces) — not in the spec, different task if ever wanted
Re-encoding the RPC transaction object back to raw RLP
Editing the onchain repo — the deletions there are the companion task named in the body
task.body:
All four methods are in the tagged execution-apis release `v1.0.0-beta.7` (`src/eth/transaction.yaml` for the three transaction getters, `src/eth/block.yaml` for `eth_getBlockReceipts`) and in the vendored local spec. Under the stack boundary they are cartouche's: the node's wire format defines them, so cartouche owns the wrapper and the decoded struct.

cartouche today can fetch a receipt (`eth_getTransactionReceipt`) but not the transaction itself. All four are absent.

All four already exist in `onchain`, hand-decoded there: lib/onchain/rpc.ex:924 (`eth_getTransactionByHash`), :672 (`...ByBlockHashAndIndex`), :715 (`...ByBlockNumberAndIndex`), :569 (`eth_getBlockReceipts`). This is the duplicated-decoder problem the boundary reversal was adopted to end — onchain could not own the decode without owning the struct, so it wrote its own.

**The invariant: one decoder, one struct.** cartouche gains the four methods and their structs; onchain's four hand-written decoders stop existing. Whether onchain keeps its public functions (returning cartouche structs) or drops them is onchain's decision in onchain's task — note that its wrappers carry retry, telemetry and node-refusal classification that cartouche does not yet have, so a bare deletion is not obviously the cheaper option. This task is the cartouche half only; a cartouche worktree cannot edit the onchain repo, and the dependency edge runs cartouche <- onchain, so this lands and ships first.

The transaction methods return the RPC transaction *object* (the JSON view), not raw RLP — that is a genuinely different shape from the signed-envelope structs, and the decision of where it decodes to is the substantive design work in this task. Cartouche.Block already faced the identical JSON-vs-RLP question; read block.ex before choosing, and follow its precedent.

Authority: the tagged execution-apis spec plus the live node.

task.title: Own the state reads in cartouche — eth_getStorageAt and eth_getProof (EIP-1186)
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.RPC gains eth_getStorageAt (address, slot, block tag -> 32-byte word) with block-tag support, pinned by a live test reading a known mainnet contract slot

Cartouche.RPC gains eth_getProof decoding into a cartouche struct covering the account fields (balance, nonce, codeHash, storageHash, accountProof) and the storageProof entries; a live test asserts domain fields of a known contract's proof, not just shape
One relevant real error per method is observed and pinned as the node actually answers it — never an assumed error string

Historical-state depth is verified against >=1 hosted endpoint via the task-136 seam, not asserted: both methods are fully standard, but archive depth is the privileged part. Whatever the hosted endpoint answers for a deep-history block IS the finding — record it verbatim, and let the @doc say what was observed rather than promising depth
@doc for both names the spec release that carries them and the observed depth caveat
Live tests flunk with exact export instructions when the node env var is absent, never skip
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Client-side Merkle-Patricia verification of a proof against the state root — a real feature, genuinely separate, and not needed to own the read
Editing onchain_evm — the deletion there is the companion task named in the body
task.body:
Both methods are in the tagged execution-apis release `v1.0.0-beta.7` (`src/eth/state.yaml`) and in the vendored local spec. Both are cartouche's under the stack boundary. Both are absent from cartouche today.

The existing duplication is smaller here than elsewhere but real, and it sits in a sibling rather than in `onchain`:

- `eth_getStorageAt` has exactly one caller in the stack — onchain_evm, lib/onchain/trace.ex:185 — where it is inlined into the trace module. Note that the hit at onchain/lib/onchain/rpc.ex:1033 is a doc-string EXAMPLE listing legal method names, not a wrapper; do not mistake it for one.
- `eth_getProof` is fully implemented in onchain at lib/onchain/rpc.ex:1193, including key normalization.

**The invariant: one decoder, one struct.** cartouche gains both methods and the proof struct. The onchain_evm inline call and onchain's `eth_getProof` decoding are resolved by companion tasks in those repos; the mechanism there is theirs to choose, but no second derivation of the proof shape may survive.

`eth_getProof` is EIP-1186 and returns a structured account proof; it decodes into a proper cartouche struct following the repo's decoding conventions, not a bare map. `eth_getStorageAt` is a thin wrapper returning a 32-byte word.

The portability point worth getting right: these are not extension methods, so rule 1 is satisfied by the tag. But spec residency says nothing about *availability at depth* — a hosted provider serves recent state and refuses or truncates deep history, and that refusal is the consumer's reality. Probe it rather than documenting an assumption.

Authority: the tagged execution-apis spec, EIP-1186, and the live node.

task.title: Own the node-introspection surface in cartouche — and mark the three methods no tagged spec carries
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.RPC gains all six: eth_syncing, eth_getBlockTransactionCountByHash, eth_getBlockTransactionCountByNumber, net_listening, net_peerCount, web3_clientVersion

eth_syncing decodes BOTH answers — the bare `false` and the sync-status object — as a single documented union; the synced case is pinned live, the syncing-object case unit-tested against its spec shape

The three methods no tagged release carries are documented as such, each with the precise reason, NOT lumped together as 'standard': net_listening and net_peerCount were merged to execution-apis `main` only after v1.0.0-beta.7 (commit 7c58b32, 'Add net_listening and net_peerCount (#843)') and are in no tag; web3_clientVersion is in execution-apis at NO point in its history and is defined only by EIP-1474. All three are absent from the vendored local spec

Per the stack boundary's rule for methods outside a tagged release, those three ship with a @doc naming what defines them and what a consumer sees when an endpoint refuses, plus a capability probe rather than a failure deep in a pipeline — the observed refusal recorded verbatim from the task-136 hosted lane, never assumed
The three that ARE in the tagged spec (eth_syncing, and both eth_getBlockTransactionCountBy*) carry no such caveat — the distinction between the two groups must be visible in the docs, not flattened
Live tests flunk with exact export instructions when the node env var is absent, never skip
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: web3_sha3 — keccak is local in the crypto layer; a network round-trip to hash bytes is an anti-pattern and is deliberately not added
net_version — already present in the tagged spec since v1.0.0-beta.1 and outside this task's set; if cartouche lacks it, that is its own task
Editing the onchain repo — the deletions there are the companion task named in the body
task.body:
Six methods, and the reason this task is NOT a rubber-stamp sweep is that they do not share a standardization status. Verified 2026-08-27 against the execution-apis repository at tag and at `main`, not from memory:

- **In the tagged release v1.0.0-beta.7, and in the vendored local spec** — `eth_syncing` (`src/eth/client.yaml`), `eth_getBlockTransactionCountByHash` and `eth_getBlockTransactionCountByNumber` (`src/eth/block.yaml`). Straightforwardly cartouche's.
- **On `main` only, in no tag** — `net_listening` and `net_peerCount`, added by commit 7c58b32 ("Add net_listening and net_peerCount (#843)"), which is `main`'s current tip and lands strictly after beta.7. Absent from the vendored spec.
- **Never in execution-apis at all** — `web3_clientVersion`. Grepped exhaustively across every `src/**/*.yaml` on `main` HEAD and on every tag: zero hits in the repository's entire history. It is defined only by EIP-1474.

That distribution is the whole point of the task. `net_listening` / `net_peerCount` are the exact shape of the `eth_baseFee` trap that node-portability rule 1 now names explicitly: merged to `main`, not in any tag, and re-vendoring the spec from `main` would silently reclassify them as standard. They are being wrapped here deliberately and with their status written down, so that nobody later reads `main`, sees them, and deletes the caveat.

All six go into cartouche — the boundary puts every `eth_*` / `net_*` / node-wire method there, with the tagged ones plain and the untagged ones carrying a `@doc` naming who defines them plus a capability probe. Ownership is not conditional on spec status; documentation is.

Existing duplication in onchain: `eth_syncing` at lib/onchain/rpc.ex:446, `eth_getBlockTransactionCountByHash` at :601, `...ByNumber` at :636. The other three exist nowhere in the stack. Those three onchain copies are resolved by the companion task in onchain's roadmap — these are scalar-returning methods, so the duplication is thin and the resolution there is cheap whichever way onchain goes.

`eth_syncing`'s boolean-or-object union is the only decode of substance. The rest are thin, and thin is fine — a general-purpose library owning the node's wire surface completely is the deliverable, and completeness of that surface is the reason, stated plainly and needing no other.

task.title: Own eth_simulateV1 in cartouche — the portable simulation entry point
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.RPC gains eth_simulateV1 modelling blockStateCalls with state and block overrides, and decoding per-call results including logs and per-call error objects into cartouche structs
The request surface covers the spec'd shape — blockStateCalls, stateOverrides, blockOverrides, returnFullTransactions, traceTransfers, validation — modelled as structs per repo conventions

A live test pins one real multi-call simulation success (e.g. a funded transfer via a state override) and one relevant real per-call failure exactly as the node reports it, including the JSON-RPC error code

Method-not-found (-32601) is surfaced as an explicit capability answer, not an opaque error — the onchain_tempo precedent at lib/onchain/tempo/rpc.ex classifies exactly this and its shape should be read before designing cartouche's
@doc names eth_simulateV1 as carried by the tagged spec since v1.0.0-beta.5 and contrasts it with the privileged trace_callMany / debug_traceCall path that task 135 documents
Behaviour is verified on >=1 hosted endpoint via the task-136 seam as well as the archive node — a real result or its real refusal, never a skip
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: A convenience simulation DSL or bundle-builder on top of the raw surface — the raw spec'd surface is the deliverable
Deprecating or changing trace_call / trace_call_many / debug_trace_call — task 135 owns their portability contract; they stay
Refactoring onchain_tempo's AA-specific simulate/3 — it is a domain caller, not a duplicate wrapper; see the body
task.body:
`eth_simulateV1` entered the execution-apis spec at tag `v1.0.0-beta.5` (2026-06-03, `src/eth/execute.yaml`) — verified by walking the tags directly, beta.1 through beta.7 — and it IS present in the vendored local spec. It is squarely cartouche's under the stack boundary, and it is the portable answer to the privileged `trace_callMany` / `debug_traceCall` pair cartouche already wraps.

Client support is real and was verified against each client's own source, not from memory: geth (`internal/ethapi/api.go`, `BlockChainAPI.SimulateV1`), reth (`crates/rpc/rpc-eth-api/src/core.rs`, with the tracking issue closed as implemented), erigon (`rpc/jsonrpc/eth_simulation.go`, and its rpcdaemon README lists it supported) and nethermind (`EthRpcModule.cs`). So the premise the earlier version of this task flagged as unverified is now confirmed for the archive node's client — but confirm the node's live answer anyway before building on it, because a client implementing a method and an endpoint serving it are different facts.

**One existing caller, and it is NOT a duplicate to delete.** onchain_tempo calls `eth_simulateV1` at lib/onchain/tempo/rpc.ex:128, but it is a domain consumer, not a competing wrapper: it builds a single AA-folded 0x76 call, interprets the result as success / revert / unsupported for a fee-payer gas-drain guard, and carries an empirically-verified note that `tempo_simulateV1` is not deployed on Tempo mainnet or Moderato. That is exactly the layering the boundary prescribes — the chain-specific package re-presents the node method for its domain. It stays.

What it does reveal is a second transport escape: it builds its own `do_rpc_request/4` directly on Req + Jason rather than going through the shared transport, mirroring why `Onchain.HTTP` exists. Worth noting, out of scope here.

Two things to take from that module rather than reinvent: its `-32601` -> `:unsupported` classification is the capability-probe shape this method needs, and its `-38013` handling shows that execution errors arrive as JSON-RPC errors distinct from transport failure. cartouche's decode must keep those three outcomes — succeeded, reverted/rejected, method unsupported — distinguishable, because collapsing them is what makes a fail-open caller unsafe.

Authority: the tagged execution-apis spec plus the live node.

task.title: EIP-712 conformance: encode_type non-termination, bytesN padding direction, array-of-struct support, int types
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.Typed.encode_type/2 terminates for a type referencing two or more DISTINCT struct types, and a test asserts termination with a bounded Task.yield rather than hanging the suite; today `%{"Root" => fields [{"z","Zebra"},{"a","Apple"}]}` never returns

Referenced struct types are appended sorted by name, per EIP-712 'the set of referenced struct types is collected, sorted by name and appended'; a test pins a type whose field order and alphabetical order differ and asserts the exact encodeType string

bytesN values are zero-padded AT THE END per EIP-712; `encode_data_value(<<0xCC>>, {:bytes, 32})` returns <<0xCC, 0::248>>. The doctest at typed.ex:279-280 currently asserts the opposite and must be corrected, not deleted
Address and uint stay LEFT-padded (address is uint160, big-endian) — a test pins both alignments side by side so the two opposite semantics can never be re-conflated into one pad/2 call

Struct types referenced through an array field are collected into encodeType (today `Root(Person[] people)` omits `Person(string name)` silently), and encode_data_value/2 encodes an array-of-structs field without raising
int8..int256 are representable: deserialize_type/1 returns an int variant, serialize_type/1 round-trips it, and encode_data_value/2 sign-extends to 256 bits big-endian per EIP-712

The whole surface is pinned against independent implementations the way docs/verification-ledger.md pins transactions: signTypedData vectors generated from BOTH ethers and viem, covering nested structs, arrays of structs, bytesN, and a negative int — following test/fixtures/vectors/generate.cjs's existing pattern
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: EIP-712 domain-separator policy or chain-id binding — this task fixes encoding conformance, not domain semantics
A typed-data message builder for Hyperliquid or any specific venue — orthogonal, and already fenced off by task 104
Refactoring Cartouche.Hex.pad/2's signature; adding a right-padding function beside it is fine, changing every existing caller is not
task.body:
`Cartouche.Typed` is the EIP-712 path the stack signs permits and orders through — task 69 records that ERC-2612 permit "already expresses it". It has four confirmed spec defects. All four were verified by executing the compiled module, not by reading it; the reproductions are below and should be turned into the failing tests before any fix.

1. `encode_type/2` DOES NOT TERMINATE for a type referencing 2+ distinct struct types. `do_encode_type/4` (typed.ex:811-836) updates its pending queue as `next_new_types = rest ++ Enum.reverse(new_types_r)` (typed.ex:831). When `rest` is non-empty and the current type discovers no new struct, `rest` is re-appended to itself instead of shrinking, so the queue never drains. Reproduced live: `Root` with fields `{"z","Zebra"},{"a","Apple"}` did not return in 4s. This is not an exotic shape — any `Order{maker: Person, item: Item}` hits it. It was never caught because every existing doctest uses exactly one distinct referenced type (`Person` twice, for `from`/`to`), and `test/typed_test.exs` (88 lines) never calls `encode_type` at all.

2. Referenced struct types are appended in field-discovery order. EIP-712 requires them "collected, sorted by name and appended". Fixing (1) without also sorting produces a terminating but still non-conforming `typeHash`.

3. `bytesN` is LEFT-padded. `encode_data_value(value, {:bytes, _})` (typed.ex:296) calls `Cartouche.Hex.pad(value, 32)`, and `pad/2` (hex.ex:632-635) prepends zeros. EIP-712: "bytes1 to bytes31 ... are zero-padded at the end to bytes32". The doctest at typed.ex:279-280 asserts the wrong answer, so the test suite ratifies the bug — this is the coverage-ratifies-the-constant pattern from CLAUDE.md, and the doctest must be corrected as part of the fix. Note carefully that the SAME `pad/2` is correct at typed.ex:292 for `:address`, because address is uint160 and numeric types are big-endian left-padded. One function is serving two opposite alignments; separate them and pin both in one test so this cannot regress.

4. Arrays of structs are broken in both directions. `encode_data_value(value, {:array, ty})` (typed.ex:300-304) recurses with a struct-name `ty` that has no matching clause -> FunctionClauseError (reproduced). And `do_encode_type`'s discovery guard (typed.ex:820) tests `is_binary(type)`, which is false for `{:array, "Person"}`, so `encode_type` returns `"Root(Person[] people)"` with `Person` silently omitted — a wrong hash even where nothing crashes.

Separately, `Type.primitive()` (typed.ex:25-33) has no int variant and `deserialize_type("int256")` raises `"unknown type: int256"`. EIP-712 defines int8..int256; signed fields (ticks, deltas, funding) are unrepresentable.

Severity ordering for the implementer: (3) and the array half of (4) are SILENT wrong signatures — no error, no validation failure until a counterparty rejects. (1) is a hang. (2) is a wrong hash. The int gap is a loud raise. Fix all of them, but write the silent ones' tests first.

Authority is the EIP-712 text plus two independent implementations — ethers `_TypedDataEncoder` and viem `hashTypedData`. Where the EIP is terse, agreement across those two is the spec in practice; a single implementation's behaviour is not.

task.title: EIP-191 personal_sign byte length, a recovery helper that applies the prefix, and the 65-byte signature invariant
acceptance_criteria: Recover.prefix_eth/1 uses the UTF-8 BYTE length of the message, matching go-ethereum accounts.TextHash and viem; a test pins a multi-byte message (e.g. "café" -> length 5, not 4) and asserts the exact prefixed bytes

A recover_personal_sign/2 (or equivalently named) function applies the prefix and recovers, so the use case Recover's own moduledoc advertises — verifying MetaMask / WalletConnect personal_sign payloads — works without the caller hand-assembling the envelope

The signature-width contract is made true or made honest: Signer.sign/3 (signer.ex:307-312) builds v as chain_id*2+35+recid and encodes it with :binary.encode_unsigned/1, so any chain id > 110 yields a 66-68 byte result, while Cartouche.signature() is declared <<_::520>> (cartouche.ex:103) and RecoveryBit.normalize_signature/2 pattern-matches <<rs::binary-size(64), v>> (recovery_bit.ex:100). A test signs on a non-mainnet chain id (e.g. Base 8453) and asserts the documented behaviour end to end, including that normalize_signature/2 does not FunctionClauseError
Signer.sign/3's @spec is narrowed from bare binary() to the real return type so dialyzer can see the contract; mix ci's MIX_ENV=test dialyzer stays clean

RecoveryBit's EIP-155 normalization no longer silently reads the process-global :chain_id (recovery_bit.ex:62, :143) when the caller can supply the signature's own chain — or, if the global stays, a test pins the documented failure for a signature from a different chain rather than leaving it to raise 'Invalid EIP-155 Signature' opaquely
Every touched module is at critical-tier >=95% coverage BEFORE mutating (raise coverage first if below, per the coverage gate)
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: EIP-712 encoding conformance — a separate task owns lib/cartouche/typed.ex and lib/cartouche/hex.ex; do not touch those files
Transaction.V1.add_signature/2's missing chain-consistency guard — related, but it is a transaction-envelope concern and would collide with the transaction surface's write set
New signer backends
task.body:
Three defects on the signing surface, all verified by execution.

`Recover.prefix_eth/1` (recover.ex:75) builds the EIP-191 envelope with `to_string(String.length(msg))` — grapheme clusters, not bytes. Its own `@doc` two lines above (recover.ex:60-63) says "the byte length of `msg`", so the implementation contradicts its documentation. go-ethereum's `accounts.TextHash` uses `fmt.Sprintf("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n%d%s", len(data), data)` over a []byte, and viem's `toPrefixedMessage` uses the byte size — two independent references agree. Reproduced: `prefix_eth("café")` emits `...\n4café` where every mainstream wallet emits `...\n5café`, so the digest differs and recovery silently fails. The only doctest uses "hello", where grapheme count and byte count coincide — which is why it survived.

The same module's moduledoc (recover.ex:19-20) sells it as the surface for "verifying user-supplied signatures (e.g. `personal_sign` payloads from MetaMask, WalletConnect)", but `recover_eth/2` does not apply the prefix and there is no personal_sign helper. A consumer following the moduledoc recovers the wrong address. Add the helper so the advertised path exists.

The signature-width defect is a type lie with a latent crash behind it. `sign/3` (signer.ex:307-312) computes `v = chain_id * 2 + 35 + recid` and appends `:binary.encode_unsigned(v)`. For any chain id above 110 — which is every chain in `Cartouche.Chain` except mainnet and the dead testnets — `v` does not fit in one byte, so the "65-byte signature" the moduledoc (signer.ex:10-11) and `sign_direct/4` (signer.ex:236) promise is actually 66-68 bytes. `Cartouche.signature()` is typed `<<_::520>>` (cartouche.ex:103) and `RecoveryBit.normalize_signature/2` matches `<<rs::binary-size(64), v>>` (recovery_bit.ex:100), so a Base or Sepolia signature FunctionClauseErrors there. Dialyzer cannot see it because `sign/3`'s spec returns bare `binary()`. The doctest at signer.ex:124-126 asserts the multi-byte behaviour, so again the suite ratifies it.

Decide deliberately which way to resolve the width contract and record the reasoning: either the concatenated form stops carrying EIP-155 v (returning 65 bytes with a parity byte, chain binding living in the transaction envelope where V1 already threads it), or the docs and types stop claiming 65. Do not "fix" it by widening the guard in one place and leaving the other two.

While in `RecoveryBit`: `recover_base/1` (recovery_bit.ex:143-151, :62) normalizes an EIP-155 v against `config :cartouche, :chain_id` — a process-global — in a library whose `Chain` module knows 24 chains and whose `Transaction.V1` takes a per-call chain id. Either thread the chain through or pin the failure explicitly.

Critical tier: this is signing. Raise coverage to >=95% on each touched module before mutating it.

task.title: Portability contract for the non-standard read surface: trace_* and debug_traceCall
acceptance_criteria: trace_transaction (rpc.ex:1435), trace_call (:1586), trace_call_many (:1790) and debug_trace_call (:1872) each carry a @doc naming that the method is absent from ethereum/execution-apis, which clients serve it, and the error a consumer on a common hosted endpoint receives — the error recorded verbatim from an observed response, never assumed

A capability probe exists following the Onchain.Trace.available?/1 precedent cited by node-portability.md rule 3, so a consumer can branch before failing deep in a pipeline rather than parsing an error string

README.md's node-compatibility section is corrected: it currently claims 'nearly all of its surface is standard ... the transaction, balance, block, log, receipt, call and fee-history methods work against any mainstream Ethereum node' while listing only base_fee and archive depth as caveats. The trace/debug surface must appear in that table

A live test pins the probe's answer on the privileged node (serves trace_*) AND the observed refusal from at least one hosted endpoint — a real result or its real refusal, never a skip; flunk with exact export instructions when an endpoint env var is absent
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Removing or reimplementing the trace wrappers — they work on nodes that serve them and consumers depend on them; this task documents and probes, it does not deprecate
eth_simulateV1 as the portable replacement — that is its own task
base_fee/1 — its own task owns that @doc
task.body:
Verified against ethereum/execution-apis `main` by two independent checks this session: the `trace_*` namespace does not appear in the specification at all, and `src/debug/trace.yaml` carries only `debug_traceBlockByNumber`, `debug_traceBlockByHash` and `debug_traceTransaction` — NOT `debug_traceCall`. So cartouche ships four non-standard read methods.

None of them carries any portability note. Grepping rpc.ex for Erigon / non-standard / Alchemy / Infura / portab returns only `fill_transaction` comments. There is no capability probe, and README.md's node-compatibility section affirmatively tells the reader the surface is nearly all standard, naming only `base_fee` and archive depth as exceptions.

This is a larger portability hole than `base_fee/1` and it is the one with no task. `base_fee` at least got a README caveat; the trace surface is invisible in the docs, the roadmap, and the module docs simultaneously.

Origin, for the @doc wording: `trace_*` is the OpenEthereum/Parity namespace, inherited by Erigon and implemented by reth (our own archive node serves it — that is why every existing trace integration test is green here). Do not write that reth lacks it; verify each client claim against that client's own documentation before putting it in a @doc, and cite what you checked.

The probe precedent to follow is `Onchain.Trace.available?/1` in the sibling onchain_evm package — read it before designing a new shape. This is rule 3 of node-portability.md applied where it actually bites: name who serves it, name the consumer-visible error, and expose a probe rather than failing deep in a pipeline.

task.title: Multi-endpoint live-test seam so node-portability rule 4 can actually be executed
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.Test.Live gains a named-endpoint lane beside the existing single live_rpc_url/0: an endpoint is addressed by name (e.g. :archive, :alchemy, :infura, :cloudflare) and resolves to a URL from a per-endpoint env var, so a test can request the SAME call on two endpoints without the whole suite being re-run under a different env var

The existing live_opts/0 and live_rpc_url/0 keep working unchanged — all 56 existing call sites across test/rpc_integration_test.exs, test/filter_test.exs and test/rpc_debug_namespace_test.exs stay green with no edit. This is an additive seam, not a migration

A helper expresses rule 4's actual assertion shape: run one call against the privileged node AND against >=1 hosted endpoint, and assert on BOTH answers — the hosted endpoint's real refusal is as much a pass as its success. A hosted endpoint that answers -32601/-32600 must be recordable as the expected result, not treated as a test error

Absent env vars flunk with the exact export command for that endpoint, never skip — matching assert_node_available!/0's existing flunk style. A portability test that silently skips on the hosted lane is the exact failure this seam exists to prevent
assert_node_available!/0's hard chain-id-1 assertion is preserved or generalized per endpoint; a hosted mainnet endpoint must satisfy the same mainnet pin the archive node does

At least one real portability test uses the seam end to end and is green: re-verify base_fee/1 (task 127's subject) on the archive node and on >=1 hosted endpoint, recording the hosted answer verbatim
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Rewriting the existing integration tests onto the new lane — additive only; migrating call sites is a later task if ever wanted
The dev/anvil lane (dev_opts/0, ephemeral anvil boot) — untouched
Fixing base_fee/1 itself, or writing the trace_* portability docs — tasks 127 and 135 own those; this task only makes their evidence obtainable
A general RPC provider-abstraction or failover layer in lib/ — this is test infrastructure
task.body:
node-portability.md rule 4 says: "Verify on a second, unprivileged endpoint before claiming portability. Green on localhost:8545 alone proves nothing. A hosted endpoint's real refusal is evidence; our node's {:ok, _} is not." The same file then admits, under Honest limits, that "Rule 4 has no tooling today — whoever builds it should build it first."

This task builds it first.

The current seam is single-endpoint by construction. `Cartouche.Test.Live.live_rpc_url/0` (test/support/live.ex) returns one string from `CARTOUCHE_LIVE_NODE_URL`, defaulting to http://127.0.0.1:8545, and `live_opts/0` bakes it into a keyword list used at 56 call sites across three test files. There is no way to express "this call, on that other endpoint" inside a test — the dual-endpoint base_fee verification recorded in node-portability.md's worked example was done by manually re-running the whole suite with a different env var, which is not something an acceptance criterion can require of a dispatched agent.

The consequence is concrete, not theoretical: tasks 127 and 135 both carry criteria demanding a hosted-endpoint observation, and as written neither is satisfiable with the current seam. Five read-surface tasks (128-132) want the same evidence. Every one of them is blocked on infrastructure that does not exist, which is why this is filed as a prerequisite rather than folded into any single one of them.

Endpoints are already available to the operator and need no procurement — ~/.secrets defines ETHEREUM_ALCHEMY_URL, ETHEREUM_INFURA_URL and CLOUDFLARE_ETHEREUM_API_URL (three distinct vendors on mainnet), alongside ETH_RPC_URL / ETHEREUM_API_URL and the Base/Sepolia URLs. Read the variable NAMES from the operator's environment; never print, log, echo or commit a value — these are credentialed URLs and an Alchemy or Infura URL embeds the API key in its path. A test that flunks must name the env var, not interpolate its contents.

Design note, deliberately left to the implementer: whether the named lane is a keyword/atom map, a per-endpoint module attribute, or a small struct is a judgment call — follow the file's existing style (module attributes + plain functions, no config) rather than introducing a config-driven registry. The one thing that is NOT a judgment call is the assertion shape: a hosted refusal must be a first-class expected outcome. If the helper can only express "both endpoints returned {:ok, _}", it has failed to encode rule 4 and would have ratified the base_fee bug.

The house idioms to reuse verbatim in docs and flunk messages: "a real result or its real refusal, never a skip"; "the consumer's node — not ours — as the case that matters"; "the identical green run on both endpoints is what the portability claim rests on".

task.title: Move the transport hardening into cartouche — retry, telemetry, node-refusal classification, batch
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.RPC gains node-refusal classification: JSON-RPC -32601 / -32600 / -32001 become distinguishable tagged results (method-not-found / namespace-unavailable / unavailable) instead of an opaque error term. Port the semantics from Onchain.RPC.classify_node_refusal/1 (onchain/lib/onchain/rpc.ex:1374-1391), whose moduledoc records that it was pinned against live Alchemy responses — keep that provenance in the @doc

Cartouche.RPC gains opt-in retry over send_rpc/3 with the same policy onchain proved: transport failures retry, JSON-RPC application errors are final and never retried (onchain/lib/onchain/rpc.ex:1317-1368). Generalize it to wrap a call rather than one hardcoded function — onchain's retry_rpc/4 can only call Helpers.do_rpc/3, which is why its typed wrappers cannot use it
Cartouche.RPC emits telemetry spans around every request, matching the event shape onchain already publishes so downstream dashboards keep working
Cartouche.RPC gains a JSON-RPC array batch primitive — cartouche has none today, which is the sole reason Onchain.HTTP's batch POST path exists (onchain/lib/onchain/rpc.ex:1516)

Cartouche's own config split is not widened: send_rpc/3 stays :cartouche-keyed end to end. Note in the CHANGELOG that onchain's batch path currently reads its URL from :cartouche, :ethereum_node while reading transport options from :onchain (onchain/lib/onchain/rpc.ex:1527-1530) — record the split, do not import it
Existing cartouche behaviour is unchanged for callers that opt into none of it: no retry, no classification rewrite of existing return shapes unless explicitly requested per call
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Deleting anything in the onchain repo — a cartouche worktree cannot; the deletions are onchain-side companion tasks
Unifying onchain's URL-vs-transport-options config split — that is onchain's own defect and its own task
Bang variants (foo!/N) — a separate ergonomic decision, not transport
task.body:
This task is what makes the stack boundary's clean cut actually safe to execute, and it was found by reading both call pipelines rather than by reasoning from the layer diagram.

The boundary says cartouche owns the transport and every in-spec method; onchain re-presents, never re-derives. Tasks 128-132 move the methods down. But a straight deletion of onchain's duplicate wrappers would be a real regression, because onchain's wrappers are not thin: each one runs inside `:telemetry.span([:onchain, :rpc, :request], ...)` (lib/onchain/rpc.ex:1310-1313), optionally inside `retry_rpc/4` (:1317-1367, transport failures retried, application errors final at :1366-1368), and its result passes through `classify_node_refusal/1` (:1374-1391), which turns `-32601` / `-32600` / `-32001` into tagged, branchable outcomes and was pinned against live Alchemy responses (moduledoc, rpc.ex:41-99). cartouche's `send_rpc/3` (lib/cartouche/rpc.ex:515-556) has none of these.

Every one of those is a transport concern. Under the boundary they belong in cartouche by definition — the layer that owns the JSON-RPC wire owns retrying it, measuring it, and telling the caller why a node refused. That they grew in onchain is an artifact of the old rule that put wrappers there.

There is a structural reason this cannot be fixed by delegation, which is worth stating so nobody proposes it later: onchain composes the hardening OUTSIDE the raw call, whereas cartouche's typed wrappers put the decode INSIDE `send_rpc/3` via its `:decode` option. So `Onchain.RPC.foo/2` delegating to `Cartouche.RPC.foo/2` inverts the nesting and silently drops retry, because `retry_rpc/4` is hardcoded to call `Helpers.do_rpc/3` (:1350) and cannot wrap a typed call. Generalizing it is part of this task, not a rider on a per-method port.

The node-refusal classification is the highest-value piece and should be treated as such. It is exactly what node-portability rule 3 asks for — "expose a capability probe rather than failing deep in a pipeline" — and cartouche currently forces consumers to string-match error text to discover that an endpoint does not serve a method. Tasks 131, 132 and 135 all need this: 131 wraps three methods no tagged spec carries, 132 needs `-32601` distinguishable from a failed simulation, and 135 needs a probe for the trace namespace. onchain_tempo independently reinvented the same `-32601 -> :unsupported` classification (onchain_tempo/lib/onchain/tempo/rpc.ex) — a third implementation of one idea, which is the signal that it belongs one layer down.

The onchain-side question — whether onchain's duplicated wrappers disappear entirely or survive returning cartouche structs — is DELIBERATELY DEFERRED until this task ships, and no task should presume either answer before then. The reason is that this task changes the answer: today a bare deletion would cost consumers retry, telemetry and refusal classification, which makes keeping the wrapper look cheaper; once cartouche has all three, deletion becomes close to free and the trade-off mostly evaporates. Deciding before that is deciding against a constraint that is about to stop existing.

Sequencing note the implementer does not need to act on but should know: onchain pins cartouche as a Hex dependency (`{:cartouche, "~> 0.6"}`, onchain/mix.exs:43; lockfile at 0.8.0), not a path dep. So this lands and ships in cartouche first; onchain adopts on a lockfile bump. Nothing is broken in between, because onchain keeps its own implementation until the commit that removes it.

task.title: DEX swap routing (optimal path across pools)
acceptance_criteria: Approach (a/b/c) chosen with a documented rationale in CHANGELOG + module @moduledoc
Onchain.DEX.Router returns an optimal-path result for at least Uniswap v2/v3-style pools given token in/out + amount
Unit tests cover path selection; integration test (env-gated) against a real pool set
Public functions carry Descripex api() annotations + @spec
task.body: Find optimal swap paths across DEX pools (Uniswap, Curve, Balancer). Three approaches to evaluate before committing: (a) Rust routing libs via onchain_evm, (b) Elixir with revm for local simulation of candidate routes, (c) QuickBEAM + Uniswap v3 SDK (see onchain_js Task 3). Primary consumer: ccxt_ex when it adds DEX trading. High design surface — the approach choice is the core judgment call; prototype before building out. Include tests.
task.implemented: Onchain.DEX.Router: route/5 (optimal path), quote_pool/4, amount_out_v2/4. All three scoped approaches (a Rust/onchain_evm, b revm, c QuickBEAM) rejected — each pulls a native dep onchain can't take and inverts the dep graph. Chosen: pure-Elixir analytic v2 (canonical getAmountOut) + on-chain v3 QuoterV2 quoteExactInputSingle eth_call. task.title: defrpc macro — codegen named JSON-RPC wrappers from declarative specs
acceptance_criteria: Macro lives in Onchain.RPC (or a private helper module); NimbleOptions schema documents the public contract
Existing 11 wrappers reimplemented through it with byte-identical public behavior (returns, error shapes, descripex hints, dialyzer story unchanged)

task.body: The 11 existing Onchain.RPC.* wrappers follow a near-identical shape: per-arg validation + param construction + do_rpc(method, params, to_signet_opts(opts)) + an identical bang variant + a Descripex api() annotation. A defrpc macro expands a declaration like `defrpc :block_number, "eth_blockNumber", decode: :hex_unsigned, description: "..."` into the full function + bang + api() + @spec. Precedents that disprove the macros-are-scary objection: Phoenix.Router, Ecto.Schema, Absinthe.Schema — defrpc faces strictly less variance. The knob-growth failure mode is solved by NimbleOptions: the validate!/2 schema IS the macro's contract; adding a knob requires changing the schema, making drift visible. Variance to handle: per-arg validators, nested-map params, literal extra params, filter-key whitelist (eth_get_logs), :decode pass-through, descripex returns: variation. If a case doesn't fit, follow Ecto and add a sibling macro (defrpc_with_filter) rather than overloading defrpc.
