task.title: Spike: measure whether per-call tokio runtime creation costs anything before reusing one
acceptance_criteria: A measurement reports runtime-construction time as a share of total `simulate_call` wall time against a real archive node, for a cheap call and an expensive one
The finding is written down as a number, and the task is either closed as not-worth-doing or converted into an implementation task that names the design chosen
If an implementation is proposed, it states what happens when several simulations run concurrently on dirty schedulers — a single shared `current_thread` runtime must be shown not to serialize them
out_of_scope: Implementing the shared runtime before the measurement exists
task.body:
Rescoped 2026-08-22 from "lazy-init a single current_thread runtime" to a measurement spike, because the original task asserted a benefit nobody measured and proposed a design that may be a regression.

`build_fork_db` builds a `tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()` per call and hands it to `WrapDatabaseAsync::with_runtime`, which takes ownership of it for the fork's lifetime. Constructing that runtime is on the order of microseconds; the fork it serves then issues dozens of JSON-RPC reads at milliseconds each for every account and storage slot the execution touches. The claim that this is worth optimizing has no number behind it, and the previous scores (b=8, u=7) were set as if it did.

The proposed fix also has a hazard the original task did not mention: `with_runtime` owns the runtime, so sharing one `current_thread` runtime across NIF calls means `block_on` from several dirty-scheduler threads driving the same single-threaded reactor. That can serialize concurrent simulations — a throughput regression traded for a microsecond saving.

Measure first. If runtime construction is not a visible share of wall time, close this and say so.
task.implemented: Landed by grok via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787394202843-b9b972f8, 39416686e65645adb79e5d930e1ee5e9de5fc354).

task.title: Gate the Rust half: run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy` from `mix ci`
acceptance_criteria: `mix precommit.full` (alias `mix ci`) runs `cargo test` over both crates and fails the gate on a failing Rust test — today all 21 of them are ungated and a Rust-only regression lands green
`mix ci` also runs clippy over both crates and fails the gate on a lint, in the same way the Elixir analyzers already do
Both crates are clippy-clean at the chosen lint level — a gate that is added while already red is not added
A lint that would catch a genuinely fallible `.expect()` / `.unwrap()` creeping into either crate is enabled, since that is the residual concern left by superseded Task 31
Each check degrades with a clear message when its toolchain component is absent, rather than failing as if the code were bad

The gate denies `clippy::unwrap_used` and does NOT deny `clippy::expect_used` — measured 2026-08-22, the production regions of both crates hold zero `.unwrap()` and nine `.expect()`, every one of the latter in the class superseded Task 31 adjudicated infallible. Denying both buys nine `#[allow]` annotations and no safety; denying `unwrap_used` alone catches the next genuinely fallible call at zero annotation cost
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Re-introducing GitHub Actions — if prebuilt artifacts need CI back, that decision belongs to Task 53

Adding either step to `mix check.dispatch` — harness worktrees start with no `target/`, so a cold Rust build there would be paid on every dispatch. The dispatch hint stays static-only and the reviewer runs focused tests
Writing new Rust tests — this task gates the ones Tasks 28 and 29 already added
task.body:
Rewritten 2026-08-22: the original task said "add cargo clippy to CI", and this repo has no CI. There is no `.github/` directory; the workflows were removed family-wide on 2026-08-22 and `CLAUDE.md` states that `mix ci` is the only gate there is. Adding clippy therefore means adding it to `mix precommit.full`, not to a workflow file.

Both crates are analyzed by nothing today, while the Elixir half runs credo, dialyzer, doctor, ex_dna, reach, sobelow and a coverage threshold. Roughly 2,200 lines of Rust — the half that can abort the VM — is the unlinted part.

The lint selection matters more than the fact of running clippy: superseded Task 31 established that the existing `.expect()` calls are infallible by construction, so the value here is catching the *next* one that is not, which is what a `clippy::unwrap_used` / `expect_used` style lint does mechanically and a per-task reviewer does not.

**Widened 2026-08-22 from clippy-only to clippy + `cargo test`, on the operator's call.** Tasks 28 and 29 added 21 crate-level tests (14 in `onchain_evm`, 7 in `onchain_solidity`) and `mix ci` runs none of them — it runs `mix test.json` for the Elixir half only. The orchestrator had to invoke both cargo suites by hand to check the integrated base after those two landed, which is precisely the manual whole-surface sweep that is supposed to be encoded as a gate instead. Same alias, same file, same reviewer as the clippy change, so this is one task rather than a sibling.

**Cost measured 2026-08-22 on the operator's machine, so the implementer does not have to guess** — a harness worktree is always cold and cannot produce an honest warm number. Cold `target/`, warm cargo registry: `cargo test` on `onchain_evm` (the revm + alloy crate) **43 s**, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` afterwards **21 s**, and the test-profile `target/` costs **1.3 GB** on disk. Warm, both are about a second. The earlier claim in this body that a cold run costs "minutes" was wrong — the real number is under a minute, and the disk footprint is the more notable cost.

**Lint selection is measured, not assumed.** The production regions — everything above `#[cfg(test)]` — hold zero `.unwrap()` and nine `.expect()`: eight `map_put` calls with statically valid terms plus one `FRONTIER starts at block 0`, exactly the infallible-by-construction set Task 31 already adjudicated. So `unwrap_used` can be denied outright today with no annotation churn, while denying `expect_used` would only add nine `#[allow]`s that document nothing new. Test code must be exempted explicitly, and this is where a naive implementation fails: a `[lints.clippy]` entry in `Cargo.toml` applies crate-wide, and `cargo clippy --all-targets` lints test targets too, so denying `unwrap_used` without an exemption reddens roughly **72** call sites at once — 16 in `lib.rs`'s own `mod tests`, 8 in `onchain_solidity`, and 48 in `native/onchain_evm/src/semantics_verification.rs`, which Task 56 landed on 2026-08-22. Note that last file carries no internal `#[cfg(test)]`: it is gated at its declaration in `lib.rs` (`#[cfg(test)] mod semantics_verification;`), so a scan that looks for an in-file `#[cfg(test)]` marker will misclassify all 48 as production. A crate-root `#![cfg_attr(test, allow(clippy::unwrap_used))]`, or the allow on the module, is the intended shape.

Both crates are clippy-clean at default levels under `-D warnings` as of this measurement, so the gate is not being added while red.

Follow the alias shape already in `mix.exs`: `precommit.full` dispatches to captured functions (`&agents_check/1`, `&advisory_freshness/1`), which is where the graceful-degradation message for an absent `cargo` or `clippy` component belongs.

task.title: Stop leaking Rust `Debug` renderings into Elixir error and type strings
acceptance_criteria: A syntax error reaches Elixir as a readable message with file position and expected-token information, not as a `Diagnostic { loc: File(0, 58, 62), level: Error, ty: ParserError, ... }` Debug dump
An unsupported type or expression yields a stable, documented placeholder or a tagged error rather than a Rust `Debug` rendering of the parse node
A test asserts the shape of a parse-error message and fails if a Debug rendering reappears
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Widening which Solidity syntax is supported — that is Task 59
The stack-overflow guard — that is Task 32
task.body:
Four `format!("{:?}", ...)` fallbacks render internal solang-parser types straight into strings that cross the NIF boundary: the diagnostic list at lib.rs:147, the type fallback at :1138, and the two expression fallbacks at :1154 and :1166.

Reproduced 2026-08-22. Parsing a contract that uses `transient` (Solidity 0.8.24) returns:

    {:error, {:parse_error, "Diagnostic { loc: File(0, 58, 62), level: Error, ty: ParserError, message: \"unrecognised token 'lock', expected \\\"(\\\", ...\", notes: [] }"}}

The useful part — a position and an expected-token list — is in there, wrapped in a struct dump with escaped quotes that no caller can reasonably read or match on. The type and expression fallbacks have the same shape: a caller receives a Rust enum's Debug form as if it were a Solidity type name.

Note the separation: *that* `transient` fails to parse at all is a parser-coverage question and belongs to Task 59. *How* that failure is reported is this task, and it is worth fixing regardless of which parser the crate ends up on.
task.implemented: Fixed by the solar-parse migration (Task 61). All four format!("{:?}", ..) sites named in the body are gone — grep for format!("{:?}" in native/onchain_solidity/src/lib.rs returns nothing. Parse errors now cross the NIF boundary as rustc-style diagnostics carrying file position and an expected-token list. The stated reproduction (transient) no longer errors at all; it parses. Regression pinned in test/onchain/solidity_test.exs asserting the message locates the failure and contains no Diagnostic{...}/loc: File(...) rendering.

task.title: Mine `defi-skills:intent-to-transaction` action surface for `onchain_evm` simulation coverage
acceptance_criteria: A 'Proposed additions from defi-skills mining' section lands in this ROADMAP listing each candidate task with D/B/U scores and which defi-skills action(s) motivated it.
The user merges accepted entries into Standalone Tasks or a new bundle.
task.body:
Planted 2026-04-30 from a cartouche session that surveyed cross-repo applicability of the `defi-skills` skill. Self-contained discovery exercise — execute it from a fresh `onchain_evm` Claude Code session so this repo's CLAUDE.md, hooks, and revm fixtures are loaded.

Prompt for the executing session:

> Invoke `/defi-skills:intent-to-transaction` to load the skill, then run `defi-skills actions --json` to enumerate the supported action surface (~50 actions across Aave, Uniswap, Lido, Compound, Balancer, Pendle, EigenLayer, Curve, MakerDAO, Rocket Pool, Fibrous, WETH).
>
> Map relevant actions to `onchain_evm`'s scope: simulation harness coverage — can `revm` + Alloy ABI parsing simulate the unsigned transactions defi-skills builds end-to-end (the approval transaction and the action transaction in sequence), surface revert reasons cleanly, and produce useful state-diff output? Propose a differential-test pattern: build with defi-skills -> simulate with `Onchain.EVM.simulate_batch/2` -> assert state changes (token balance deltas, approval allowance, log emissions). Identify any defi-skills action shape that the current `simulate_batch` API can't represent (e.g. unusual fork-DB requirements, value-bearing calls, multi-tx sequencing limits).
>
> For each gap or coverage opportunity, propose a ROADMAP entry with D/B/U scoring per `~/.claude/includes/task-prioritization.md`. Output: a "Proposed additions from defi-skills mining" section the user reviews before merging into the appropriate bundle or `Standalone Tasks`.
>
> Read-only exercise — discovery + scoring only, no `Onchain.EVM` / Rust code edits in this task itself. The skill is already installed (`pip install defi-skills`); no new deps. Companion tasks were planted in `hieroglyph`, `onchain`, and `onchain_aave` ROADMAPs the same day.

CLOSED 2026-08-22 during a backlog review. This is not a task, it is a prompt for producing tasks, and it cannot be executed by the pipeline that would receive it:
- Its deliverable is "a section lands in this ROADMAP", but agents no longer write roadmap files at all — reviewers emit `proposed_tasks` and the orchestrator files them.
- Its acceptance criteria terminate in "the user merges accepted entries", which no implementer or reviewer can check.

task.title: Adopt `rustler_precompiled` for both native crates — artifacts cross-built locally with cargo-zigbuild
acceptance_criteria: `mix ci` is green on this checkout with NO release existing for the current version — this is the criterion the first attempt failed and the one that pins the whole task. The pre-commit gate compiles, so a load path that unconditionally tries to download 404s and the code can never be committed. The library's own checkout must source-build while `checksum-*.exs` is absent

A checksum MISMATCH always fails the load. A MISSING `checksum-*.exs` fails the load for a package installed from Hex — where `files:` guarantees it ships — and source-builds in this repo's own checkout. Distinguishing the two is what makes the task buildable before its first release; do not collapse them
`@version` in `mix.exs` is bumped to `0.6.0`, so `:base_url` points at a tag that can still be cut. v0.5.1 is already published on Hex and cannot be re-released with new code
Target resolution is unit-tested without a live release: a supported host resolves to download mode, an unsupported target and `ONCHAIN_EVM_BUILD=1` each resolve to source-build
A committed build script cross-builds every shipped target for both crates from a single macOS host, with no CI service involved
The shipped `:targets` list is exactly the set the build script actually produces — no target is declared that cannot be built
`RUSTLER_PRECOMPILED_FORCE_BUILD_ALL=1` is documented in the README and verified to actually rebuild from source
`checksum-*.exs` is listed in the `files:` field of `mix.exs` so it ships in the Hex package — generating it needs live artifacts and belongs to Task 62
The release procedure is written down as an ordered runbook: build -> upload -> download+checksum -> commit -> `mix hex.publish`
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Cutting the GitHub Release, uploading artifacts, generating the committed checksum files, and `mix hex.publish` — all of Task 62. Those need org credentials and an irreversible publish, so no agent can do them and no criterion here may depend on a live artifact URL
Any Windows target — see the body; Windows consumers build from source
Re-introducing GitHub Actions or any other CI service
Adding riscv64 / armv7 targets — the build script should make them a one-line addition, but they are not shipped here
task.body:
Hex-release blocker (see "Path to hex.pm Release"). Without prebuilt artifacts, every consumer of `onchain_evm` needs a working Rust toolchain plus several minutes to compile `revm` + `alloy` + `solang-parser` from source.

**Mechanism settled by the operator on 2026-08-22: no CI. Artifacts are cross-built locally with `cargo-zigbuild` and uploaded to a GitHub Release with `gh release upload`.** This repo has no `.github/` directory — the Actions workflows were removed family-wide and `mix ci` is the only gate there is. That does not block this task: GitHub *Releases* are independent of GitHub *Actions*, so a release still works as the artifact host that `rustler_precompiled`'s `:base_url` points at. Do not re-introduce a CI service, and do not add a workflow file.

Wrap both `native/onchain_evm` (revm, alloy) and `native/onchain_solidity` (alloy-json-abi, solang-parser) with `RustlerPrecompiled.use/1` instead of plain `Rustler`.

**Ship exactly these five targets**, all reachable with `cargo-zigbuild` from one Apple Silicon Mac:

- `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`
- `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`
- `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`

Pin the glibc floor by suffixing the target triple, e.g. `--target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.28`; unsuffixed, Zig picks a default that drifts with the Zig release. Note that `-C target-feature=+crt-static` against glibc is not supported by `zig cc`, and an invalid glibc suffix silently falls back instead of erroring — so assert the produced artifact's requirements rather than trusting the build to fail loudly.

**Windows is deliberately not shipped.** Two independent reasons, either sufficient: `cargo-zigbuild` supports only Linux, macOS and Windows *gnu* targets — `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` is explicitly unsupported — and unlike Unix, where NIF symbols resolve at load time, a Windows build genuinely links against the `erl_nif` import library, which a cross-build from macOS has no clean way to source. `rustler_precompiled` falls back to a source build when no artifact matches the host, so Windows consumers still work; they just need a toolchain. Do not add a Windows target "for completeness" without solving both problems.

Deliver a committed `scripts/build-precompiled.sh` that loops both crates over the target list and emits the correctly-named artifacts. The release runbook is ordered and the order matters — the checksum step *downloads* what was uploaded, so artifacts must be live first:

1. tag and push
2. run the build script
3. `gh release create` / `gh release upload` the `.so`/`.dylib` artifacts
4. `mix rustler_precompiled.download <Module> --all --print` to fetch them back and write `checksum-Elixir.<Module>.exs`
5. commit the checksum file
6. `mix hex.publish`

Add both checksum files to the `files:` field in `mix.exs` — if they are missing from the package, every consumer silently loses checksum verification.

Verify `RUSTLER_PRECOMPILED_FORCE_BUILD_ALL=1` actually forces a source build; the per-package `:force_build` option and any per-package env var spelling should be confirmed against the installed version's docs rather than assumed.

Trade-offs, stated honestly: the release becomes a manual local ritual with no build provenance or attestation, and it is reproducible only on a machine with the Zig toolchain installed. That is the accepted cost of not running CI.

---

**Re-scoped 2026-08-22 after the first attempt was rejected (run `run-1787383438157-8ee2346b`, cursor).** The rejection was correct and the defect was in this task, not in the agent's work: the original criteria required artifacts to be downloadable from a GitHub Release, but cutting that release needs org credentials and an irreversible `mix hex.publish`, so no dispatched agent can satisfy them. Worse, the two halves deadlocked — the pre-commit gate compiles, compilation tried to download, no release existed, 404, so the code could not be committed to *reach* a release. The release half is now Task 62; this task ends at "green with no release yet."

**The retained branch `harness/run-1787383438157-8ee2346b` already carries most of this and is worth building on rather than restarting.** Two commits, 507 insertions: `lib/onchain/precompiled.ex` (shared opts, target resolution, `force_build?`), `scripts/build-precompiled.sh` (192 lines — the reviewer confirmed it really cross-built all five targets for both crates, and it already guards the silent glibc-suffix fallback), `test/onchain/precompiled_test.exs`, plus the `mix.exs` / README / `.sobelow-skips` changes. What it lacks is exactly the deadlock fix: `force_build?` consults only the target and `ONCHAIN_EVM_BUILD`, never whether a checksum file exists, so on a supported host with no release it resolves to download and 404s.

task.title: Behavioral golden tests for EVM fork+execute — safety net before the revm/alloy major bump
acceptance_criteria: Onchain.EVM fork+execute paths covered to >=95% (mix test.json --cover, critical tier)
Fork integration tests pin fixed block numbers; a known view call returns its known on-chain value
Revert path asserts {:error, {:evm_revert, reason}}; error taxonomy (:fork_error/:timeout/:evm_error) asserted per Task 49
State-override (balance/nonce/storage) effect on simulated result asserted
No exact-gas equality assertions; gas asserted as present/plausible only
Full check_command gate green; integration tests run (not silently skipped) against the archive node
out_of_scope: Any change to native/onchain_evm Rust code or Cargo deps (that is the next task)
onchain_solidity crate / Onchain.Solidity tests
Trace module coverage
task.body:
The next task (revm 19→41 + alloy 0.7→2.1 major bump) rewrites the security-sensitive native EVM execution crate. Its whole risk is *silent* behavior drift in the fork+simulate path. Before that rewrite, lock current behavior in deterministic golden tests so the migration has a regression net it must keep green.

Expand `Onchain.EVM`'s test coverage — especially the fork+execute integration paths (currently only exercised under `--include integration`) — to the critical tier (>=95%, this is EVM execution / money-adjacent simulation). Pin fork tests to FIXED block numbers against the archive node so results are deterministic across runs.

Cover at minimum: a known view-function call against a well-known mainnet contract at a pinned block returns its known on-chain value; a call that reverts surfaces `{:error, {:evm_revert, _}}` with the revert reason; state-override (balance / nonce / storage) changes the simulated result as expected; and the error taxonomy from Task 49 (`:fork_error` on connect-refused, `:timeout`, `:evm_error`) classifies correctly.

CRITICAL — lock SEMANTICS, not volatile internals. Assert return-value correctness, revert reasons, error tags, and state-override effects. Do NOT assert exact gas figures by equality: gas accounting can legitimately change across revm major versions (EIP updates), so an exact-gas golden would force a false failure during the migration. Assert gas is present and plausible (> 0 / within a wide tolerance) only.

Modernize the revm/alloy stack in `native/onchain_evm` to clear the last open Dependabot alert: lru < 0.16.3 (GHSA-rhfx-m35p-ff5j). lru is transitive via alloy-provider, and `lru ^0.16` (the fix line) first appears at alloy-provider 1.8.3 — which forces revm off 19 too (revm's `alloydb` feature re-exports alloy types, so revm and alloy must move together). Target the latest stable revm (~41.x) and alloy (~2.x).

Keep the Elixir-facing NIF surface IDENTICAL — same atoms, same return shapes, same error taxonomy (`:evm_revert` / `:evm_error` / `:fork_error` / `:timeout`). Task 54's golden tests are the regression net; they must stay green (allowing for legitimate gas-accounting differences, which 54 deliberately does not pin by equality). No change to `Onchain.EVM`'s public API.

Known breaking changes to migrate (verify against current docs/source — these are the API seams, not line-by-line instructions):
- revm DB reorg: `revm::db::{AlloyDB, CacheDB}` moved out of the monolith into the `revm-database` crate (and `AlloyDB` may now require an explicit async-runtime wrapper). Find the new import paths.
- revm EVM builder: `Evm::builder()...build()` was replaced by the `Context` builder pattern (`Context::mainnet()....build_mainnet()` + `.modify_tx_chained()` / transact API). Rebuild the execute path on it.
- alloy provider transport generic collapsed: `RootProvider<Transport, Network>` → `RootProvider<Network>` in alloy 1.x; `ProviderBuilder::new().on_client(client)` was removed/renamed — use the current builder + `connect_*`.
- `TxEnv` / `BlockEnv` moved from struct-field construction to a builder; verify field renames.
- `ExecutionResult` / `HaltReason` enum shape shifts — re-match exhaustively.
- Task 49's `classify_transport_error` downcasts the underlying `reqwest::Error` through the alloy/revm `Error::source()` chain. Re-verify that chain is still walkable on new alloy (the tasks.toml note at the Task-30/49 line flags this fragility); keep `is_timeout()`/`is_connect()` classification working, fall back to the display-string heuristic only if the source chain no longer preserves it.

Bump the native crate version 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 to match the Elixir package. Use `cargo update -p lru` (or the alloy bump's natural resolution) to confirm the lockfile lands lru >= 0.16.3.

task.title: Validate the documented `Onchain.EVM` option surface at the Elixir boundary, not in the NIF
acceptance_criteria: Every option named in Onchain.EVM's public typespecs, plus the `calls` argument of simulate_batch/2, returns a tagged `{:error, {atom, term}}` for malformed input without invoking the NIF
A test enumerates the documented option surface and fails when a documented option has no Elixir-layer guard, rather than asserting only the four known cases
simulate_batch/2 returns a tagged error for a non-list `calls` and for elements that are not 2-tuples — no silent {:ok, []}, no escaping FunctionClauseError
Each of the four premises above is either reproduced before its fix or recorded as no-longer-reproducing
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Rust-side changes under native/ — panic removal is Task 31, source-size limits are Task 32
New public functions or changes to the success-path return shapes
task.body:
Close the "NIF catches what Elixir should" class as an invariant rather than patching its four known instances. Every option `Onchain.EVM` documents in its public typespecs must be validated at the Elixir layer and rejected with a tagged `{:error, {tag, term}}` tuple, so a malformed option never crosses the NIF boundary and never surfaces as a bare-string `{:evm_error, "..."}` from Rust or as a raised exception escaping the `{:ok, _} | {:error, _}` contract.

Known instances — Tasks 45, 46, 47 and 48, superseded by this one — all discovered 2026-04-22 during onchain_aave Task 41 (first real consumer integration) — treat each as a premise to re-confirm against current code before fixing, not as established behavior:
- `simulate_batch/2` accepts any `Enumerable`, so `%{}` returns a silent `{:ok, []}`; non-2-tuple elements raise `FunctionClauseError` out of `validate_calls/1`.
- `maybe_put_value/2` checks only `is_binary/1`, so `""` and `"not-a-hex"` reach Rust as an invalid-U256 error.
- `maybe_put_state_overrides/2` does not enforce the all-strings rule its own `@type state_overrides` documents; atom keys and integer values fail in Rust.
- `parse_hex_block/2` applies no upper bound, so a >u64 value fails as `invalid param type: block_number` in the NIF.

Re-confirmed 2026-08-22 against `lib/onchain/evm/params.ex`: all four premises still reproduce, and none of the four has been quietly fixed since 2026-04-22. `validate_calls/1` still reduces over any `Enumerable` with a bare `fn {addr, data}` head; `maybe_put_value/2` still guards on `is_binary/1` alone; `maybe_put_state_overrides/2` still guards on `is_map/1` alone; `parse_hex_block/2` still calls `Integer.parse(rest, 16)` with no upper bound. Note the code lives in `Onchain.EVM.Params`, the cover-able sibling module, not in `Onchain.EVM` — the NIF shell is excluded from coverage, the validation is not.

This is the second round of the same class (Bundle 1 was the first), which is the reason to ship the invariant and its enumerating test instead of four more point fixes. The deliverable that closes the class is a test that walks the documented option surface itself, so a newly documented option without an Elixir-layer guard fails the suite rather than becoming a Round 3 task.

task.title: Populate the fork's block environment and stop state overrides from clobbering un-fetched accounts
acceptance_criteria: Multicall3 getBlockNumber()/getCurrentBlockTimestamp() through simulate_call return the forked block's real number and timestamp, for a numeric :block pin, for block: "latest", and when :block is omitted
An Aave V3 supply simulated through simulate_batch against a forked mainnet archive node succeeds instead of reverting with Panic(0x11)

A state override of balance, nonce or storage on a contract that has not been touched yet leaves its deployed code and unspecified fields intact — balanceOf on WETH still answers after %{weth => %{"storage" => "{}"}}
Rust or Elixir tests pin the block-environment fields and the override-preserves-code behaviour, and fail against the current implementation
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Deriving SpecId from the forked block or a chain-aware hardfork schedule (documented limitation at native/onchain_evm/src/lib.rs:556)
Adding block-environment override options for callers to fake number/timestamp
task.body:
Simulation currently executes against a fork whose state is real but whose block environment is not. `Context::mainnet()` is built with revm's default `BlockEnv` at every site in `native/onchain_evm/src/lib.rs` (do_simulate_call, do_simulate_transaction, do_simulate_batch), so contracts observe `block.number == 0` and `block.timestamp == 1` regardless of the `:block` option. Measured against a mainnet archive node at head 25_808_519: Multicall3 `getBlockNumber()` returned 0 and `getCurrentBlockTimestamp()` returned 1 for `block: "latest"`, `block: <number>` and no block option alike.

This silently breaks every time-dependent protocol, which is most of DeFi. An Aave V3 `supply` reverts with `Panic(0x11)` (arithmetic underflow) because `MathUtils.calculateLinearInterest` computes `block.timestamp - reserve.lastUpdateTimestamp` against a 1970 clock. Reads that ignore time return correct values, so the failure looks like a caller mistake rather than a missing environment — the module's own headline use cases ("test liquidation thresholds", "run what-if scenarios") are the ones that break.

The second defect shares a root cause with the first's blast radius: `apply_state_overrides` seeds `info` from `db.cache.accounts`, which on a fresh ForkDB is empty because fork state is fetched lazily. `unwrap_or_default()` therefore yields an empty `AccountInfo`, and `insert_account_info` writes that back — replacing the account instead of amending it. Overriding any field of an account that has not yet been touched drops its deployed code: after `%{weth => %{"storage" => ~s({})}}`, `balanceOf` on WETH returns `"0x"`. Overrides must be applied on top of the account as the fork would resolve it, not on top of a default.

Fetch the forked block's header once per simulation and populate number, timestamp, basefee, gas limit, coinbase and prevrandao from it; keep honouring `:block` so a historical pin executes in that block's environment. The pre-existing SpecId limitation documented at lib.rs:556 is a separate concern and stays as it is.

task.title: Spike: pick a Solidity parser frontend that understands post-0.8.24 syntax
acceptance_criteria: The gap is quantified, not asserted: a list of Solidity language features shipped since solang-parser's last release that this crate cannot parse, each with a source snippet and the observed failure
At least two actively maintained candidate frontends are evaluated against that list, plus the option of staying on solang-parser, with the cost of each stated

The evaluation states what a migration would do to the crate's public output shape — selectors, canonical type strings, NatSpec attachment — since Onchain.Contract.Generator consumes it at compile time
The spike ends in a written recommendation with a D/B/U-scored follow-up task if migration is recommended, or a recorded decision to stay if it is not
Read-only: no parser swap is performed in this task
out_of_scope: Performing the migration itself
The stack-overflow guard (Task 32) and the Debug-rendering cleanup (Task 44), both of which are worth doing on whichever parser is chosen
task.body:
`onchain_solidity` pins `solang-parser = "0.3"`. 0.3.5 is the latest release and it was published 2025-06-22 — over a year stale, from a project that has effectively stopped maintaining the standalone parser. `cargo outdated` reports the crate as up to date precisely because there is nothing newer to move to, so the staleness is invisible to the dependency tooling.

The consequence is already reachable, reproduced 2026-08-22 on this checkout: a contract declaring `uint256 transient lock;` (EIP-1153 transient storage, Solidity 0.8.24, shipped March 2024) fails to parse with `unrecognised token 'lock'`. The keyword does not appear anywhere in solang-parser 0.3.5's grammar. Anything written against a modern compiler is a candidate for the same failure, and the failure lands at **compile time** for consumers of `Onchain.Contract.Generator` — a `.sol` file that solc accepts simply cannot be code-generated from.

This is scoped as a spike rather than a migration because the answer is genuinely open: `parse_abi_json` (the compiled-ABI path) is unaffected and is already the recommended path, so the honest question is how much the source-parsing path is worth investing in versus documenting its ceiling. Candidates to weigh include the actively developed Rust Solidity frontends (solar, slang) and staying put. Decide with the feature list in hand.

task.title: Derive the EVM revision from the forked block instead of always executing under one modern SpecId
acceptance_criteria: A simulation pinned to a pre-Cancun block executes under that block's EVM revision, demonstrated by an opcode or behaviour that differs across the fork boundary rather than by reading the configured value back

The mapping from block number to revision is driven by a chain-aware hardfork schedule, and a chain the schedule does not know is rejected or clearly documented rather than silently treated as mainnet
An integration test pins at least one historical block on either side of a hardfork against the archive node, and flunks rather than skips when RPC configuration is absent
The KNOWN LIMITATION comment at native/onchain_evm/src/lib.rs:556 is removed or rewritten to describe what actually remains
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Populating the block environment fields (number, timestamp, basefee, gas limit, coinbase, prevrandao) — that is Task 58, which this depends on
Supporting chains beyond those the module already targets
task.body:
Every `Context::mainnet()` site in `native/onchain_evm/src/lib.rs` executes under revm's configured modern revision regardless of which block the fork is pinned to. The code says so itself at lib.rs:556 ("KNOWN LIMITATION ... applies to every `Context::mainnet()` site below too"), and Task 58 explicitly declares it out of scope so that the block-environment fix stays reviewable.

Nothing tracked it, which is why this exists: a limitation documented only in a code comment and in another task's `out_of_scope` is invisible to the backlog, and this one is the same class as Task 58 — the fork's state is real, its execution environment is not.

It matters for exactly the use case a historical `:block` pin implies. Replaying a transaction from before a hardfork under today's rules can change gas accounting, opcode availability and refund behaviour, so a simulation of a historical block can succeed where the real transaction failed, or price differently than it did. Reads that touch none of the changed semantics still return correct values, so as with Task 58 the failure looks like a caller mistake rather than a missing environment.

Sequenced after Task 58 deliberately: 58 fetches the forked block's header, which is also where the block number a revision decision keys off comes from, and landing both against the same header fetch avoids two independent implementations of it.

task.title: Migrate Solidity source parsing from solang-parser to solar-parse
acceptance_criteria: The four sources in native/onchain_solidity/PARSER_FRONTEND_SPIKE.md parse successfully through Onchain.Solidity.parse_sol/1
Existing source-parser and Generator tests pass without output-shape changes
Tests compare source and JSON-ABI signatures, selectors, topics, canonical nested types, and NatSpec attachment

task.body:
Task 59 measured solang-parser 0.3.5 against Solidity 0.8.36 and recommended solar-parse 0.2.0. The spike is native/onchain_solidity/PARSER_FRONTEND_SPIKE.md; this task is the migration it scored D:6/B:8/U:7.

solang-parser's documented ceiling is Solidity 0.8.22. Four forms that solc 0.8.36 accepts fail today (`transient` state variables; literal / constant / erc7201 custom storage layout). Those failures are parser grammar gaps, not this crate's AST adapter, and they abort `Onchain.Contract.Generator` at compile time. Task 59 already pinned the four failures as a Rust characterization test in native/onchain_solidity/src/lib.rs — invert that test; do not leave it asserting rejection.

Replace the source parser with released `solar-parse`. Keep `parse_abi_json` on alloy-json-abi. The frontend is private: do not expose Solar AST values, and do not change the terms returned by `parse_sol`, `__parse_sol_root__`, or `__extract_sol_imports__`.

Preserve the existing output contract:

- selectors and event topics stay Keccak-256 of the canonical signature computed in this crate (`tiny-keccak`); do not substitute parser-provided semantic hashes without a separate compatibility proof
- payable addresses and contract references become `address`; enums become `uint8`; structs expand to tuples / `tuple` parameter maps with `:components`
- `:return_type` remains a parenthesized comma-separated tuple string accepted by `Onchain.ABI.decode_response/2`
- NatSpec stays the existing function-level `%{notice, params, returns}` map — either keep `extract_doc_comments` or prove byte-for-byte parity before using Solar's DocComments
- source order, root-contract filtering, import extraction, structs, enums, constants, constructor shape, mutability strings, and `{:error, {:parse_error, reason}}` stay as they are

Solar 0.2.0 required Rust 1.95 in the spike; this host is on 1.96. Update the crate lock and any documented toolchain floor the new closure needs.

Task 29 also writes native/onchain_solidity/src/lib.rs (unit tests for the current adapter). Write-set overlap will serialize the two; if 29 lands first, keep its selector/canonicalization/NatSpec pins and rewrite only the syntax-rejection case.

task.title: Cut the v0.6.0 release — upload precompiled NIF artifacts, commit checksums, publish to Hex
acceptance_criteria: `scripts/build-precompiled.sh` has produced all ten artifacts (five targets x two crates) for v0.6.0 on this machine

`mix rustler_precompiled.download Onchain.EVM --all --print` and the same for `Onchain.Solidity` both succeed against the live release and write `checksum-Elixir.Onchain.EVM.exs` / `checksum-Elixir.Onchain.Solidity.exs`

Both checksum files are committed, and `mix ci` is green with them present — the load path now DOWNLOADS on this host instead of source-building, which is the first time that half is exercised end to end
Deleting a checksum file is confirmed to fail a Hex-installed load rather than silently source-building, and corrupting one entry is confirmed to fail the load
`mix hex.publish` has published 0.6.0, and a scratch project depending on `{:onchain_evm, "~> 0.6"}` compiles with no Rust toolchain invoked
out_of_scope: Any change to the precompiled wiring, the build script, or the target list — that is Task 53 and must be landed and green first
Adding targets beyond the five Task 53 ships
Publishing any other package in the onchain stack
task.body:
Operator-gated by construction — this is the half of the original Task 53 that no dispatched agent can perform. It needs push access to the ZenHive org to cut a Release, and it ends in `mix hex.publish`, which is irreversible: a published Hex version can never be replaced, only retired.

**Ordering is not a preference, it is a dependency chain.** The checksum step *downloads* what was uploaded, so the artifacts must be live before checksums can be generated, and the checksums must be committed before publishing or every consumer silently loses verification:

1. Confirm Task 53 is landed and `@version` reads `0.6.0`
2. `scripts/build-precompiled.sh`
3. `git tag v0.6.0 && git push origin v0.6.0`
4. `gh release create v0.6.0` and upload all ten `.so.tar.gz` assets
5. `mix rustler_precompiled.download Onchain.EVM --all --print`, same for `Onchain.Solidity`
6. commit both `checksum-Elixir.*.exs`
7. `mix hex.publish`

**Why the version is 0.6.0 and not 0.5.2:** v0.5.1 is already tagged and published on Hex, so it cannot host new code. The first attempt at Task 53 failed partly on this — its `:base_url` pointed at a v0.5.1 release that could never be created.

Step 4 is the first genuinely public, hard-to-undo action in this repo's history, and step 7 cannot be undone at all. Do not let an agent run either.
task.implemented: Release v0.6.0 cut end to end: build-precompiled.sh produced all ten artifacts, tag v0.6.0 points at e271bd1, GitHub Release ZenHive/onchain_evm carries the ten assets, both checksum-Elixir.*.exs were downloaded from the live release and committed, and mix ci is green with them present. Hex 0.6.0 published (db81646d). Verification round-trip: all ten uploaded assets re-downloaded byte-identical to the local tarballs; GNU targets sit exactly at GLIBC_2.28, musl carries zero GLIBC symbols. Corrupting one checksum entry fails the load with 'the integrity check failed'; deleting deps/onchain_evm/checksum-Elixir.Onchain.EVM.exs in a Hex-installed scratch project fails compilation with 'the precompiled NIF file does not exist in the checksum file' even with cargo on PATH, so there is no silent source-build fallback. The scratch project resolved {:onchain_evm, "~> 0.6"} and, with an empty NIF cache and cargo/rustc stripped from PATH, downloaded both .so archives from the Release and ran Onchain.Solidity.parse_abi_json/1 and parse_sol/1 successfully; the EVM NIF forked mainnet through the local archive node and returned USDC.decimals() = 6.

task.title: Close the assertion gap in the semantics harness: every vector asserted against every key the oracle checks
acceptance_criteria: The LOG VMTest comparator asserts the fixture's `out` and its `post` state, not only gas and log fields — today `revm_matches_official_vm_storage_log_and_gas_vectors` checks all three for `sstore_load_1` and skips both for `log1_nonEmptyMem`, in the same function, on the same fixture format

The asymmetry cannot silently return: a vector's assertion set is derived from what the fixture declares rather than hand-written per case, so a newly committed vector carrying `out`/`post`/`gas` is checked on all of them by construction. This is the point of the task — patching the one LOG call site and leaving the next vector free to under-assert is not a fix

A top-level create *transaction* vector is covered, not only `CREATE_EmptyContractWithStorage`, which exercises the CREATE opcode from inside a CALL. Contract creation as a transaction is a distinct path through the fork configuration

The negative control still fails for every strengthened assertion — a corrupted `out` and a corrupted `post` entry must each be rejected, the same way corrupted storage already is. An assertion that cannot fail is not an assertion
`verification-ledger.json` reflects the widened key set, so the ledger does not claim more agreement than the comparators establish
cargo test passes for both crates and mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Wiring `verify-semantics.sh` into `mix ci` — it needs Docker and the pinned ~GB Kontrol image on the host, which no gate may assume. The reviewer raised this on run run-1787389160672-cbfd01cd; it is declined by design, not deferred
Adding the cargo suites to `mix ci` — that is Task 43
Broadening the vector set beyond the create-transaction gap named above
task.body:
Filed 2026-08-22 by the orchestrator from two reviewer concerns on Task 56's run (run-1787389160672-cbfd01cd, verdict approve with `review_warning`). Merged into one task because they are one defect class, not two patches.

The harness's whole claim is differential: revm is checked against official `ethereum/tests` vectors, with KEVM/Kontrol as the independent oracle. That claim is only as strong as the weakest comparator, and the comparators are uneven. Verified by reading `native/onchain_evm/src/semantics_verification.rs` at 34b41fe:

- `assert_blockchain_vector` asserts status, `output`, `gasUsed`, empty logs, and the full post-state.
- The SSTORE VMTest asserts `out`, `gas`, and `post`.
- The LOG VMTest, sitting in the same test function, asserts `gas` and the log's address/topics/data — and never touches `out` or `post`.

KEVM's GST checking keeps `out`, `gas`, `logs` and `post` for VMTESTS, so for `log1_nonEmptyMem` the claimed oracle agreement is broader than what the Rust comparator establishes. Nothing is wrong today; the gap is that a passing test proves less than it appears to.

The second concern is a coverage gap of the same kind: the committed CREATE vector is `CREATE_EmptyContractWithStorage`, which runs the CREATE opcode inside a CALL. A create transaction configures the fork differently and is not exercised.

Scope this as the invariant, not the instance. Hand-fixing the LOG call site leaves the next contributor free to add a vector that checks two of four keys, and the reviewer of that diff would have no written rule to reject it against. Derive the assertion set from the fixture so under-assertion becomes impossible rather than merely absent.

- **onchain Sleuth** (see onchain/ROADMAP.md Task 62) — compile a custom read-only `.sol` query to bytecode, hand off to `Onchain.Sleuth.query/3` which ships it in an `eth_call` for one-shot execution against live chain state.

**Authority:** the Solidity compiler's own Standard JSON input/output contract
(solidity docs / solc-js) defines semantics here. Third-party Elixir or JS
wrappers are reference material only and never override it. Drive solc through
Standard JSON rather than the legacy string API, so optimizer settings, EVM
version and output selection are expressible.

Dispatch trigger: EVM bytecode is the deliverable, it is a public contract two

task.body: `Onchain.Tempo.Transaction.Builder` `@default_gas_limit` bumped from 200_000 to 500_000 — a stock TIP-20 transfer on Moderato consumes ~272k, so the previous default under-provisioned real transfers. Integration test no longer needs a per-call `gas_limit` override. 500k is a ceiling, not an amount spent — no real-world cost change; just prevents `out of gas` for the common TIP-20 path.
task.implemented: Bumped Builder @default_gas_limit from 200_000 to 500_000 to cover the ~272k a stock TIP-20 transfer consumes on Moderato. Shipped in v0.1.1.

task.title: Replace Faucet fixed-sleep settle with poll loop
acceptance_criteria: fresh_funded_wallet/1 returns as soon as the funding tx is confirmed on-chain (not after a fixed sleep)
Integration suite remains green on Moderato (faucet still funds reliably)
Poll loop respects a configurable timeout / max-iterations to avoid hanging on slow blocks
Unit tests can still skip the wait by passing the existing :settle_ms shortcut (or equivalent zero-poll-time option)
task.body: `Onchain.Tempo.Faucet.fresh_funded_wallet/2` currently sleeps a fixed `@default_settle_ms` (2_500ms) after funding before returning. Replace with a poll loop on `eth_getTransactionCount` or `eth_getBalance` so the helper returns as soon as the funding transaction lands (Moderato blocks ~500ms; the fixed sleep wastes ~2s per integration test). Discovered during the v0.1.1 integration test work and carried forward when the helper was promoted to a public module in v0.2.0.
task.implemented: Replaced the Faucet fixed @default_settle_ms sleep with an eth_getBalance poll loop bounded by a configurable timeout / max-iterations; unit tests retain the zero-wait shortcut. Shipped in PR #1.

task.title: Public `Onchain.Tempo.Faucet` helper for `tempo_fundAddress`
task.body: Promoted the previously test-only `Onchain.Tempo.TestSupport.ModeratoFaucet` (`test/support/moderato_faucet.ex`) into public `Onchain.Tempo.Faucet` at `lib/onchain/tempo/faucet.ex` so downstream consumers writing their own integration suites can reuse the Moderato faucet recipe. Public API: `rpc_url/0` (Moderato default, `TEMPO_RPC_URL` override), `fund_address/2` (thin wrapper around `tempo_fundAddress` JSON-RPC, returns `{:ok, [tx_hash]}`), `fresh_funded_wallet/1` (generates a 32-byte keypair, funds it, sleeps for settlement). Both accept an opts keyword list with `:rpc_url`, `:req_options`, and (for `fresh_funded_wallet/1`) `:settle_ms`. Registered in `OnchainTempo`'s Descripex.Discoverable module list. Integration suite migrated; old test-support helper deleted; new unit tests at `test/onchain/tempo/faucet_test.exs` cover happy/error/transport paths via Req.Test stubs.
task.implemented: Promoted the test-only ModeratoFaucet to public Onchain.Tempo.Faucet (rpc_url/0, fund_address/2, fresh_funded_wallet/1) registered in OnchainTempo's Discoverable list, with Req.Test-stubbed unit tests. Shipped in v0.2.0.

task.title: Migrate signing to Cartouche
task.body: Switched internal signing/recovery aliases from `Signet.Signer.Curvy` / `Signet.Recover` to `Cartouche.Signer.Curvy` / `Cartouche.Recover` in `Onchain.Tempo.Transaction` and `Onchain.Tempo.Transaction.Builder`. Cartouche is ZenHive's fork of signet — drop-in compatible, available transitively via `onchain`. Tightened the `onchain` dep from `~> 0.5` to `~> 0.5.3` to ensure the cartouche-bearing version is resolved. Public API unchanged — purely internal refactor for consumers.

task.title: Stop hardcoding Builder @default_gas_limit — estimate gas per-tx (mirror mppx)
acceptance_criteria: Builder estimates gas via eth_estimateGas when :gas_limit is omitted, with a headroom multiplier
A cold-storage TIP-20 transfer / transferWithMemo on Moderato no longer OOG-reverts at the default
An explicit :gas_limit override is still honored unchanged
Interim: if estimation is deferred, @default_gas_limit is raised to >= 1_000_000 with a comment citing the ~560k measured cost
out_of_scope: Adding the eth_estimateGas RPC wrapper itself (tracked in onchain's roadmap)
Faucet funding changes (the poll now waits on the fee-token balanceOf via eth_call rather than native eth_getBalance, so it no longer depends on gas-vs-pathUSD landing order)
task.body:
`Onchain.Tempo.Transaction.Builder` `@default_gas_limit` (currently 500_000, raised from 200_000 in Task 4 for the then-"~272k" cold TIP-20 transfer) is stale again: a cold-storage TIP-20 transfer on Moderato now measures ~560k, because the chain charges a protocol fee (a Transfer to the `0xfeec…` collector) on the transfer path. At the 500k default these transfers OOG-revert (`gas_used == gas_limit`, status 0) — empirically confirmed: identical transfer reverts at 400k/500k, succeeds at 2M using 560019 gas. This is the second time a static default went stale; the constant chases a moving on-chain number.

Mirror the reference SDK (mppx sizes every transaction via `eth_estimateGas`, not a constant): have the Builder estimate gas per transaction (consuming the `eth_estimateGas` helper being added to `onchain` — cross-repo dependency) with a safety headroom multiplier, instead of a fixed default. Keep an explicit `:gas_limit` override working. As an interim until estimation lands, raise `@default_gas_limit` to >= 1_000_000 (> the measured 560k, < the mppx fee-payer `maxGas` ceiling of 2_000_000) so cold transfers stop reverting.
task.implemented: Builder estimates gas per-tx via Onchain.RPC.eth_estimate_gas (1.25x headroom) when :gas_limit omitted; per-call summed, errors propagate, explicit override honored. Probed Moderato: cold eth_estimateGas=807k captures the protocol fee, so standard estimation suffices. onchain floor ~> 0.9. 21 offline + 4 live Moderato tests (incl. cold transfer confirms), Builder 100% cover.

task.title: Update transport stub off the :cartouche,:client seam after onchain's Req migration

It stubs the onchain RPC transport via onchain's post-migration mechanism and passes
mix.exs onchain requirement covers the migrated onchain version
Full offline suite green
out_of_scope: The onchain transport migration itself (its own roadmap task — must ship first)
Any cartouche change
task.body:
Follow-on to onchain's transport migration (onchain roadmap task: "Migrate HTTP transport off cartouche's removed Finch seams"). cartouche 0.5.0 dropped the `config :cartouche, :client` seam and onchain is moving its own transport off it; once onchain ships, `test/onchain/tempo/transaction/builder_estimate_test.exs` no longer works — it stubs the onchain RPC transport by toggling `Application.{get,put,delete}_env(:cartouche, :client, module)` (its `setup`/`restore_client` helpers, lines ~44-51, plus the `async: false` comment at the top explaining the global-seam toggle).

After onchain ships its new transport-stub seam (Req.Test / function plug, or onchain's own override key), rewrite this test's stubbing to use that mechanism instead of `:cartouche, :client`. Bump the `{:onchain, ...}` requirement in mix.exs to the version that ships the migration if onchain raises its version. Keep the test's intent unchanged (it asserts builder gas-estimate behavior against a stubbed RPC).

task.title: Mutation-grade 0x76 transaction and signing invariants
acceptance_criteria: Property tests cover every 0x76 transaction field, canonical encoding, fee-payer/signing domain, boundary-sized values and malformed inputs
Bytes, hashes and recovered identities are differential-checked against the current official Tempo SDK/specification and a live Moderato success plus relevant error
A reproducible mutation campaign targets field order/indexes, type/domain bytes, fee-payer data, numeric encoding and signature recovery; every survivor is classified with evidence
A wrong field index or signing-domain canary is detected and makes the verification run fail
The ledger records SDK/spec commits, live evidence, tool versions, mutations and survivor review; touched critical modules remain at least 95% covered and mix ci passes
task.body: Establish adequacy-tested evidence for Tempo's 0x76 transaction and signing semantics. Observe the current provider-owned SDK/spec and live Moderato behavior before fixing expected bytes, then challenge the local encoder and recovery paths with properties, independent vectors and mutation. Do not accept a fixture generated by the same local field layout as an independent oracle.
task.implemented: Landed by grok via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787754429899-05e4c762, 6dc15935efe3bca8ea9de7135d32787382a81ff1).

task.title: Verify optional 0x76 key_authorization across encode, sign, and recover
acceptance_criteria: key_authorization is encoded in its specification position for both the 0x76 sender payload and the 0x78 fee-payer preimage, and the fee-payer preimage path no longer discards the has_key_auth flag

Differential vectors from the current official Tempo SDK (exact version recorded) match on unsigned bytes, sign payload, serialized bytes, cosigned bytes and recovered sender/fee-payer identities, for transactions both with and without key_authorization
Property tests cover key_authorization presence and absence, boundary-sized and malformed values, and canonical RLP quantity encoding of the surrounding fields

A deliberate negative control - a wrong key_authorization insertion index, and a dropped key_authorization in the 0x78 preimage - is injected and makes the verification run fail; the run is invalid if the canary is not caught

A mutation campaign targets the key_authorization slot, its insertion index and the fee-payer preimage flag; every survivor is classified as equivalent, unreachable, redundant or a genuine gap, with the reachability assumption named
A live Moderato success and a relevant live error are recorded as evidence; absent endpoint access the run fails loudly with the exact setup needed, never a silent skip
priv/verification/0x76/ledger.json is extended with the SDK/spec version, artifact commit, tool versions, mutation totals and survivor review for this surface
Existing Task 12 vectors for transactions without key_authorization still match byte-for-byte, Onchain.Tempo.Transaction stays at or above 95% coverage, and mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Verification of transaction types other than 0x76 and its 0x78 fee-payer preimage
Changing the wire layout of transactions that carry no key_authorization
task.body:
Task 12 built a mutation-graded verification stack for 0x76, but it covers only the 13 named fields plus the sender signature. The optional key_authorization slot is unverified and partly unimplemented: Onchain.Tempo.Transaction.split_base_fields/1 computes has_key_auth (transaction.ex:391) and build_fee_payer_preimage_fields/4 then discards it as _has_key_auth (transaction.ex:396), while the verification oracle's spec_order/0 carries no key_authorization slot at all (test/support/tempo_verification/spec_encoder.ex:10-24). The module's own spec list does include it (transaction.ex:11). Verified by reading those lines on 4d648ce.

Close the gap on the authorization side of the signing domain: give key_authorization its spec position in both the 0x76 sender payload and the 0x78 fee-payer preimage, and hold that position against an oracle independent of our own field layout. The provider-owned authority is the current official Tempo SDK/specification plus live Moderato behavior; the local encoder is never its own oracle, and a fixture generated from our field indexes is not independent evidence. Observe the SDK and the chain before fixing any expected bytes.

Then challenge the result the way Task 12 challenged the base surface — properties over presence and absence, differential vectors, a deliberate canary, and a mutation campaign whose survivors are each classified with evidence.
